policy.coverage: All tracked plugin C++/headers, all docs Markdown plus root overview/notices/changelog/glossary, game Python test scenarios and focused native/hook/catalyst static tests. Excludes gameplay TSV/assets, unrelated tools, upstream agent instructions and unavailable toolkit implementation.
policy.extraction: Pattern-based source/reference extraction, not complete semantic decompilation. Source types, comments, table headers and unresolved symbols retained.
policy.corroboration: Shared toolkit or Suite ancestry and repeated upstream observations are not independent corroboration.

- Gameplay code is host-authoritative from day one, though multiplayer is tested only in its phase.
- Hooks live in one header per D2R build; on an unknown build a plugin logs and leaves the feature off.
- Each per-system plan lists companion hook points to avoid; a game check proves the port runs alongside every bundled companion.

- 2026-11-03: plugins renamed from `pd2-*` to `core-*` so the names stay valid if the port moves away from PD2 branding. Nothing had been built under the old names.
- 2026-11-03: a bundled companion may be Shared (Buff HUD is). Every release pins one version of each companion, so host and client match by construction; the "client UI never forces a match" rule binds only our own plugins.
- 2026-11-04: `core-events` (Shared) holds the map system's own code (opening maps, map stats, cube op 30, map events, invaders), so it can be built and turned off on its own, and used outside this project; it never calls `core-rules`. Rules the map system shares with other content stay in `core-rules` ([map-system.md](../features/map-system.md), [#152](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/152)).
- 2026-11-04: `core-events` also holds the uber bosses' own code (the Blood Fountain opening, area rules, tier scaling, phase scripts, drops and Desecration), since the uber bosses share the maps' opening and one-area-per-game gate; their skill functions stay in `core-rules` ([uber-bosses.md](../features/uber-bosses.md), [#153](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/153)).
- 2026-11-04: a system gets its own plugin only when all three hold: a player or another mod would turn it on or off as a whole; it shares no hook point or function slot with another plugin; and it never calls `core-rules`. The item rules fail the second (crushing blow's event slot 16 is shared with Smite, crit and deadly strike sit in the class skills' damage path, item procs go through `SrvSkillDispatch`), so they stay in `core-rules` ([item-rules.md](../features/item-rules.md), [#158](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/158)). Size alone is no reason to split: a large plugin is split into source files, and its off switch already leaves single parts out.
- 2026-11-04: item procs no longer go through `SrvSkillDispatch`: skill on cast moved to the Cast Triggers companion and core-rules' hook there is removed (IR2, #237). The item rules still share event slot 16 and the damage path, so they stay in `core-rules`.
- 2026-11-18: our plugins (core-rules, core-events, core-ui, Cartographer) install mod-scoped, in `<game>/mods/<mod>/d2rloader/plugins` beside the companions, no longer game-wide (#1180). The loader runs a mod folder's plugins in file-name order, so core-rules' table listener runs before Cast Triggers' with no `load_order` (the launcher keeps an edited d2rloader.toml as is, so a written order would miss existing installs); core-rules hooks `0x442c60` once tables load, after Progressive Affixes' load-time check; install.ps1 moves old game-wide copies out, and the launcher's Update removes them from the other plugin scope.

# Cartographer owns native maps; core-events preserves PD2 encounters

The 2026-11-15 scope removes PD2 map items, PD2 map affixes/stat routing, map tiers and map cube recipes, with the explicit exception of the Catalyst recipe adapted to native map items. Use a small Cartographer-native catalogue with one map per game-verified tileset and no tiers. This supersedes the earlier proposal to preserve PD2 map identity, affixes and crafting.

Retain the rewritten PD2 map-event fights and all uber encounters together in Shared core-events, with one shared AI registry and fixed-area lifecycle. Preserve the Altar/Guardian and its 2–3 Catalyst Shards; the retained recipe guarantees an event and excludes the Altar when forcing. Preserve Horazon's fight, then open an eligible native map at the source monster level and drop six native map items. Retain vanilla arenas for Lilith, Uber Izual and Uber Duriel. Use D2R's Uber Tristram arena with PD2 bosses and encounter/reward rules. Build new D2R-native static levels for Dclone, Rathma/Mendeln stages, Lucion arena and Temple. Build Bitter Depths and any justified Horazon bridge independently too.

Cartographer stays standalone, PD2-neutral and usable without a consumer. Add only the narrow optional SDK-mediated integration required by retained encounters, with one native-hook owner. General cube/item/stack/skill rules, corruption, Demonic Cube, retained refusals, Almanac and generic roll helpers remain in core-rules; uber keys/tiers and Desecration remain functional. The mod's whole data folder is committed as `files/data/`: PD2's tables, JSON, sprites and strings as the mod ships
them, with what the old `patches/` did folded in once (#1100). A data change is a direct edit of the table or JSON
file there, reviewed as a plain diff; there are no JSON patches. `modkit build` copies `files/data/` to `out/data/`
unchanged and `modkit install` installs that, so installing, testing and releasing need no PD2 install, extract or
merge. `tools/pd2_extract.py` and `tools/pd2_merge.py`, with the rules in `merge/`, are only the import run when PD2
itself releases a new version: its raw output is kept on the `pd2-import` branch and its change is applied to
`files/data/` as a three-way merge, reviewed as a diff. `pd2-import.txt` lists the files the import owns. The
table-diff gate compares the committed tables with PD2's baseline tables, which the self-hosted runner extracts
from the PD2 install. Blizzard's own D2R install and CASC files, saves and dumps are never committed; a unit test
refuses them and any path outside the allowed ones. Supersedes ADR 0002.

1. **Lock a slot.** With `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected`, `MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml`: `game_slots.py status`, then `MODKIT_RUN=<owner> game_slots.py lock <N> <owner>` on a free slot of this repo's registry entry (Slot2-5 here; game-slots.md, "Steps" 1-2).
   No free slot: stop and file a `ready-for-agent` issue with the steps left.
2. **Install the build** (game-slots.md, "Steps" 3-4). `plugin\build.ps1` builds against the toolkit's PluginSDK, found with the toolkit.
3. **No DS1 pinning** (retired with the converter, #965): levels are D2R's own or Cartographer's.
4. **Start the game** in HD on a character that meets the AGENTS.md test rules:
   `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> python <toolkit>/testing/game_ctl.py --slot <N> start`.
5. **Set the cheats** `cheat nogethit 1`, `cheat speedup 300`, `cheat god 1`, each through
   `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> game_ctl.py --slot <N> console "<cmd>"`. God mode also kills any unit the character damages in one hit, so never judge a boss's life, stages or immunity from the character's hits; lower its life with the plugin's test commands instead.
   Before any spawn whose item must survive a Save and Exit, also run `cheat savecheatitems 1`: cheat-spawned items are
   dropped from the save otherwise (any item, not only maps). The flag applies at spawn time: items spawned before it
   are still dropped.
6. **Warp** to each spot with `cheat goto <level>,<x>,<y>` (formula: `cheat-commands.md`).
7. **Shoot** only what settles the question (`MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> game_ctl.py --slot <N> shot`); log lines are the preferred proof. Take an HD,
   then `key g` legacy pair only when the change is visual in legacy. Look at each screenshot for a held cursor item
   before the next click.
8. **Never upload.** Shots stay in the slot's run folder. Never commit or push one, to any branch: `issue-assets`
   keeps old links only, nothing is added to it.
9. **Close out** right after the check: `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> game_ctl.py --slot <N> stop`, then, with the same three set, `game_slots.py unlock <N> <owner>`.
10. **Report** what you saw per spot in words and log lines.

A **game slot** is a separate copy of the D2R install for one test run, with its own plugins, mod data and saves.
"Set up a slot" means: lock one, install a build into it, and hand it over. d2rAI-toolkit's `testing/` folder holds the
tools (`game_slots.py`, `game_ctl.py`, `game_checks.py`; its [`testing/README.md`](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/732a7146e71402a48d8fd379887b75977a971ad1/testing/README.md), which also describes the fixture pattern our
`tests/game/fixtures/*` follow: one tiny mod per check).

One build of the mod runs on D2R 3.4 (build 95032) and 3.3 (93847): D2RLoader 1.3.1 runs its own engine image
(`0x6ab3782c`, 93847's code) with the installed game's data, so every plugin signature and address is the same on both
(#1509). The tables and strings the mod ships replace the game's; of the files 3.4 changed, only `propertygroups.txt`
(one new row) and the `ui-controller` and `vo` strings reach the game from 3.4.

- Slot 1, the config's `install_dir`, is the owner's 3.4 game, `C:\Games\Diablo II Resurrected`: read only, never
  written, launched or locked. Slots 2-5 are made from it and run 3.4.
- After a D2R patch, sync each slot, one at a time, with the lock held: `game_slots.py lock <N> <owner>`,
  `game_slots.py setup <N>`, `unlock`. Under `Data` the sync mirrors slot 1 and removes the CASC files the patch dropped
  (a stale `.idx` fails with "needs repair"). It hard-links on the same drive and copies (about 30 GB) to a slot on F:.
- A 3.3 slot: `C:\Games\Diablo II Resurrected Infernal Edition` is a 3.3 copy (also read only). Copy the config, set
  its `install_dir` to that folder, and run `setup <N>` with `MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG` pointing at the copy; run `setup`
  with the normal config to bring the slot back to 3.4.
- Which version a slot runs: `Version` in `<slot>\.build.info`, or the loader log's `[BUILD] D2R version` line. Our
  plugins log it too, with the image check: `core-rules: 0.2.0 loaded (mod PD2Resurrected, D2R 3.4.0, image 0x6ab3782c
  (expects 0x6ab3782c, match), ...)`. The loader's `mod build 93847` comes from the mod's dataversion, not the game: it is no mismatch on 3.4.

1. `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml python <toolkit>/testing/game_slots.py status` and pick a free slot your registry entry allows (here 2-5).
2. `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> python <toolkit>/testing/game_slots.py lock <N> <owner>`. For a slot the owner tests by hand, use an owner name
   such as `owner-<work item>`: a manual lock lasts until `unlock`.
3. Build and install: `plugin\build.ps1`, then, with `MODKIT_RUN` set to the lock's owner,
   `tools\install.ps1 -Game C:\D2RTestSlots\Slot<N> -Data . -NoValidate` (it copies the committed `files/data`; no extract
   or merge; main still has known validation errors). modkit install refuses a slot, so `install.ps1` installs a slot's data through
   the toolkit's `testing/slot_install.py`, which keeps the slot's own savepath and needs the lock held by `MODKIT_RUN`. `install.ps1` checks the lock first (`game_slots.py check <N> $MODKIT_RUN`) and writes nothing, failing, when `MODKIT_RUN` is unset or does not hold it (#1241).
   `install.ps1` installs our plugins (`core-rules.dll`, `core-events.dll`, `core-ui.dll`, `cartographer.dll`) mod-scoped, in
   `<slot>\mods\PD2Resurrected\d2rloader\plugins`, beside the companions (#1180). It leaves only the test harness
   (`test-harness.dll`, `d2r-testharness-console.txt`) in the game-wide `<slot>\d2rloader\plugins`: it moves anything else there,
   our old game-wide copies included, to `C:\D2RTestSlots\backups\stray-plugins-<date>\Slot<N>\` and lists it. Install always overwrites the slot's `cartographer.dll` with d2r-tools' `dist\cartographer` build, so testing a cartographer branch build needs `-Cartographer <path>`. It copies the latest `cartographer.dll` (`-Cartographer`, `CARTOGRAPHER_DLL`, else d2r-tools' `dist\cartographer`; it refuses one older than the d2r-tools commit pinned in `tools/cartographer.pin` (#1300), checking before touching the folder), and outside a test slot fetches and installs the companions. Pass `-KeepExtras` to keep third-party plugins in the game-wide folder (our old copies still go).
   Our plugin logs and `<plugin>-off.txt` files are now in the mod's `d2rloader\logs` and `d2rloader\config`. With `-Data` it also copies
   `companions/cartographer/signatures.txt` into the mod's `excel/d2rloader/cartographer/` (core-rules' cube hook needs it).
4. Check the installed data holds the change (the table row in `out/data`).
5. For a hand test, write the slot, its lock owner and the unlock command into the game-check issue.
6. `MODKIT_PROJECT=pd2-resurrected MODKIT_TESTING_CONFIG=C:/D2RTestSlots/modkit-testing-pd2.toml MODKIT_RUN=<owner> python <toolkit>/testing/game_slots.py unlock <N> <owner>` once the test is done.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

Each part and each status counters line is one object in a lane folder: `PartReg r<order>(<order>, "<word>", <install>)`
and `CountersReg c<order>(<order>, <counters>)` (`part_registry.h`). `plugin.cpp` sorts them by order and installs them, so the
order is the install sequence and the log line order. Orders are one global sequence in steps of 10; a new part takes an
unused number (the test fails on a duplicate). `plugin/CMakeLists.txt` globs `core-events/lane-*/*.cpp`, so a lane adds
files in its own folder and edits neither `plugin.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` nor this file; only a file outside the lane
folders (lane S, or a lane's older flat files) needs a row above and a CMake line.

Use Cartographer-native map items and native map-property behavior. Remove PD2 map items, the PD2 map affix/stat system, map tiers and PD2 map cube recipes, with one explicit exception: retain the Catalyst recipe adapted to the new native map items.

Start with a small native catalogue: one map per game-verified Cartographer tileset, using native defaults and no tiers. Unsupported or unverified tilesets wait. Names, codes and concrete table assignments are reviewed in implementation PRs; there is no requirement to preserve PD2 map identities.

Adapt only the removed-system dependencies of events. Preserve Horazon's summoner fight, then open another eligible native map at the source monster level and drop six native map items. Preserve the Altar/Guardian fight and its 2–3 Catalyst Shards; the retained Catalyst recipe guarantees an event on the resulting map and keeps the existing forced-selection exclusion of the Altar. Keep Lilith, Uber Izual and Uber Duriel in their vanilla arenas. Use D2R's Uber Tristram arena with PD2's Tristram bosses and encounter/reward rules. Build new D2R-native static levels for Dclone, Rathma/Mendeln stages, Lucion and the Temple. Do not carry forward the old converted arenas. Rebuild required fixed event areas such as Bitter Depths independently too, so the PD2 DT1/painter/generator-converter pipeline can be retired completely.

- **This revision supersedes the previous spec and 26-ticket draft.** Do not implement PD2 map-item/affix/tier/recipe parity. No child issues were published under that draft.
- **Ownership:** Cartographer owns native mapping and native map properties. core-events owns retained PD2 map events, event AI and all uber scripts, common PD2 AI registry, arena lifecycle and encounter rewards. core-rules owns general skill/item/cube/stack behavior and Almanac. core-ui retains unrelated UI duties. Do not create core-ubers or a PD2-specific Cartographer fork.
- **Native catalogue:** use one native map definition per game-verified tileset and native defaults; defer unverified tilesets. Supply actual mod-defined items, properties, catalogue data and normal acquisition rather than assuming the plugin ships a production catalogue. Review names/codes/tables in implementation. Use a single tierless acquisition pool; preserve unrelated loot and make its source/weights explicit. Horazon's six item rolls use that native pool.
- **Cuts:** remove PD2 map acquisition and map-specific items/consumables, affix eligibility/stat routing, fortify/population/drop modifiers, tier logic and map cube recipes except Catalyst. Unique maps and the special dungeon system remain cut. Prune removed branches from event/general treasure classes while keeping surviving loot; do not invent compensation rewards. Keep reserved saved-ID positions where applicable rather than renumber shared data.
- **Catalyst exception:** retain the existing recipe's ingredients, eligibility restrictions, event-forcing semantics and Altar exclusion, adapting its map input to native items. Retain only the isolated recipe/metadata needed for forcing, not the PD2 affix system or other map recipes. Treat the marker as event metadata: native property application must not apply it as a player/monster modifier. No direct-use shard consumable is being built.
- **Event preservation:** retain scripted fights, AI, waves, altars, cleanup and surviving rewards. Adapt active-map membership and progress from fixed PD2 level/room lists to generated-area identity. Keep existing quality-based event odds (normal 11%, magic 17% if applicable, other quality 34%) unless a recorded existing deviation applies. The native item supplies quality; the PD2 affix system is not needed.
- **Horazon:** keep the summoner encounter. Select another eligible Cartographer map, run that destination at the source monster level and give six native map items. Remove PD2-tier destination pools, old tier treasure classes, PD2 map-stat propagation and the unique-map roll. Preserve independent source/destination state and return travel; do not unintentionally reroll the event or reset progress.
- **Event areas:** preserve Bitter Depths for Void/Tomb, distinct from the removed Outer Void unique map. Newly built D2R-native fixed event areas are permitted where needed. Bitter Depths needs a converter-independent replacement with its retained encounter placement. Prove concurrent destination support, including same-tileset cases, or build a new validated native fixed-area bridge; old converted geometry is not a fallback. Ordinary Cartographer opening currently has global state; it is not proof that arbitrary second destinations are safe.
- **Ubers:** retain all existing fights, access/key recipes and uber tiers, which are not map tiers. Reuse the vanilla mini-uber arenas and D2R Uber Tristram arena with PD2 bosses; build new Dclone/Rathma/Lucion/Temple areas and preserve stage/state contracts, scaling, shared life, re-entry, stripping/pets, guaranteed and existing rare rewards, Temple chests and Desecration. Preserve fight mechanics while adapting placements; exact old geometry is not required.
- **New static content:** build the new Dclone, Rathma/Mendeln, Lucion and Temple static content, reusing/composing matching native assets where suitable. Do not build new mini-uber or Uber Tristram arenas: retain the vanilla mini-uber content and use D2R's Tristram arena with PD2 bosses. Preserve PD2 entry/tier/re-entry/reward rules, without duplicate stock boss spawns or stock rewards. Native engine DS1/DT1 resources may still be used; the retired dependency is this port's PD2 DT1/layout translation, painter and HD generator-converter. Do not bake old converted arenas into the permanent replacement.
- **Shared placements:** before parallel arena work, reserve level/preset IDs and disjoint asset namespaces, define arrivals, boss/add/soul/chest placements, phase regions, stage exits and return links, and make AI plus server/client skills consume the same placements. A serial owner changes the shared access/skill contract; fight authors edit private level/placement inputs and fight modules. Use a simple existing data seam where possible, not a general authoring framework.
- **Complete fight slices:** each fight slice delivers a playable encounter on its approved arena, including new static content only where required. Keep the vanilla mini-uber chain separate from D2R-arena/PD2-boss Tristram integration. Retain vanilla mini-uber IDs/portal/spawn behavior unless a proven integration change is necessary; arena reuse must not introduce new geometry or duplicate stock/PD2 spawns and rewards.
- **Acquisition:** prove normal acquisition for every retained uber ingredient after map removal. Preserve non-map key sources and Mendeln's retained rewards. Where an existing source is a map-boss concept, adapt it to an eligible native map boss with the retained base odds rather than carrying PD2 map-affix bonuses or old boss AI solely for acquisition. If no usable baseline source/rate exists, record that existing gap and obtain a concrete source decision; console-spawned test ingredients do not prove acquisition.
- **Generic cube rules:** remove map-only rows/branches, not the general matcher/executor. Retained non-map op-30 refusal rows exist, and the existing corruption follow-up search relies on blocking semantics. Preserve quantity/leftover behavior and Demonic Cube. Desecration is currently triggered from the old map plugin's search hook; keep that trigger and its corruption/Desecration roll helpers after deleting map-stat behavior.
- **Almanac:** retain its item-use implementation even though it is not a map cube recipe. Preserve the existing item-dispatch path rather than substituting an unproven local UI event.
- **Single hook owner:** resolve cube execution shared by Cartographer and core-rules, item use shared with uber/Almanac handling, monster setup needed by uber scaling, and room lifecycle/portal hooks needed by events. Prefer optional Cartographer cube stamping that does not install a second executor hook; prove the chosen seam. Never rely on load order.
- **Small generic contract:** use existing SDK services first and versioned optional extensions only for activation/refusal, area identity, room progress, monster lifecycle, item/event metadata, portals and teardown as required by retained scripts. Document thread/lifetime/registration rules. Missing required capabilities refuse unsafe activation without consumption. Native gaps are justified and executable writes use MutationService. Do not introduce a general engine API or retain a custom PD2 map-stat policy.
- **Shared helpers:** separate mixed map/uber/key/death logic before removal. Event Nihlathak/Mendeln code currently shares Dclone code; general corruption helpers and retained uber arena drops share map-stat code. Preserve those callers, one AI registry and common level effects. Delete ordinary PD2 map-boss behavior only when no retained script uses it.
- **Build:** build required native map/item and authored static-level data deterministically without the retired converter; do not mutate installed player tables after packaging. The stock installer restriction on adding IDs at 511 is not resolved merely by removing map stats, because unrelated retained PD2 stats already exceed that. Keep append-only ID reservations and verify the RotW table bank and text lookups agree.
- **Release:** obtain/pin a real Cartographer distributable and content hashes. Build core-events, retain core-rules/core-ui and retire core-maps after retained behavior has verified owners. Handle stale owned DLLs in both plugin scopes while preserving unrelated user files.
- **Concurrency:** at most four agents total. First separate mixed modules and freeze exact file ownership, shared interfaces, build/dispatch registration and private tests. Parallel lanes cover native maps, generic rules, map events and ubers. Each wave starts from one reviewed base; shared-file/API changes run through a serial owner/checkpoint, not a fifth concurrent agent. Unexpected boundary changes stop affected work rather than create overlapping edits.
- **Alpha saves:** keep the existing player savepath and compatibility as best effort, not a release gate. Add no conversion tool, mandatory fresh characters or retired-item layer. Do not deliberately rewrite/delete player saves. Warn about expected breakage and preserve snapshots for rollback.
- **Order:** freeze retained behavior/ownership; prove a minimal standalone-compatible contract and a native map with generic rules; prove a new native static area and freeze shared placements/IDs/asset ownership; adapt retained events/ubers with their new levels; implement the verified native catalogue and normal acquisition; remove obsolete PD2 maps after retained callers are separated; retire the geometry pipeline only after every retained area has a native replacement; stage, upgrade and rehearse rollback; retire the old backend and document cutover. The replacement work-item graph is reviewed before child publication.
- **Architecture:** revise the port's old core-maps ownership/no-calls decision, generated-PD2-level policy and upstream Cartographer's interface restriction while preserving independent use. Existing append-only saved-ID rules remain.
- **Rollback:** preserve the complete matched old release/config/hash/save snapshots; close game/loader; restore the full plugin/table/content/config set and check both scopes. Preserve newer candidate saves and deliberately restore a baseline snapshot if needed. Do not hot-swap hooks or promise downgrade compatibility.

Verify AI and server/client skills agree on placements.

| The Uber Tristram primes' minions: rolls, tie to the prime, corpses | approximated | PD2's AI wrappers (`0x10357ba0`, `0x10357d50`, `0x10357f00`) roll with `0x1036f320` and the CRT's rand(), tie each minion to its prime (`0x10339ad0`, not read) and remove dead monsters' corpses by the prime (`0x1036d1e0`). core-events rolls PD2's odds with the CRT's rand(), leaves the minion untied and keeps the corpses ([#483](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/483)) | [UB3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/228) |
| Rathma's stage spawns (`0x1036fef0`) | approximated | the bosses, the arena portal (none at the start of stage 1, owner, #1262) and the arena rooms' empty populate are ported. Left out: the area-type check (the level stands in, as levels 146-148 open from the Rathma key alone), the spawns' 1.13c flags `0x3000000`, the `empty` marker object and its waypoint removal, and the area rules for the in-level portal. A boss takes the nearest free spot to PD2's ([pd2-uber-bosses-dll](pd2/uber-bosses-dll.md), section 5) | [#525](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/525) |
| Rathma's tier-0 re-entry (`0x103a9780`) keeps the grey portals' exit in game counters | approximated | PD2 spawns an `empty` marker (587) at each new exit and relinks the three grey portals to it (`0x1038a510`). The port stores the exit's level and spot (`UBRL`, `UBRX`, `UBRY`); a grey portal warps the player to that level and places them at the spot, or at D2R's arrival in that level after a next-level portal, where PD2 searches a free spot by the act spawn location ([pd2-uber-bosses-dll](pd2/uber-bosses-dll.md), section 3) | [#479](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/479) |
| The Pandemonium keys' recipe takes D2R's portal output, without PD2's game event gate | approximated | PD2's cube walk (`0x10366f40`) opens the portal only while the game's event field (`game+0x1DF4`) is unset or 0x28, sets it to 0x28, and a map then refuses to open (but the Talisman). The port leaves the field out: the keys take D2R's own `Pandemonium Portal` output, which opens a level of 133-135 not opened yet in the game, as PD2's copy of it (`0x10366740`) does, but neither blocks nor is blocked by a map ([#485](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/485)) | [UB3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/228) |
| The organs' recipe outputs the Talisman itself, not `useitem` + output b | approximated | PD2's row gives output `useitem` and output b `ubtm`. In D2R `useitem` hands Diablo's Horn back, so the port makes `ubtm` the output and uses up all three organs, as PD2 players see ([#593](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/593)) | [UB3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/228) |
| Map event Horazon: what PD2 does besides | approximated | core-events drops six native maps on a `summonerMap` death while the game's event is Horazon's, once per game ([#506](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/506), [#959](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/959)); the tier pools, the unique map drop and the portal are gone (see the portal row). Left out (from PD2's handler): its slot-10 area entry (value: the new level; read only by a resist rewrite not decoded) and its refresh of the map stat panel for players in the new level (`0x1037f240`, see the panel row). The map drops roll at the monster's level, where PD2 passes `0x103a1b00`'s value (an import not identified) ([pd2-map-system-dll](pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 4) | [MS8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/222) |
| Uber Tristram's drop: item level, portal and repeat | approximated | PD2 (`0x10377710`) makes the Hellfire Torch and the Black Soulstone at item level 130; core-events drops them at the last prime's own item level (120 in Hell, the Torch's level). D2R's own drop of the same deaths (the Torch and a Standard of Heroes per player, `0x5a8450`) is turned off, as PD2 replaces it ([pd2-uber-bosses-dll](pd2/uber-bosses-dll.md), section 6). The town portal is PD2's red portal (`xactportal_red`), not object 60, whose D2R town-portal operate refuses it; and the drop is made once per game, where PD2 drops again on any later prime death | [UB3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/228) |
| Map boss swap: Uber Tristram's area test and prime bits, the Imperial maps' spawns | approximated | core-events' `map_open.cpp` ([#614](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/614), moved there from `map_bosses.cpp` in [#964](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/964)) ports PD2's preset swap for the uber levels (`0x1038b990`, and `0x1038bfc0`'s rewrites for levels 194-196): the `lesserhydra1`-`3` placeholder presets there spawn as their bosses. The native maps' bosses are the separate row below. Uber Tristram's placeholders roll the primes in level 181 whatever the game's area, where PD2 also needs it to be Uber Tristram's (`game+0x1df4` 0x29), which the port does not keep; the primes' bits (PD2's `game+0x2628`, which the opening sets to 0) are their own counter (`UBTB`), so a prime placed during the opening's warp keeps its bit. In the Imperial Palace boss room the preset spawns the bosses where PD2 spawns them itself (`0x1038a060`, `0x1037cd00`) and keeps them in `game+0x2600`-`0x260c`; in the Imperial Palace map the preset spawns Kamyr where PD2 spawns him on a free spot (`0x1038a0d0`) and keeps him in `game+0x2600` ([pd2-map-system-dll](pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 6) | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| Map bosses: five native maps' bosses spawn as Cartographer superuniques | approximated | PD2's map bosses spawn as Cartographer map Bosses, one per native map, as superuniques (PD2 swapped a `lesserhydra1` preset for a plain boss, `0x1038b990`). As superuniques they get the game's superunique bonuses, which PD2's plain preset spawn did not. Ruins of Viz'jun and River of Blood have PD2's `unravelerboss` and `baalminionboss` now that Cartographer has no 16-entry bosses.txt cap ([#1419](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1419)). `leoricMapBoss` runs D2R's ReanimatedHorde think: PD2's own AI (summon nova, bone armor, joust) was cut in [#964](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/964). Replaces the old map boss swap row: core-events' `map_bosses.cpp` was deleted in #964 | [#1115](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1115), [#1074](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1074) |
| Unique map boss deaths: portals and drops | approximated | core-events ([MS7b](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/499), [MS7c](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527)) opens the portals and makes the drops of Zhar, his mini-bosses, the Warlord of Blood (with his 2-3 random uniques and `demonpillar` kills), Iskatu, Rakanoth, Kamyr, the Imperial Palace boss and Ureh's boss (3 random uniques), and leaves the Warlord's arena rooms empty. The drops take the monster's item level, not PD2's 99/130, but for Zhar's charms (99, his mini-bosses' 90); a random unique is drawn from the uniques that pass PD2's test, where PD2 draws from all rows and stops after 20 (Warlord) or 40 (Ureh) misses; the portals stand at the body, not on a free spot; Kamyr's red portal leads to level 190's arrival spot, not to PD2's `empty` marker in the arena ([pd2-map-system-dll](pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 6) | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| The Outer Void: in-level portals, step drops, the bosses' list on room release | approximated | core-events ([#532](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/532)) ports PD2's Outer Void preset rewrite (`0x1038bfc0`: a random boss of three lists on each placeholder `lesserhydra`, 200/175/150% max life and state `mapevent`'s list; a red portal on each placeholder object) and its three death steps (`0x10379170`). PD2 links each in-level portal to an `empty` marker it spawns deeper in the level (`0x1038a510`); core-events has the portal's operate move the player to that spot (D2R's own same-act warp, `0x491ca0`). The steps' portals stand at the body, not on a free spot, and their uber parts drop at the monster's item level, not 130. PD2 saves state `mapevent` when a boss's room is released and remakes its list when the room comes back (`0x10371520`, `0x10371590`); core-events keeps a room holding a live `mapevent` boss instead, as for the uber bosses. PD2 picks the boss with `rand()`; so does core-events. The step counter is per game and never reset, where PD2's event setter (`0x10383060`) rewrites `game+0x2628` when a map opens: a second Outer Void map in one game finds the level already stepped ([pd2-map-system-dll](pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 6) | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| Zhar's seals: portals, tomes, progress | approximated | core-events ([#531](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/531)) ports PD2's Zhar preset rewrite (`0x1038bfc0`, levels 176-179: three open blue portals in the hub, a closed portal and a tome in each wing, the red one in one wing) and its seal operate (`0x103aa670`, PD2 operate 80 in D2R's free slot 64): a tome opens the portal in its rooms and steps `game+0x262a` (counter `MZHR`). The red wing is picked once per game by a per-thread generator, where PD2 takes the game seed mod 3; a wing's partner portal (at its spot 11) is made on the first trip from the hub, where PD2 makes it with the hub's; a portal's trip is D2R's level warp, then a move to the partner portal or PD2's `empty` marker spot, where PD2 links the two objects (`0x1038a510`). Zhar's four taunts (sounds 4704-4707) are logged, not played (D2R's sound table lacks them). The portals draw D2R's red portal and the tome D2R's tower tome ([pd2-map-system-dll](pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 6) | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| Unique map and dungeon readers left out | not yet | the dungeons' boss swap and boss blockers, value 9 ([#533](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/533)) | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| Unique map and dungeon kill counters | cut | Every unique map boss death adds 1 to two counters in the killer's player data (+0x39d, +0x419). PD2's `.kills` chat command reads them (`0x10361a70`, "maps" and "dungeons"; `0x1039db80` loads them with the character), and the port has no `.kills` command | [#527](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/527) |
| Map event Altar of the Catalyst: what PD2 does besides | approximated | core-events places the altar, calls its guardian `GuardianOfFate` on the first use and drops 2-3 Catalyst Shards on the use after its death, as PD2's operate 79 (`0x103aa460`) does ([#504](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/504)). The shards drop by the user at the user's item level, where PD2 drops them by the altar at item level 90. The guardian and its clones run PD2's AI (`0x1035a6b0`) and the clones die with it (`0x10378080`, [#609](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/609)); the altar's and the death's sounds play on each player, where PD2 plays them on the altar and the guardian (packet 0x2c's unit), and a clone already dead is not killed again | [MS8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/222) |
| Map event Spire of Darkness: the shadows' kill | approximated | core-events places the altar and three fog objects; the altar's use darkens the act and plays PD2's two sounds, the rooms then send shadow waves, and past progress 90 (`0x1036eb30`) the darkness lifts with PD2's sound and the shadows die, as PD2 does ([#505](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/505)). PD2's kill reads only the first monster of each of the game's 128 lists; core-events walks each list whole. The darkness goes off through a player in the level (PD2 passes the level's act) | [MS8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/222) |
| Map events on Cartographer's native maps (levels 138-144) | approximated | every `cmap` map rolls and runs the Shadow of Mendeln, Horazon, Dark Wanderer, Treasure Fallen, Spire of Darkness, Gheed, Altar of the Catalyst, Invaders and Void/Tomb scripts with PD2's odds, with progress counted against the built level's own room count (PD2R_MAP_ROOMS overrides it for tests); PD2's Rathma arena room skip comes from Cartographer's room-populate service ([#1032](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1032)); Void/Tomb leads to Cartographer's Bitter Depths arena, level 151 (#960) | [#950](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/950) |
| Invaders map event: spawn and drops | approximated | the portal spawns up to three times, at progress above 25, 45 and 65 (PD2's `25 + (n-1) x 20`); the invader's `0x30bdb0(invader, 0xd1, 1)` call (PD2's per-invader state) is not ported, it was not read; a kill by a missile, a pet or a console cheat drops for the game's first player; the drop table is PD2's, including the Barbarian's weapon split (one 2-hander, two throwing weapons or two 1-handers, one in three each) | [MS10](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/224) |
| Invaders are drawn with vanilla stand-in monster art (Code, monstats2 visuals and HD model of Dark Archer, Iron Wolf, Talic, Madawc, Summoner, Zakarum Zealot, Rogue hireling), legacy and HD; the Paladin's Bash uses mode A2 | approximated | PD2 draws them with player-class art, which D2R's data has no monster path for; real player art is [#1215](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1215) | [#1200](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1200), [#1199](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1199) |
| Arena fill: Mesa1 instead of PD2's Mesa3 | approximated | Cartographer's arenas (Diablo Clone 145, Rathma 146-148, Lucion 149, the Temple 150, Bitter Depths 151) are built from Mesa1 pieces, which place no monsters: the Mesa3 ("Chaos") pieces place Act IV monsters that would crowd the arena. The look differs from PD2's arenas where the Mesa3 pieces show | [#960](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/960) |
| Map event Void/Tomb: the portal | approximated | PD2 places a gold portal (`xactportal_gold`) by the spot and another in the Bitter Depths (level 207) and links them (`0x1038a510`). core-events opens D2R's red portal pair (object 60, `rva::PortalMaker`) to the level instead: the same linked pair, red ([#507](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/507)) | [MS9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/223) |
| Map stats: aligned monsters | approximated | PD2 gives a monster with a monstats `Align` (a minion or ally) an empty list under the `map` state; core-events gives it neither ([ms3-map-stats](research/maps/ms3-map-stats.md)) | core-events |
| PD2's blank `<reserved>` objects rows 573-583: D2R's rows stand there | approximated | they hold the ids of 1.13c's engine objects (random shrines and chests, the Arcane Sanctuary's portal), which D2R made rows of its own at the same ids; a PD2 DS1 that places one gets D2R's row ([#211](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211)) | [LP1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211) |
| levels `Teleport` 3 (Monastery Map, Realm of Terror, Sanctuary Of Sin Map, Imperial Boss Map) reads as 1 | cut | PD2's 3 refuses a teleport past the level's `blocker_teleport_*` objects; those levels are cut ([#1230](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1230)) and the blocker check was removed with them | [#1232](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1232) |
| levels `DrawEdges` is 0 in every PD2-only area of Act 5 (all 19 that set it, incl. Zhar Library, Lucion Vault, Halls of Torture Map), so no floor is drawn past a map's edge | approximated | D2R's client builds an act's edge tile for Acts 1-3 only (`0x327090`); in Act 5 it is empty, and drawing it crashes in `FUN_14021d090` (reads `0x14` through null) once the player stands near where the drawn floor ends ([#258](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/258)). PD2's own Act 5 edge drawing (1.13c) is not checked | [LP1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211) |
| monpreset act 5: PD2's rows from 51 on sit after D2R's own, from 57 on | approximated | D2R's act 5 rows 51-56 are its own ([#146](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/146)); PD2's DS1 are rewritten to the new indices, so only the numbers differ ([#211](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211)) | [LP1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211) |
| monpreset's `SpiderBoss` is spelled as monstats names it, `spiderboss` | approximated | D2R's lookup is checked case for case; same monster ([#211](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211)) | [LP1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/211) |
| PD2 cells that name a row no table defines, or hold a note in a number column, are blank; two property codes are lowercased | approximated | D2R's validator rejects them; 1.13c finds no row (or reads 0) for each, so the game behaves as before, and `Thorns` and `Light` match `thorns` and `light` in any case ([modkit-validation](process/modkit-validation.md), [#171](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/171)) | [#171](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/171) |
| Skill tree backgrounds are redrawn from the tables in D2R's box and arrow art, not PD2's: arrows run straight, a diagonal that skips rows branches off the straight arrow below its skill (as PD2's do), and arrows keep clear of the counter boxes; an arrow may pass under a box between | approximated | PD2's tree art is classic size and is not upscaled; the routes are generated, so their look is checked in game | [#84](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/84) |
| PD2-only missiles draw D2R stand-in models | approximated | each of PD2's new missiles maps to a D2R missile's HD model (`merge/missiles-hd.tsv`, `tools/pd2_missiles_hd.py`); PD2's missile art is classic DCC sprites and an HD missile is a 3D model, so no script converts them, and the stand-ins are final ([#198](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/198)) | P10 |
| PD2-only monsters draw D2R stand-in models | approximated | each of PD2's new monsters maps to a D2R monster's HD model (`merge/monsters-hd.tsv`, `tools/pd2_monsters_hd.py`): its `BaseId`'s or its `Code`'s, and a hand-picked one for the 22 with PD2-only art (Zhar, Iskatu, Lucion, Na-Krul, the Invaders, ...) and for 7 whose `Code` D2R draws with several models (the Countess, the Dopplezon, ...); without an entry the HD renderer draws nothing for them ([#198](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/198)) | [UR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/200) |
| PD2-only overlays draw D2R stand-ins | approximated | each of PD2's 33 new overlays copies a D2R overlay's HD json, picked by look (`merge/vfx-overlays.tsv`, `tools/pd2_overlays_hd.py`); shared overlay rows keep D2R's `Character` (the HD folder), as PD2's classic values (all, ?, Assasin, Bar) left shrines, Battle Orders, curses and auras invisible ([#198](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/198)) | [UR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/200) |
| PD2's buff timers, mini skill icons and skill bar | approximated | covered by the Buff HUD companion (Pyre-Flies, `companions/manifest.json`); PD2's `bufficons` and `skillicons_mini` art is not ported ([#198](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/198)) |  |
| PD2's tooltip stat ranges | approximated | covered by the Item Roll Ranges companion (Pyre-Flies, `companions/manifest.json`); its ranges are not compared with PD2's ([#198](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/198)) |  |
| PD2's DPS counter | approximated | covered by the DPS Counter companion (`synpoox/d2r-tools` 1.0.0, `companions/manifest.json`): the damage per second your hits deal, above the life globe; it counts only in games you host, not damage over time, and is not compared with PD2's own counter | [UR9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/207) |
| PD2's potion counter | approximated | covered by the Potion Counter companion (`synpoox/d2r-tools` 1.0.1, `companions/manifest.json`): a framed picture of the potion in each belt column above the belt slot, not compared with PD2's own counter | [UR10](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/208) |
| Uber ingredient drops: dcso and dcbl come from treasure-class data | approximated | PD2's DLL rolls them (`dcso`: about 1 in 21 per Hell Diablo kill, 1 in 13 per Baal kill; section 6 of `docs/pd2/pandemonium-uber-tristram.md`). The port adds `dcso` to the Hell rows of Mephisto, Diablo and Baal and their `q` rows (7, 7 and 11 against a row sum of about 1000, seven picks: 1 in 21, 21 and 13.5 per kill) and to the Hell Desecrated item rows (weight 1, 1 and 2 against a row sum of 177 or 178 with NoDrop: about 1 in 26, 26 and 13; the weights are whole numbers, so Mephisto and Diablo cannot reach 1 in 21). Each Cartographer map boss's Hell TC gets a wrapper (`Map Boss T<n> Blood`, `dcbl`, 1 in 9 with one player; no PD2 rate is known, the owner confirmed 1 in 9). `rtmf` has no source by owner decision. | [#985](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/985) |
| Dark Pact's damage synergy sum sits in calc2 | approximated | D2R reads a formula only to 255 characters. PD2's `EDmgSymPerCalc` is 270 long here (D2R's skill names are longer than PD2's), and an over-length formula evaluates to 0; the nine x12 terms move to the unused `calc2` (`clc2`), the sum is unchanged | [#1257](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1257) |
| Megademon Armageddon boss synergy names Eruption, not Fissure | approximated | PD2's `MegademonArmaBoss` `DmgSymPerCalc` and `EDmgSymPerCalc` name `skill('Fissure'...)`, which no table defines. Eruption is PD2's and D2R's name for skill 234, which 1.13c called Fissure; the megademon boss has none of the named skills, so the sum stays 0 either way | [#1434](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1434) |
| Treasure classes Fallen Rune NM and Invader 2h Sword move above their first user | approximated | D2R resolves a treasure class's entries in table order and asserts on one defined further down (`MapStat DropCrafting` Item2, `InvaderBarbarian1h` Item4); both rows move up one block, unchanged, so the drops stay as PD2 has them | [#1434](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1434) |
| Cyclone Armor (monster) aura stat formulas: one stray closing bracket removed | approximated | PD2's `aurastatcalc1` and `aurastatcalc2` end `...*256)` with a bracket no opening matches; D2R's formula check asserts at load. The value is the same | [#1257](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1257) |
| Slow Movement tooltip: the empty operand in max(edln,,25) is dropped | approximated | PD2's tooltip formula has two commas in a row, which D2R's formula check asserts on at load; `max(edln,25)` is assumed to be what the empty operand evaluates to | [#1257](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1257) |
| Hell Act 1 weapon and armor treasure classes: the entry naming a missing Normal class is cleared | approximated | `Act 1 (H) Weap A` and `Armo A` name `Act 5 (N) Weap C` and `Act 5 (N) Armo C`, which no table defines (PD2 and D2R alike). The engine asserts at load and skips the unresolved entry without counting its weight, so clearing Item9/Prob9 keeps today's drops | [#1257](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1257) |

| Holy Sword parry | approximated | PD2's roll (class 5 = 2hs, chance from the block function with Holy Sword's `passive_weaponblock`, cap 75, a third against Lucion) runs before D2R's avoid; the 4-frame no-avoid window after any player avoid is kept (per player id, in the plugin, not in playerdata); the claw block (class 13) is rolled by PD2's roll (cap 75, a third against Lucion) only while walking or running, the modes D2R skips (player 2/3, monster 2/0xf); in other modes D2R's own claw block runs; the known difference there is Lucion's third (D2R's block chance function `0x450070` has its body behind a jump into the protected section, not in the dump, so whether it caps at 75 is unknown); not ported: the PvP-level halving and sound 4713 | [#1466](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1466), [#1482](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1482), [#1483](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1483) |

Rathma's two clones split it like PD2 ([#645](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/645)): the half holds after the first clone dies, as in PD2; the port puts no list on the dead clone, and stops halving once its unit is gone from the game's monster lists. records.excerpt:
Resolves research ticket [#19](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/19) (framework from [#14](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/14)). The hook list it fills is [docs/features/core-rules.md](core-rules.md). Findings only: no
PD2 or Blizzard file content is in this repo; skill, missile, stat and recipe names below are short identifiers.

- **98 hook-list rows** (92 in the first pass, 6 added by the second review in section 5). 78 need plugin code (bucket c: 38 S,
  36 M, 4 L), 2 are a service (b), 12 are data only (a) and are listed so their check is not lost, 5 are unreachable and 1 is cut.
  About a third are `verify`: their bucket or slot depends on a check that has not been done.
- **Two corrections to the data inventory ([#2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/2)) change the plan:**
  1. PD2's server do functions **153-170** are PD2's own (vanilla stops at 152), and D2R 3.x uses 153-171 for its own RotW
     skills. So 17 PD2 functions collide, not 3. With PD2's 15 own numbers in 173-189 that is 32 functions for 19 free slots
     (172-190). **The srvdofunc table must be extended** (a dispatcher detour for values 191+), or the plan does not fit. The same
     collision hits `cltdofunc` 97-105 and 109 (9 values, which do fit in 110-129) and `srvstfunc` 64, 66, 69, 70.
  2. Misc `pSpell` 12 and 13 are inside D2R's range but mean something else in D2R: 12 is D2R's Resist Scroll, used by **PD2's 48
     map items**, and 13 is D2R's respec token, used by PD2's unlimited TP/ID books. Both are engine rules (re-map to 16, 17).
- **Unreachable:** item events `docrit`, `dopierce` and `corpsefinish` (so only 2 of the 4 event stats are live: skill on cast with
  62 item rows, skill on block with 5), `descfunc` 30, the boss skill Power Strike Tomb Boss and 5 missile rows (listed below).
  Every function-number value from [#2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/2)'s section 4 has at least one reachable row.
- **Values inside D2R's range checked against D2R's own data guide:** cube ops 16 and 18 (item stat less than / equal to) and every
  `descfunc` PD2 uses except 30 have the vanilla meaning in D2R, so they are data. The skill and missile values inside D2R's range
  (srvdo 41/143/163, cltdo 15/22/83, hit 5/6/30, client hit 4/11/12/26, missile do 40/72/12) could not be checked: D2R's function
  tables are filled at run time, so they stay `verify`.
- **Server rules from [#3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/3):** confirmed by strings (`.noexp`, `.set-home`, stat commands, corrupted zones, teleport-blocked areas,
  loot allocation, PvP and battle-royale checks, map events and invaders). Phasing, the charm rule, the Act 3 quest 5 patch and the
  skill palette / player mode / NPC patches exist but their effect is not identified, so they are `verify`. Pass 1 also found three
  item rules the earlier tickets missed: skill while equipped, the map item spell and the corruption roll.

|---|---|
| `pd2-data/s14-alliance/data/global/excel/*.txt` (a sibling folder of the repos, outside the toolkit) | PD2 tables. [#2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/2) showed they are byte-identical to `pd2data.mpq` in the install, so they stand for the PD2 baseline |

**Why so many collisions.** D2R's base bank stops at srvdofunc 152 and cltdofunc 97; D2R 3.x added 153-171 and 96-109 for RotW.
PD2 also numbered its additions from 153. Same-name comparison shows PD2 moved vanilla skills onto its own numbers: Leap 77 -> 153,
Double Throw 74 -> 154, Teleport 27 -> 155, Bash 2 -> 158, Static Field 20 -> 160, Poison Dagger 32 -> 164, Hunger 122 -> 165,
Firestorm 117 -> 166, Find Item 72 -> 168, the Assassin finishers 34/35 -> 170. In D2R as is, Leap would run Sigil Death
Explosion's server code and 19 Paladin auras would run Cleave's client code. D2R's same-name number is each rule's fallback if it is
not built (an approximated deviation, not silent breakage).

**Slots.** Free in D2R and kept: srvdofunc 173-182, 184-186, 188, 189; cltdofunc 110-114, 117-119; srvstfunc 71-79 (if the table is
94 entries, Q3); pSrvHitFunc 61-65; pCltHitFunc 66, 67 and 6 (empty in D2R); cube ops 30, 31 (D2R ignores unknown ops). Proposed
re-maps: srvdofunc 153 -> 172, 154 -> 183, 155 -> 187, 156 -> 190, then 157-170 (without 163) -> 191-203 through the overflow
table; cltdofunc 97 -> 115, 98 -> 116, 100-105 -> 120-125, 109 -> 126; srvstfunc 66 -> 80, 69 -> 81, 70 -> 82, 64 -> 67 (data,
per the toolkit notes); pSpell 12 -> 16, 13 -> 17; srvdofunc 109 -> 9 (data). Each re-map is a `merge/` rule logged on its row.

**Likely same, still verify.** Server hit 6: the toolkit notes it spawns the monstats row in `sHitPar1`, and all five PD2 users are
summon-on-hit missiles; the `sHitPar1` ids must be remapped (monstats ids collide). cltdofunc 15: D2R has a function there ("random
spray around the target"), PD2 uses it for one boss nova.

**Unknown, verify.** srvdofunc 41/143/163, cltdofunc 22/83, server hit 5/30, client hit 4/11/12/26, missile do 40/72/12, damage
18/19, aura event 32/3, state remove 12: D2R's data never uses these numbers, and D2R's tables live in `.data` past the file's
initialised part (srvdofunc at 0x238ea00 is beyond `.data`'s 0x3afa00 raw bytes), so the file can't show whether a slot is empty.
A one-time plugin log of each table's non-null slots answers it in one session (Q2).

**Order hint for the work items (not decided here).** Plumbing first (installer, RVA header, cltdofunc client example, **srvdofunc

- **Q1. srvdofunc overflow.** 32 PD2 server do functions, 19 free slots. The dispatcher (`SrvDoDispatch`) rejects values over 190;
  the field is 16 bits. Proposal: detour the dispatcher and serve 191+ from a plugin table. Not tested; it is plumbing for work
  item 1. Alternative: build fewer rules and take D2R's fallback for the rest.
- **Q2. What D2R holds in slots its data never uses** (srvdofunc 41/143/163, cltdofunc 15/22/83, hit and missile do values above).
  Also whether `srvprgfunc`/`cltprgfunc` index the do-function tables: PD2 uses srvdofunc 143 and cltdofunc 83 for its Royal Fire
  bosses, which are D2R's vanilla prg numbers for Fists of Fire and Blades of Ice. If prg values index the same tables, PD2's prg 171
  collides with D2R's srvdofunc 171 (Korlic's Leap Attack).
- **Q3. Start-table sizes.** `srvstfunc` table at 0x238e710 sits 0x2f0 bytes before the srvdofunc table, which suggests 94 entries
  (inferred, not verified). The client start table is not located; PD2 needs 54-58 and D2R data stops at 61.
- **Q4. Did PD2 change vanilla function bodies?** Rows marked `data` assume a vanilla number does in D2R what it did in PD2. Strings
  can't tell; a balance difference would show only in the PD2 baseline test.
- **Q5. Rows picked by code.** splitthrowglaive/pilum (weapon-type choice, as in the spike) and blizzard2/3 have no data path. Check
  ProjectDiablo.dll / D2R's Blizzard code before calling them unreachable.
- **Q6. Effects not identified:** phasing, the charm single-unique rule, a3q5, SkilPal, PlrModes, SUNITNPC, PerfectShrine. Each
  needs a PD2 baseline observation or a ProjectDiablo.dll read.
- **Q7. Map system.** Map items (`pSpell` 12), the `map_mon_*` / `map_play_*` / `map_glob_*` stats, map recipes (op 30), map events
  and invaders are one large engine system. It needs its own plan; the rows here are its hook points only.
- **Q8. Cube op 30 meaning.** Guessed from the rows: it gates map recipes and the "BLOCK ... duplicates due to stackable maps" rows,
  so it probably checks a single, unstacked input. Op 31 rows have no output; the op probably rerolls the input in place. Both need
  the PD2 baseline.
- **Q9. Corrupted zones vs D2R's desecrated zones.** D2R's `pSpell` 15 and desecrated-zone config may carry most of it as data.
- **Q10. Corruption flow.** Answered by [P9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/56) from the rows and D2R's recipe search (`0x529090` takes the first matching
  row; the executor `0x5269c0` runs it once): each item group has a roll row (op 18, `corruptor` = 0: `corruptnum`
  1-1000, the shard handed back as `output b`) ahead of its outcome rows (op 16, thresholds rising to 1000, `corruptnum`
  1001). So D2R gives PD2's outcomes and odds in two presses. PD2's `ladder` column tags the rows (2 roll, 1 outcome,
  3 destroyed, 4 map), which points at its cube code re-running the search after a roll row and marking the new item
  a "destroyed" outcome makes (those rows carry no mods). [P9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/56) marks those items in the merge; one press is a later hook.

# core-rules hook list

- **PD2 source**: table column and value (`srvdo` = skills `srvdofunc`, `cltdo` = `cltdofunc`, `srvst`/`cltst` = start functions,
  `prg` = `srvprgfunc1-3`/`cltprgfunc1-3` (`srvprg`/`cltprg` for one side), `shit`/`chit` = missiles `pSrvHitFunc`/`pCltHitFunc`, `sdo`/`cdo` = missiles
  `pSrvDoFunc`/`pCltDoFunc`, `dmg` = `pSrvDmgFunc`), or the DLL source for server rules.
- **Bucket**: (a) data only, (b) D2RLoader service, (c) native hook, (d) UI rebuild, (e) cut.
- **D2R slot**: PD2's number where that slot is free in D2R. `->` marks a re-map (collision or past the table end), logged here.
  Slots 191+ need the srvdofunc overflow table (plumbing, see the research file, Q1).
- **RVAs**: names only; the values live in the per-build header. `?` = not located yet.
- **Tier**: Exact or Function-equivalent (glossary).
- **Size**: sessions. S under 1, M 1-2, L 3+. Every size here is an estimate from the spike, not measured.
- **Status**: `spiked` (proven in a spike), `open` (to build), `verify` (a value inside D2R's range, or a rule whose effect is not
  yet confirmed: treat as different from D2R until checked), `data` (no plugin code expected; listed so the check is not lost),
  `unreachable` (no row reaches it in play; not added to the deviation list), `cut`.
- **Work item**: the build slice that carries the row (see Work items below); empty = after the alpha 0.1.0 cut (in the alpha), in the order
  below. map system rows name their `MS` work item from [map-system.md](map-system.md), whose map-only code lives in `core-events`; uber boss rows name their `UB` work item from [uber-bosses.md](uber-bosses.md); item rule rows name their `IR` work item from [item-rules.md](item-rules.md); `later release` rows wait for multiplayer.
- **Test**: the log assertion the `tests/game/` check makes. Expected values come from PD2's data unless noted.

1. Router slot: built in [W10](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/51) as srvdofunc 190 (dispatching by skill id; Bash first). Further rules join it.
2. The 4 dead item events and the remaining shared hit-function groups.
3. Class-themed item rules (Ormus' Robes): built in [P12](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/108), with skill on cast for every cast-skill item. The remaining item rules are bundled into [IR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189)-[IR8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/243) ([item-rules.md](item-rules.md), [#158](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/158)); skill on cast moved to the Cast Triggers companion in [IR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/237).
4. Monster and boss kits, then cube ops: the kits a fight uses join its UB item, the rest are [W36](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/244) ([#210](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/210)).
5. Investigations: phasing, a3q5, SkilPal/SUNITNPC, PerfectShrine, charm rule, cube op 30/31. a3q5, SkilPal/SUNITNPC,

records.excerpt:
Cartographer is **not modified** and stays PD2-neutral. The PD2 side (core-events, today core-events' lane C/D code) adapts to
what Cartographer already exposes plus D2RLoader's PluginSDK services. Inspected: d2r-tools 629f08b. Cartographer
publishes no service or event (`PluginCommunicationService`, `ItemInteractionService` and `LifecycleService` are unused
there), so there is nothing to consume yet; the consumer runs observe-only.

| Piece | Rule |
|---|---|
| Capabilities | `Activation`, `AreaIdentity`, `RoomProgress`, `MonsterSetup`, `Teardown` (bit flags). |
| Discovery | A provider publishes the service named `event-link.v1` (a breaking change takes a new name; the SDK limits names to 127 bytes) through `PluginCommunicationService`: a table `{uint32 size; uint32 version; uint32 caps;}`, new fields only at the end, read only up to `size`. The consumer acquires it at load, keeps the handle until unload, and treats a missing service as `NoProvider`. |
| Versions | A newer provider table must keep serving older callers; new fields go at the end. `Check` refuses a provider older than `ContractVersion`. |
| Refusal | `Activate(provider, need, consume)` runs `consume` (take the item, charge) only on `Ok`. `NoProvider`, `OldVersion` and `MissingCaps` touch nothing. |
| Area identity | `AreaId = {level id, session generation}` from the SDK's `LevelChanged` event (UI thread). A `MonsterDeathEvent` has a level id but no session, so the consumer caches the session from the last `LevelChanged` event and builds the `AreaId` from it, both under one mutex. Cartographer reuses a slot's level id within one game: without `AreaIdentity` the consumer calls `AreaTracker::Opened` on every fresh open, which resets that entry (tested). |
| Progress | `AreaTracker` keeps one entry per area. Entering, killing in or closing a second area never edits the source's entry (source/destination independence for Horazon and Bitter Depths). Monster deaths come from the SDK's `MonsterDeathListener` (server thread, observation-only). |
| Threads and lifetime | Lifecycle callbacks arrive on the UI thread, death callbacks on the server thread: the real plugin guards the tracker with a mutex. Event pointers are valid only inside the callback. A map that carries a layered marker makes Cartographer log one warning ("a stat with a layer cannot be a map property") on open: expected, not a bug. Listeners and service handles are released at unload. |
| Metadata | Event metadata (the Catalyst's forced-event marker) must sit on a stat **with a layer** (`MarkerLayer`). Cartographer turns every layer-0 item stat into a player buff and drops a layered stat (`itemStatsToProperties`), so the marker never becomes a buff and no Cartographer change is needed. A layer-0 marker would become a native player stat (the check proves it). |

- Which ItemStatCost row carries the marker. The ticket asks for an unused existing row, not a new one. The row needs a Save Param Bits setting so it can hold a layer. Ticket 4 publishes the reserved metadata definition (the row); ticket 10 owns the game proof that a layered stat survives the Catalyst recipe and a save.
- `RoomProgress` and `MonsterSetup` (spawn-time) hooks. The SDK offers death and level-change events only. Room activation and monster setup stay on core-events' native hooks until a provider publishes them.

- **Parity: Exact.** One core-rules row per rule, not per stat: crit chance and multiplier are one row, deadly strike
  multiplier and maximum one, Nightmare's Feast's two stats one, enhanced damage per ethereal item and per missing life
  one. Crushing blow efficiency joins the existing crushing blow formula row (both are PD2's event 16).
- **DLL-only is checked in the work item.** [#148](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/148) found the 14 stats DLL-only from the tables, not in Ghidra. Each work
  item starts by tracing its stats in `ProjectDiablo.dll`; a stat D2R already handles shrinks to data.
- **Companion plugins first.** RuffnecKk's suite (MIT) has a plugin for several rules. [IR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189) checks each against PD2's
  numbers and against our hooks:
  - Cast Triggers takes skill on block and skill on cast. [P12](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/108)'s listener walk is removed once it passes; Ormus' Robes
    (func 25 -> 26) stays in core-rules. If it clashes with core-rules' hooks (`0x43acb0`, event slot 16), it is forked
    into core-rules instead.
  - Ethereal Item Rules gives set items rolling ethereal, and Progressive Affixes the rare affix minimum. The Item Durability and Mass Identify companions were removed ([#1467](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1467)); core-rules builds PD2's ethereal durability ([#1478](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1478)); the Almanac stays [IR5](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/240)'s ([#189](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189)).
  - Mercenary drop on hire (yinyin333333, closed source) gives a mercenary's gear back when another is hired.
  A plugin that matches PD2 closes its row; one that only comes close makes its row approximated.
- **The dye stat** (`transform_dye`) tints the output of 35 PD2 cube rows (the Annihilus corruptions and the magic-item
  "added mod" rows). The recipes work in the port without the tint: an approximated row. How D2R Reimagined tints
  items is researched for a later patch ([#190](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/190)).
- **Wiki-only rules** get a core-rules row with status `verify`: the open wounds rework, set
  items rolling ethereal, loot from flying monsters landing on walkable tiles, and monsters killed by Chaos Sanctuary
  seals dropping nothing. Potions going to the belt and items that can't be sold are data checks. A rule the DLL does
  not have is dropped.
- **Work items are bundled by the code they share**, not one per rule.

| # | Work item | Plugin | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [IR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189) | Investigation ([#189](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189), done): RuffnecKk's suite plugins next to core-rules on 93847, each against PD2's rule | none | none |

Cast Triggers is 1.1.12 from the D2RLoader Hub (the suite's GitHub 1.1.1 refuses D2RCore 1.3.1); its procs await the owner's game check | companions, core-rules (removal) | [IR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189) |

| [IR4](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/239) | Curses: curse effectiveness, max curses | core-rules | none |
| [IR5](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/240) | Item use and charges: unlimited TP and ID books (`pSpell` 13 -> 17 and 18), throwing potions with PD2's weapon spell columns, item casts (`ItemEffect`), replenish charges | core-rules | none |
| [IR6](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/241) | Cube rules: the demonic cube reroll (op 31) and corruption in one press ([ir6-cube-rules](../research/items/ir6-cube-rules.md)). The stack split moved to [#316](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/316) (`HOTKEY_ItemQuantity` is a display toggle), stack-counting recipes to [#315](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/315) | core-rules | none |
| [IR7](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/242) | Equipped items: skill while equipped and phasing (the charm "only one unique" rule, [#358](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/358)) | core-rules | none |
| [IR8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/243) | Item generation and loot: the ethereal bonus (25%), weapon durability loss at half the rate, the wiki rules [IR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/237) does not close (rare affix split, staffmods, loot placement, seal kills), the belt and no-sell data checks | core-rules | [IR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/189) |
Rare Cartographer maps roll PD2's map affixes in PD2's tier bands. Tables only: the rows are in `magicprefix.txt` and `magicsuffix.txt` (maps are never magic, so the magic rows serve rare maps).

Cartographer's drop class and extra group stats take a Param (a treasure class, a monstats Id), but a property cannot carry one. Instead of one stat with a Param, each Param has its own mod stat and property (append-only ids pinned in `merge/ids-itemstatcost.tsv`), and `files/data/global/excel/d2rloader/cartographer/statroutes.txt` routes each stat to the behaviour and Param:

`item_splashonhit` needs a skill and level in its layer, which a map property cannot give. So `mon-splash` (property 469) sets the mod stat `cartographer_map_mon_splash` (itemstatcost 650, tooltip "Melee Attacks Deal Splash Damage") to the chance, and `statroutes.txt` routes it: `Monster`, `Apply` `item_splashonhit`, `Param` 27521 = (430 << 6) | 1, `proc_SplashDamage` at level 1. The second set has its own pair, `mon-splash2` (property 470) and `cartographer_map_mon_splash2` (itemstatcost 651), routed with `Param` 27522, level 2. Each monster of the map gets that stat and core-rules' splash (event 20, srvdo 190) fires on its melee hits. The route's `Param` needs a Cartographer with monster route layers ([d2r-tools#551](https://github.com/synpoox/d2r-tools/pull/551)).
`of the Adventurer` had no affix string: id 51541 in `item-nameaffixes.json`. `Large` uses D2R's own `Large` key (`ui.json`).

`tools/tests/test_map_affixes.py`: every affix row with a `cmap`/`t1m`..`t3m` type names only real properties and only those types, and the rolling set (spawnable 1, rare 1, frequency above 0) is 105 rows (103 by name and table) and holds the 27 of #1305, so a dead pool fails. The six Splashing rows point at `mon-splash` and its route, every `statroutes.txt` row names a real stat, treasure class or monstats Id, and `corrupted`/`corruptor` route to `None` so the map panel skips them (#1349).
Table edits only: `cubemain.txt` (65 rows appended under the existing Catalyst rows), `misc.txt` (`upmp`, `fort`), and the orb strings. Art for the two orbs was already in place (#1292).

## Anya (#1324)
Anya sells `upmp` and `fort` as PD2's Drehya does: `AnyaMin`/`AnyaMax` 1, no magic columns, price 200000 (`upmp`) and 15000 (`fort`). The vendor columns already equal PD2's `misc.txt`, so no table row changed.

[#942](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/942) (merged in [#1058](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/pull/1058)) cut PD2's map items, map stats, tiers and the generated PD2-only map areas: maps are native Cartographer maps (`m01`-`m25`), and `core-events` keeps the map events and uber fights ([ADR 0006](../adr/0006-cartographer-and-core-events.md), [cartographer-migration.md](../cartographer/migration.md)). The owner reversed part of that cut on 2026-11-17 ([#1303](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1303)): the Cartographer maps get PD2's map progression back, with table edits wherever tables can express it. The sections below `## Scope` describe the older PD2-parity plan; read them for what PD2 does, not for what the port builds.

- Every map has one tier, like PD2: T1 opens at area level 87, T2 at 88, T3 at 89 (`maps.txt` `Level`; Cartographer stamps it on each new map as `cartographer_map_level`, shown as `Area Level: N`). A map that already exists keeps the level it was made with (alpha: no conversion).
- A map's misc `type` is its tier type, `t1m`, `t2m` or `t3m`. Each is a direct child of `cmap` (`Equiv1 cmap`, no chain between tiers, so a T3 map is not a `t2m`). The PD2 rows were reused and repointed, so no code is new. `Magic`/`Rare`/`Normal` match `cmap`.
- The tier line is one string per tier: misc `spelldesc 1`, `spelldescstr` `MapTier1`/`MapTier2`/`MapTier3` ("Tier: 1" ...), with `spelldesccalc`, `stat1` and `calc1` empty. A `spelldesc 2` line with `stat1 hpregen` (#1304's carrier) scaled the number like a healing potion, so the tier read 1/3/4 or 2/4/6 depending on the class ([#1316](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1316)). The map-open log reads `0 item stat(s)`.
- No map rolls magic naturally. `cmap` and the tier types read Magic 0, Rare 1, Normal 0; a magic map is never made: core-rules refuses the magic affix maker (D2R `0x442c60`, found by signature) for any `cmap` item, so whatever rolled magic (a champion or boss TC, a failed set/rare/unique roll, a forced quality, any call site) falls to the game's normal quality, the same result as Cartographer's roll hook (#1415). The TCs keep PD2's Magic ratios, since itemtypes and TC columns cannot refuse magic. Maps that already exist stay as they are.
- `levelreq` is unchanged. The Catalyst recipe (`cmap` + `iwss`) still matches every map, since each tier type is a child of `cmap`.
- Tier assignment, about 8 per tier, with outdoor and indoor tilesets in each (PD2's own tier where the map has a PD2 namesake: Phlegethon, Tomb of Zoltun Kulle, Blood Moon, Lost Temple, Sanatorium T1; Horazon's Memory, Ruined Cistern T2; Bastion Keep, Royal Crypts, Arreat Battlefield, Kehjistan Marketplace T3):

`maps.txt` `Monsters` (up to 10 monstats Ids, the column Cartographer writes into the map's level) lists the `*map` variants restored in #1253 and the `*map2` rows below. PD2 gave each map area its own per-area monster copies (`zombieSiege`, `mummyIce`, ...); the port has one `*map` row per base class, with PD2's `Map H2H`/`Map Cast`/`Map Miss`/`Map Swarm` `t1` or `t3` classes in `TreasureClass(H)`, `Champ(H)` and `Unique(H)`. A map's list is the monsters of the PD2 area paired with it (levels.txt row whose `Id` is the PD2 map's misc `len`, [map-system-dll.md](../pd2/map-system-dll.md); `mon1`-`mon10`), reduced to the base classes (monstats `BaseId`) that have a `*map` row, and topped up from the closest-themed area when that left fewer than 4 (marked "fill"). Excluded: `baalminionmap` (Rarity 0), the event and boss rows (`summonerMap`, `griswoldmap`, ...) and the Void `*UniqueMap` rows. Every listed row is enabled, `isSpawn` 1 and Rarity above 0 (unit test `test_map_monsters.py`).

Drop tier follows PD2's area, not the map's tier: PD2's per-area copies use `Map ... t1`, `t2` or `t3` by area. The `*map` rows only cover t1 and t3, so `monstats.txt` has 22 `<base>map2` rows (a map2 row's minions are map2 rows too) (copies of the `*map` rows whose three `(H)` TC cells point at the existing `Map ... t2` classes, appended at the end so no class id moves). A list uses `map2` where PD2's area is t2. Where an area's tier is t1 or t3 and the base's only row is the other one, the existing row is used (the two differ only in the `Map Good` area level 85/86/87); those are marked "tier differs".
