Map bosses and columns ([#1419](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1419)): every map has `Density` 150, `Champions` 100 (read, never applied), `Uniques` 100 and `MinCharLevel` 80. Bosses follow PD2's level-to-boss swap (`0x1038b990`): Ashen Plains `AshenBoss`, Halls of Torture `TortureHallsBoss`, Ruined Cistern `lernaeanhydra2` (own bosses.txt entries), Sewers of Harrogath `SewerBoss`, Blood Moon `CowBoss`. Ruins of Viz'jun `unravelerboss` (Karvarousku the Cartographer) and River of Blood `baalminionboss` (Belial Lord of Lies). With Cartographer's 16-entry cap gone (d2r-tools #552), bosses.txt has 21 entries: Johnathan The Damned (`BastionBoss`, PD2's Fortress map) takes Bastion Keep, Indio The Insane (`ThroneBoss`, PD2's Throne Map, 150) takes Khazra Den (no longer sharing Sharptooth with Lost Temple), and Rotting Horror (`PoisonedWellBoss`, PD2's name for it) takes Leoric's Passage again.

- **Treasure classes** are PD2's, over m01-m25 by tier: `Map Tier 1-3` list the maps of each tier (Rare 400, Magic 800 as PD2; a natural magic roll becomes normal), `T1 Map Drop`, `T2 Map Drop` and `T3 Map Drop` pick a tier (T1: 66/33 of T1/T2, T2: 39/40/20, T3: 32/33/33). The `Act 1-5 (H) Good` pools name `Map Tier 1`, so Hell drops outside maps are a T1 pool. `Map Good t1-t3`, `Map Boss T1-T4`, `Treasure Fallen Map`, `UberAncients` and the two `T4*MapBoss` classes call the tier drop again (their P3 no-drop lines are gone). The tierless `Cartographer Maps` class stays for the Horazon drops.
- **Map boss loot follows the map tier** ([#1423](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1423)): a boss's `superuniques.txt` row names one fixed `Map Boss T1`-`T3` class (Hell: the `Blood` variant), but the same boss opens maps of every tier (Toadflax: T1, T2 and T3), and a map's `Boss` column names one `bosses.txt` entry, so a data-only fix would need a boss entry and a `superuniques.txt` row per boss and tier. The hook keeps those tables as they are. So core-events wraps D2R's TC drop (`0x4404f0`, signature `TcDrop`; `plugin/core-events/lane-c/map_boss_tc.cpp`): when a superunique drops one of those classes in a map opened from a map item, the class of that map's tier drops instead, in the same family. The tier is the map item's type `t1m`-`t3m`, kept per game when the map item is used (log `map use: the map opened, tier N`); each swap logs `map boss tc: monster <class> in a tier N map: its row names "..", rolls ".."`. A map opened without an item keeps the row's class. Unit tests: `tools/tests/test_map_boss_tier.py` (boss x tier -> TC) and `plugin/tests/map_boss_tier_check.cpp`.
- **Map counts:** each tier holds 8/8/9 maps against PD2's 10/10/9, so each map drops slightly more often.
- **Stacking** ([#1326](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1326)): m01-m25 stack to 50, but only normal maps with equal stats merge (a core-rules hook on D2Common's stack-equal check, found at load by its byte signature). A rare map, or one with another Area Level or a forced event, stays its own item. The Ctrl+click split (stack held) copies the source's non-quantity stats onto the new piece, and a cube recipe's leftover maps keep the source's stats.
- **Anya** already sells the five orbs in `misc.txt` (`imma`, `imra`, `rera`, `scou`, `upma`). `upmp` and `fort` come with the recipes PR ([#1306](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1306)); add their `AnyaMin`/`AnyaMax` 1 then.
- **Map monsters** are the `*map` variants listed in `maps.txt` `Monsters` (section above, #1322); their TCs are the `Map ... t1/t3` classes. Not done (needs code): Anya's quest reward (a map instead of her scroll) is game code too.

Map affixes are PD2's rows in `magicprefix.txt` and `magicsuffix.txt`, in PD2's tier bands ([#1305](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1305), [#1309-#1313](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1309); `docs/features/map-affixes.md`); only the Splashing rows stay neutral. The recipes are in `docs/features/map-recipes.md`.

- **Parity: Exact.** The map tables (items, affixes, uniques, recipes, treasure classes) are already merged ([P3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/47)). The
  code is built to PD2's behaviour. If a map stat cannot be reproduced, only that stat gets its own approximated row on
  the deviation list; no whole group of stats is approximated up front.
- **Opening a map:** a right-click in Harrogath, as in PD2 (misc `pSpell` 12 -> 16). PD2's gates apply: Hell, level 80+,
  the Ancients killed, one map or uber area per game. The plugin makes the red portal itself.
  Reimagined's cube output `Red Portal,lvl=<id>` shows that a red portal reaches any Act V level, but it is not used as
  a recipe, because a recipe would change the controls and skip the gates.
- **Which area a map opens** comes from `ProjectDiablo.dll`, read with Ghidra, never paired by name. [MS1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/216) found that
  the DLL takes it from the misc `len` column, so the port reads that column
  ([pd2-map-system-dll.md](../pd2/map-system-dll.md), which also holds the gates, stat routing, op 30 and the
  event roll).
- **Map drops:** the [P3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/47) no-drop lines in `merge/item-tables.txt` come back in the same work item that makes maps openable,
  so no build drops a map you cannot use.
- **Stacking:** normal maps stack to 50 and split as in PD2 (Ctrl+left-click with the stack held). Every PD2 stackable
  shares this, so it is built once in [#316](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/316), not in a map item ([#210](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/210)).
- **Invaders** run their table AIs (the vanilla `BloodRaven`, `Summoner` and so on). That is an approximated deviation.
  The portal's think and the invaders' ears and drops are PD2's (MS10, `plugin/core-events/lane-c/invaders.cpp`).
  PD2's own invader brain (`AiThink4.cpp`) replaces them in [MS11](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/225).
- **Plugins:** `core-events` (Shared) holds the code that belongs only to the map system: opening maps, map stats, cube
  op 30, map events and invaders. It is a plugin of its own because the map system is large enough to be used outside
  this project ([ADR 0004](../adr/0004-plugins-split-by-multiplayer-scope.md), amended). Rules the map system shares with
  other content stay in `core-rules`: the Teleport 3 blocker check, the
  Find Item and Desecrate monster lists, and the death novas. `core-events` never calls `core-rules`.
- **Rules deferred to the map plan** (core-rules rows and their deviation rows) join the work item that first brings in
  their levels or monsters (table below).
- **D2R Reimagined:** we copy no code from them. Their GPL-3.0 code stays out (ADR 0005), and their map plugin is
  closed source. We use their engine findings as facts, with credit in the research doc: one world rectangle per Act V
  level, automap `Layer` under 100, `Position=0` on new levels, a self-linked entry warp so the portal lands at the
  start, and maze routines that place stairs only for fixed level ids. If a build item hits an engine limit that we
  cannot solve, reverse engineering their `d2rl-maps.dll` with Ghidra becomes an investigation of its own. It is for
  knowledge only, and no code is copied.
- **Level ids:** D2R's merged `levels` table has 138 rows, so PD2's 74 areas append to about ids 139-212, under the 255
  limit.

The Warlock is the one class not held to the PD2 baseline. It is D2R's Warlock on build 93847, changed only where a
skill falls short of PD2's style: a skill that already meets the bar below stays as D2R has it. No full redesign is
needed. These are its goals, set in [#149](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/149). The tree is not
redrafted ([#150](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/150) was dropped): changes go into the change log one
skill at a time. Balance targets and items were set in [#195](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/195).

1. **Identity.** Keep D2R's three trees and their themes: Demon (summons, blood), Eldritch (sword, blades, hexes) and
   Chaos (fire, sigils, miasma).
2. **Skill count.** The class ends at 33 skills, 11 per tree, like PD2's classes. The alpha ships D2R's 30 skills,
   changed where needed, with one grid position per tree left empty; the three new skills fill those positions in the beta.
3. **The PD2-style bar.**
   - Every tree carries at least one full endgame build.
   - Main skills get PD2-style synergies written on their descriptions, mostly from their own tree.
   - No dead skills: each skill is a main skill, a synergy, a working one-point utility or a prerequisite worth taking.
   - A mastery per tree is not required.
4. **Allowed changes.** Numbers, synergies, prerequisites, a skill's position inside its own tree, and reworking how one
   skill works while it keeps its theme. Not allowed: moving a skill to another tree, replacing a skill, re-theming a
   tree or reworking a whole tree; PD2 has never done these.
5. **Engine budget.** Only engine rules the port already has or builds anyway: D2R's Warlock functions and PD2's
   functions ported for the other classes. Each new engine rule needs the owner's approval.
6. **Baseline.** D2R's Warlock on build 93847. The change log below records every change from it and why. A D2R patch
   that changes the Warlock is reviewed as a re-baseline, not followed.

- Hellfire Torch and Spirit Ward roll classes 0-7 (the committed `itemtypes.txt`), as D2R's own Torch does.
- Corruption and crafting already reach grimoires: PD2's rows name item types (`shld,nos`, `shld,mag,noe`), and a
  grimoire is a `shld`.
- PD2 made class affixes ten times as common (frequency 1, 2, 4 -> 10, 20, 40); D2R's Warlock affixes take the same
  (the patch).
- PD2 added, for each other class, +1 class skills on body armor, shields and helms, and two kinds with `rare` 3:
  +2 class skills on the same, and +3 to each tree on the class's items. `rare` 3 means rare items only
  ([#254](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/254)): ProjectDiablo.dll's affix picker (rva `0x389080`,
  its quality from D2Common #10106; asm `0x3892c1`-`0x38934c`) takes `rare` 0 on no rare, crafted or tempered item
  (quality 6, 8, 9), 1 on any, 2 on no crafted or tempered item (no PD2 row has 2), and 3 on quality 6 only. D2R
  reads the column as a flag (`0x58c940`), so core-rules refuses 2 and 3 where PD2 does (`loot_rules.cpp`,
  `docs/features/core-rules.md`). The Warlock gets the same five rows, the
  tree ones on daggers and grimoires as its other tree affixes, at ids 1042-1046 (the `+` lines in
  `merge/ids-magicprefix.tsv`).
- PD2's grand-charm skillers also roll on the PvP charm (`lchp`); PvP is cut, so the Warlock's don't.

Research for [#1064](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1064). It reads PD2's `ProjectDiablo.dll` and the
1.13c `D2Game.dll` from the PD2 install in Ghidra (project `PD2.gpr`) and compares them with main at 80cd1575. Static
reading only: the game was not run. Addresses are PD2's: `ProjectDiablo.dll` addresses from its `0x10000000` base,
`D2Game.dll` RVAs from its `0x6fc20000` base. Monster ids are PD2's unless marked "port".
From [pd2-map-system-dll.md](map-system-dll.md) section 4, checked again in `0x1036fef0` (room activation):

- The map roll picks event 14 (`game+0x1df4 == 0xe`) for 1 in 9 rolled tiered maps.
- The n-th Wanderer (n = 1..3, count at `game+0x2628`, `puVar2[0x98a]`) spawns when `n x 25 < progress` and
  `rand() % 100 < 25`. Progress is the level's activated rooms x 100 / a per-level room constant (`0x1038b1d0`).
- The spot is the activating room's centre, through the spot search `0x10389c20(xy, room, mask 0x805, reach 8, shift 1)`;
  the spawn is `0x1038a170` -> `0x1038a060(x, y, class 0x399, 1)`. `0x1038a060` spawns through `0x10371c30` and sets
  bits `0x3000000` of the unit flags (+0xc4); nothing there makes him untargetable.
- Each spawn sends `MapEventNotifyDarkWanderer`.
think is `D2Game 0xa6e60` (the only pointer to it is the AI table entry at `D2Game 0x10ed40`):

1. `0xe2780`: the a3q7 gate. It walks the game's quest list (`game+0x10f4`) for quest 0x1c and returns 0 unless that
   quest's data byte +0 is set (only the Act 3 docks set it). On success it writes the spot (quest data +4/+8, y-20 on first use, nudged by
   `Ordinal_10686` collision checks) into the think's local.
2. `0xa6e8e: TEST EAX,EAX` / `0xa6e90: JZ` -> idle 10 frames (`0xf22c0(10)`).

**PD2's patch.** `ProjectDiablo.dll`'s patch table (installed DLL, file offset `0x49bfc8`) holds the entry
`{dll 3 (D2Game), offset 0xa6e90, fill 0x90, type 0, length 2}` (its neighbours are type-1 hooks: `{3, offset, hook address, 1, 0}`): it NOPs the `JZ`. So the gate's result is ignored and the
think always runs. In a map the gate returns 0 without writing the spot, so the walk target is whatever is on the
stack: undefined, in practice not reachable.

- No target, or the target 20 or more away (`tick+0x14 >= 0x14`): idle 40 frames (10 with no target).
- State 0 -> 1 (`monster AI params +0x14`), trips (+0x18) = 0.
- State 1: walk to the spot (`0xf2540`), state 2.
- State 2: if the distance to the spot (`0xb07b0`) is below 2, or trips > 2: unit flag `0x20000` (no treasure), death
  mode (`0xf21e0(game, unit, 0, 0)`), then a3q7's callback `0xe6760`. Else trips + 1 and walk again.

`0xe6760` marks quest 0x1c's data (+0xd = 1, +0x10 = his unit id) and runs the quest's update the first time in a game
(+0xc and +0xd clear). In a map that is the first Wanderer to leave: a3q7's effect `0xe57d0` (8 missiles around him, a
player quest update). Main skips it on purpose (#1087, so the real a3q7 never arms); see Open questions.

The leave puts him in death mode, so PD2's dead-mode wrapper `0x1037a330` runs its steps. `0x10375fe0`, class 0x399:
sound 705 to every client (`0x1037f240`), then a unit timer (`0x103164f0`, type 7) at frame + 0x55 (85) with callback
`0x10370d90`. That callback (decompiled again here, same as #1006's comment):
- One free-spot search at the corpse (`0x10389ad0`, size 1); none, no boss.
monstats count + hcIdx (`0x1030cb00(2, id)`), plus monsters 256 izual and 267 bloodraven as they are.
- Spawn `0x103a1420(id, room, game, x, y, 1)`: the stock spawn, so the level is the area's (no level override).
Not the boss's TC and not the superunique row: a death step. `0x1037a330` calls `0x10379950` near the end, only when
the dying unit lacks unit flag `0x20000` (no treasure):

```
0x379957: CMP dword ptr [EAX + 0x1df4],0xe      ; the map's event is the Dark Wanderer
0x379960: PUSH 0xd5 / CALL 0x1030c320          ; the dying monster has state 213 (mapevent)
0x379974: code = 'wss '                         ; Worldstone Shard
0x379984: CALL 0x1036f320                       ; the monster's seed
0x37998b: DIV 7 ; EDI = rem + 4                 ; 4..10 drops
0x3799a5: 0x1036ebc0(game, monster, code, 7, 0x83, 0, 0, 0, 3) x EDI
```

Answers research ticket [#3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/3) (map [#1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/1)). Sorting scheme from [`knowledge/porting-classic-mods.md`](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/ce0a3174ec1ca7c08a1d27d54e63ab1aa9e844d3/knowledge/porting-classic-mods.md) section 1 of the d2rAI-toolkit:
(a) data only, (b) D2RLoader service, (c) native hook, (d) UI rebuild, (e) cut.

- PD2's own engine code is two things: `ProjectDiablo.dll` (5.2 MB, the client/server/UI core, with guilds) and `BH.dll` (1.4 MB, the
  loot filter and screen-info layer). `PD2_EXT.dll` is only a loader shim. Everything else is third-party, and most of it D2R already
  does natively.
- Cut outright (D2R covers or makes it irrelevant): `D2HD.dll`, d2gl (`glide3x.dll`), cnc-ddraw (`ddraw.dll`), SGD2FreeRes, `PD2_EXT.dll`,
  the Battle.net/launcher plumbing, and PlugY's windowing, language and save-path options.
- The real porting work is the loot filter (BH), the stash system (categories, search, shared and hardcore-shared stashes, currency tab),
  custom item/skill rules in `ProjectDiablo.dll`, controller support, and the PD2 aura/event/notification features. Most of it is
  UI rebuild plus plugin services. Native hooks are needed for a handful of server rules.
- Guilds (a large subsystem with its own save blob and UI) belong with the online/server features the map marks out of scope. Cut for now.
- Whether the `ProjectDiablo.dll` rule hooks need hooks or are data-only cannot be settled from the DLL strings. That needs the
  data-table diff (new function numbers in `pd2data.mpq`), which is a separate ticket.

[`knowledge/porting-classic-mods.md`](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/ce0a3174ec1ca7c08a1d27d54e63ab1aa9e844d3/knowledge/porting-classic-mods.md) (sections 0 to 1, 5 to 6) and [`knowledge/engine-re.md`](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/ce0a3174ec1ca7c08a1d27d54e63ab1aa9e844d3/knowledge/engine-re.md) in the d2rAI-toolkit for the bucket definitions and
D2R's existing hook points.
Addresses are RVAs from the DLL's `0x10000000` base. Level ids are PD2's `levels` ids. Stat ids are PD2's

- **The area is data, not a DLL table.** The map handler evaluates the item's misc `len` column as an item calc
  (D2Common ordinal 10428) and uses the result as the level id. Every map row holds its level there (section 1), so the
  port reads `len` too. The `missiletype` column picks the portal object (584 `xactportal_red` for maps).
- **Gates:** Hell, character level 80+, Rite of Passage done (Hell quest 39), standing in Harrogath (level 109), and no
  map yet in this game (the game's map-event field is 0). Uber areas skip the level-80 check. Levels 152, 153 (the
  disabled Cathedral of Light) and 255 always fail.
- **Map stats are routed by the `Divide` column.** PD2 repurposes `itemstatcost.Divide` on `map_*` stats: below 1000 the
  stat goes to monsters as that vanilla stat id; `1xxx` goes to players as stat `xxx`; `2xxx` is area slot `xxx`; `3xxx`
  is phys-as-extra damage; `1024` (the default) goes to monsters unchanged. Monsters get their list on spawn, players on
  entering a map area, both as a stat list under state 198.
- **Density and rarity scale by `1 + v/100`.** They multiply the level's monster-region `MonDen` and its champion/unique
  pack min and max. Area level adds `v`. Fortify (skirmish mode) multiplies all three by `v/100` and adds fixed monster
  stats.
- **Cube op 30 blocks always.** If an op-30 row matches the cube's contents, the transmute stops and nothing is made, so
  the row shadows the rows after it. Its inputs (for example `nor` maps) decide what it blocks; stacking does not.
- **Event roll:** tiered maps only. Chance by the map's quality: rare 34%, magic 17%, normal 11%; a Catalyst Shard
  (`map_force_event`) forces one. The event is one of 9, uniform (8 when forced: no Altar of the Catalyst). Dungeons,
  unique maps, uber and PvP areas never roll.
- **Events that open areas:** the Void/Tomb event (one event: `MapEventNotifyVoid` is never used) spawns a gold portal to
  level 207. Horazon's death opens a red portal to a random tiered map of the same or the next tier, never the current
  level, and copies the map's area stats onto it.
- **A plugin can open a red portal to a map area.** D2R's portal maker (`0x432ce0` in the 93847 dump) takes the
  destination level and object 60, the red portal. It needs the same act and a level id up to 255; the port's map
  levels (Act V, about 139-212) fit both. PD2's own portal objects (`OperateFn` 77) do not exist in D2R's 75-entry
  operate table, so the port uses object 60.
The use handler is `0x383060`, called from `0x36b9f0` with (game, player, item). Its order:

1. Refuse if the player unit's `+0x6C` word is set, or the game's map-event field (`game+0x1DF4`) is above 0. Value
   0x28 (set by the Uber Tristram cube recipe, op 28) is the one exception: it lets levels 136 and 185 open.
2. Look up the item's `ItemsTxt` record and evaluate its `len` calc (`+0xB0`) through D2Common ordinal 10428 (the item
   calc evaluator). The result is the target level. `missiletype` (`+0xFA`) is the portal object; 0 means object 60.
3. Refuse levels 152, 153 and 255 (`0x37f450`).
4. PvP arenas (157, 159, 166; `0x37c7b0`) only open from the Rogue Encampment (level 1). Cut with PvP.
5. Otherwise: refuse in Normal and Nightmare. In Hell, refuse a character below level 80 unless the target is in the
   uber set {136, 137, 161, 162, 163, 168, 185, 188, 189}. Refuse if the Hell quest record lacks quest 39 (Rite of
   Passage, the Ancients). Refuse unless the player stands in level 109 (Harrogath).
6. Uber keys whose target is in {137, 161, 168, 188} go to their own branch (uber milestone, not covered here).
7. Make the portal pair next to the player with `0x38a300` (room, x, y, level, object): it places the object, sets its
   destination and builds the return portal in the target level.
8. Route the map's stats (section 2), send the client packet 0x55 with up to 24 of them (the map tooltip in the HUD),
   and apply the area stats to the level (`0x38b4d0`).
9. Set the map-event field: unique maps get their own value (0x1E-0x24, below); otherwise the event roll (section 4).

**Event-type values** in `game+0x1DF4`: 0 none yet; 9 dungeon (no event); 10 no event rolled; 11-21 the events
(section 4); 0x1E Zhar (176), 0x1F Warlord of Blood (181), 0x20 Fallen Gardens (183), 0x21 Outer Void (180), 0x22
Imperial Palace (192), 0x23 Ureh (195), 0x24 Djinn's Domain (197); 0x28-0x2D uber areas.

records.excerpt:
**Where the area slots land.** `0x38b4d0` (game, level, first) writes D2Game's monster region of that level
(`game+0xF0 + level*4`): `+0x2B8` `MonDen`, `+0x2BC` and `+0x2BD` the boss (champion/unique pack) min and max, `+0x14` the
13 monster groups, `+0x2DC` and `+0x2E0` the monster level. Those are the same fields D2R fills from the `levels` row
(`MonDen`, `MonUMin`/`MonUMax`, `mon1`-`mon25`, `MonLvlEx`), so the port can scale them where D2R builds a level's
monster region. Density's multiplier is also kept in `game+0x262C`. Slots 4, 12 and 14 add stats to the monster list only
on the first call.

**Monsters.** On spawn (`0x38af90`, called from `0x371590` and `0x371c30`), a monster in a map area (levels 137-210,
not the guild halls 202-206; `0x37c510`) gets the monster list. A monster whose monstats `Align` byte (`+0x4C`) is set
(allies, neutral) gets an empty list. The list is applied by `0x38aa00` as a stat list under state 198. Two cases are
rewritten on the way:

**Players.** A hook on the player's level change (`0x38b000`) applies the player list under state 198 when the new level
is a map area, and removes state 198 and state 212 when it is not.
Two functions decide it. `0x365fe0` collects the candidate rows for the cube's contents. Every other op must pass its
filters there (difficulty, class, input count, and a stackable-item check); op-30 rows skip them. `0x366f40` then walks
the candidates in order. The first row whose inputs fully match (`0x364e30`) is used, and if that row's op is 30, the
function returns without making anything. Op 31 calls `CubeFunctions.cpp` (`0x3669b0`) instead.
**Roll** (in `0x383060`, after the stats). Tiered maps only: the roll is skipped when the level is in the dungeon set

**When it spawns** (`0x36fef0`, run as rooms of a map area activate). The event waits for the level's progress:
`progress = region[+0x04] x 100 / constant(level)`, where the constant is a hard-coded per-level switch (`0x38b1d0`). For
the tiered maps it is 120-280 (for example Arreat Battlefield 139: 240, Phlegethon 145: 270, Lost Temple 158: 120);
unknown levels use 200. `region[+0x04]` counts the level's rooms activated so far: 1.13c D2Game's room monster spawn
(`0x6fc67a20`, which PD2's spawner wraps and calls last) first calls `0x6fc66cd0`, which adds 1 to it
([MS8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/222)). So the constant is a room count.

- One-shot events (Mendeln, Horazon, Gheed, Altar, Void/Tomb): spawn once when `rand() % 100 + progress > 140`.
- Dark Wanderer and Treasure Fallen: the n-th of 3 spawns when `n x 25 < progress` and `rand() % 100 < 25`.
- Invaders: the n-th of 3 when `25 + (n-1) x 20 < progress` and `rand() % 100 < 25`.
- Spire of Darkness: the altar spawns with a 20% roll once `region[+0x04] > 15`; its waves follow, and at progress above
  90 `0x36eb30` runs.

**The altars** ([#504](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/504), [#505](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/505)). Both use PD2's operate 79 (`0x3aa460`; PD2's
operate table is filled in `0x36c320`: 77 `0x3a9780`, 78 `0x3aa270`, 79 `0x3aa460`, 80 `0x3aa670`). `game+0x2628` is
the event's state:

- Altar of the Catalyst (event 19): the spawn places object 611 by the spot search, state 1. The first use sets the
  altar's mode 1, adds its open event and spawns monster 1064 `GuardianOfFate` 10-29 subtiles from it (40 tries, spot
  size 2), state 2. Its death (`0x378080`, event 19 and state 2) sets state 3 and kills the `GuardianOfFateClone`s
  (1065) around it; the guardian's AI (`0x35a6b0`) summons them. The next use sets mode 3 and drops 2 or 3 `iwss`
  (Catalyst Shard) by the altar at item level 90 (`0x36ebc0`), state 4.
- Spire of Darkness (event 16): the altar goes at a random point of the room (`0x389ea0`), then the spot search; fog
  object 374 at (x+2, y), (x, y+2) and (x-1, y-1); state 1. The use sets the altar's mode 1, darkens the level's act
  (`0x37dc70`: packet 0x53, D2's Tainted Sun) and plays sounds 0xa78 and 0x24 to the user's level (`0x37f240`), state 2.
  While the state is 2-49 each room activation draws `rand() % 6`: 1, 2 or 3 spawn a group of 993, 994 or 995 (MinGrp to
  MaxGrp read from the monstats record, +0x2f and +0x30: 3-6, 8-14, 1) at the room's centre +- 5 (spot size 10).
  `0x36eb30`, past progress 90: state 50, the darkness lifted (`0x37dc70` with 0), sound 0x26d for the level's players
  (`0x37f240`, packet 0x2c), and every 993-995 in the game killed without drops (`0x356e00`; it reads only the first
  monster of each of the 128 lists at `game+0x1320`).
The objects go through `0x38a060`, which spawns an object in mode 0 (it passes `type != 2` as the mode) and sets
bits `0x3000000` of its unit flags.
**Void / Tomb** (event 21): the spawn places object 586 `xactportal_gold` by the spot search, then `0x38a1f0` places
another 586 in level 207 at its spot (`0x38a000`) and `0x38a510` links the two both ways; object 594 marks the spot.
**Horazon** (`0x377ca0`, on `summonerMap`'s death while the event is live). It builds a pool from three hard-coded level

Three flags on the event context pick the lists: T1 and T2, T2 and T3, or T3 alone. That fits the wiki's "same or higher
tier". The flags are the dying monster's level: `0x3760a0` sets them when it is in the T1 set (`0x105deb18`), the
T2 set (`0x105debf4`) or the T3 set (`0x105deb08`), the same sets the pool is built from ([MS9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/223)). The handler
runs only while the event is Horazon's and `game+0x2628` is 1, which its portal raises, so once per game. It draws a
level other than the current one, adds an area entry (slot 10, value = the level), applies the area stats to that
level (`0x38b4d0` with first = 0, so no monster stats are added again), and opens a red portal (object 60) to it at
the monster (`0x38a300`). With a 10% roll it calls `0x381510`. Then it drops from treasureclassex rows 54-56 (`Map Tier
1`, `Map Tier 2`, `Map Tier 3`; `0x37f430` adds the row to the compiled TC base): 3, 2 and 1 picks in a T1 map, 1, 3
and 2 in T2, 1, 2 and 3 in T3, through 1.13c's TC drop (`0x30f120`).
**No events at all** spawn in the uber areas and unique-map areas (the set at RVA `0x5def44`).

D2R's portal maker `0x432ce0` (game, unit, room, x, y, destLevel, &object, objectId, 0, 1), from the toolkit's
[address notes](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/ce0a3174ec1ca7c08a1d27d54e63ab1aa9e844d3/knowledge/d2r-93847-addresses.md), is the
counterpart of PD2's `0x38a300`: it places the portal object, sets its destination and places the return portal.
Object 60 is the red portal. D2R's limits that apply ([toolkit `engine-limits.md`](https://github.com/synpoox/d2rAI-toolkit/blob/ce0a3174ec1ca7c08a1d27d54e63ab1aa9e844d3/knowledge/engine-limits.md)):
- The destination setter `0x34e9d0` keeps one byte. The port's map-area level ids (about 139-212) are below 256.
plugin in this repo calls `0x432ce0` yet.

[MS7b](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/499), read in Ghidra: `FindDisp 0x1df4` over ProjectDiablo.dll
lists every instruction on the field; these are the ones that test 9 or 0x1E-0x24. Monsters are PD2 `hcIdx` (the port's
id is 17 more), levels PD2 ids. Most readers are entries of the monster-death switch `0x10378d80` (keyed on the dead
monster's class), which PD2's death handler `0x1037a330` calls. Its context is: +0 game, +8 the monster, +0xC the
killer's player (when a player), +0x14 the uniqueitems table, +0x5C an item code for the drop helper `0x1036ebc0`
(code, quality, item level). `0x1038a300` (x, y, level, object) is the portal at the body with its return portal.

  scripts kept outside the repo, plus `patchstring.tbl` through `tools/pd2_strings.py`'s `read_tbl`. "Row N" means the
  Nth data row, counted from 0 after the header. Where a number is a file line (the header is line 1), it is called a
  line. The ticket's "rows 181 and 184" are lines of the merged `out/.../cubemain.txt`; they are data rows 179 and 182.

  [Patch:Season 3](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Patch:Season_3) and
  [Patch:Season 5](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Patch:Season_5). The wiki is a secondary source. Where it and the

records.excerpt: Both gates run one after the other in the two player set-mode paths (the code around `0x784ba` and the function at
`0x78550`); a 0 return from either drops the mode change.

Arguments: game, player, requested mode, a flag, the skill the new mode will use. Unchanged parts: refuse if the player is
`uninterruptable` (state 54), dead or dying; allow if the request is death or the flag is 0; a skill flagged in skills.txt
(dword +4 bit 31, read here as `interrupt`; inferred, not confirmed) takes the `concentrate` (state 15) / `concentration`
(state 42, roll against `skill_concentration`, stat 164) path; otherwise a neutral player is put through `0x78550` and
allowed, and a busy one is allowed only for listed modes that pass the frame check `0x77e00`.
PD2's changes, keyed on the current skill's `srvdofunc`:

1. **Inferno and Arctic Blast (182)**: any request that carries a skill is allowed at once. New in PD2 (182 is PD2's own
   function number).
2. **Blade Fury (48)**: a request with a different skill is allowed at once; another Blade Fury request is refused, so
   the channel keeps going. New.
3. **Charge (PD2's 180)** joins Charge (67) and Whirlwind / Blade Dance (76) in the "same skill again is allowed" rule, and
   the rule now also allows requests with no skill (vanilla: same skill only).
4. **Run (mode 3)** is added to the modes a busy player may switch to when the frame check passes (vanilla: attack 1/2,
   cast, throw, skill 1, sequence).
5. **Concentrate / Concentration**: when the roll keeps a busy player uninterrupted, vanilla refuses every request; PD2
   still allows the listed modes when the frame check passes. Net: Concentration blocks get-hit, not your next attack.

| Current mode | Vanilla | PD2 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 death, 17 dead | refuse | refuse |
| 1 neutral, 3 run | allow | cast (10) or sequence (18) refused until 5 frames after a timestamp at player data `+0x16c`; the rest allowed |
| 4 get-hit, 9 block | refuse | allowed in the last 2 frames before the mode's end event |
| 7, 8, 10, 11 attack, cast, throw | frame check, else only get-hit/block | same |
| 12 kick, 13 skill 1, 15 skill 3 | frame check; class not Amazon; class not Druid | same |
| 18 sequence | allowed if the skill has `seqinput`, else frame check | same check, PD2 reads its own copy of the skills table |
| 2, 5, 6, 14, 16 | allow | allow |
| 1 neutral, 3 run | allow | cast (10) or sequence (18) refused until 5 frames after a timestamp at player data `+0x16c`; the rest allowed |

records.excerpt: The end frame is the unit's earliest type-1 timer event (`0x8e490`, the mode-end event). The vanilla check is
## Life regen (`0x77cba` -> `0x102fc000`)

PD2 wraps the `hpregen` read in the player regen tick: when `0x1037c820` is true for the player's level (a level-id test
through `pPath->pRoom->...->pLevel+0x1d0`, not decoded further) and the value is over 30, it returns 30, or the
`bloodwarp` (state 205) stat list's value when that state is on. [MS3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/218) decoded the test: it is true only in the PvP arenas
(levels 157, 159, 166), so the cap is cut with PvP ([ms3-map-stats](../research/maps/ms3-map-stats.md)).

D2R has its own `PlrModes.cpp` (`D2Game\src\Player\PlrModes.cpp` asserts). Its mode change (`0x429d10`; [W21](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/96) found
this is a mode-table entry, and gate A's counterpart is `0x42bfb0` / `0x42d840`, [druid-w21](../research/skills/druid-w21.md)) is a rewrite:
it switches on the current mode, reads skill flags at txt `+0x24`/`+0x27`/`+0x36` instead of `srvdofunc` numbers, has
input windows of 2 and 6 frames, and adds a `bear` (state 140) roll next to Concentration. So D2R is not 1.13c here, and
PD2's patches can't be carried over as code.

- Each change above is a `verify` row: first check in D2R whether it already behaves as PD2 (D2R's buffered input may
  already cover 4 and part of gate B), then hook `0x429d10` only for what differs. Rows added to core-rules.
- 1-3 key on PD2's function numbers (180, 182), so they wait for the skills that use them (P2 remaps ids; [W8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/54)-[W10](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/51) cover
  Charge's group). Whirlwind/Blade Dance (76) and Blade Fury (48) are vanilla numbers.
- The regen cap is PvP only, cut with PvP ([MS3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/218)).
- Not decoded: the death handler and the two other hooks. They need their own read before any death-rule row is listed.

- **PD2 ships one string table: `patchstring.tbl`, English only.** It holds 3,278 entries (3,152 distinct keys). PD2 does not replace `string.tbl` or `expansionstring.tbl`; it overrides their keys from `patchstring.tbl`.
- **1,934 keys are new** (in no vanilla 1.13c table and not in D2R). **79 vanilla keys have changed text**; 34 of those change only colour codes (mostly rune names). The other 1,131 keys repeat vanilla text.
- **New keys land mostly in item and skill files:** skills 394, item-modifiers 268, item-names 237, item-nameaffixes 188, monsters 127, levels 99, item-runes 23, others 20. 320 are looked up by name from `ProjectDiablo.dll` (UI, guild, stash, hotkeys), and 256 have no reference I could find.
- **Collisions with D2R-only content are few:** 4 keys PD2 adds that D2R also added (`Runeword171` means a different runeword; 3 have the same text), plus 4 keys that differ from a D2R key only by letter case. No Warlock key collides.
- **The ID budget is ample.** 37,429 free IDs between 28,106 and 65,535 after skipping D2R's used low-16-bit values. All new keys use about 5% (IDs 28,106 to about 30,043).
- **Markup:** PD2 uses the same `ÿc` colour form as D2R (311 strings), plus three codes D2R's English text never uses (`ÿc;`, `ÿc:`, `ÿc/`). 242 strings are multi-line. D2R reversed the line order of multi-line skill text, so PD2's skill descriptions need their lines flipped. Placeholders are `%d`, `%s`, `%%` and 5 uses of `%S`.
- **The DLLs build a lot of text at run time.** `ProjectDiablo.dll` names 324 table keys and has about 140 English literals; `BH.dll` names only one table key and has about 140 English literals with inline colour codes. Both are plugin work, not data.

records.excerpt: ## 2. Opening at the Blood Fountain (`0x10383060`)

1. It fails if the player is busy, or if `game+0x1df4` > 0 (an area is already open). The exception is 0x28, which
   allows only levels 136 and 185.
2. Level = the item's misc `len` (dcma 137, rtma 161, luca 188, ubtm 185). Maps open a portal whose object is misc
   `missiletype` (584 red for maps, dcma and ubtm, 585 ghostly for rtma, 622 dark grey for luca), or 60 when the column
   is empty.
3. Gates: Hell only, character level 80 or more, Rite of Passage done (quest flag 0x27), and the player stands in
   Harrogath (level 109). Levels 0x98, 0x99 and 0xff are refused.
4. **Uber keys only** (levels 136, 137, 161, 168, 185, 188; 168 is PD2's Uber Ancients, cut in the port): `0x1037d840` must report the player at most 0x95 from
   (5074, 5114), the Blood Fountain. `0x1037d840` returns the squared distance, so that is within about 12 subtiles (read for [UB2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/227)). The tier is the item's stat 185 (`uber_difficulty`). For levels 137, 161 and 188 it
   is stored in `game+0x2629`.
5. **Uber keys warp the group straight in. No portal is opened.** The code places object 587 (invisible) at the use
   spot. `0x1038a680` then warps every player in Harrogath whose squared distance to the fountain is under 0x96 and who is level 80 or more. Each
   player goes through the portal-entry code in section 3. The count is stored in `game+0x2628`, and the opening fails
   if it is 0. So the uber keys' `missiletype` is not used here. For 585 and 622 it matches the portals the fights open
   later (sections 5-6).
6. It sets `game+0x1df4` to the area type (table above). For Dclone, Rathma and Lucion it also clears the stage bytes.
7. **Tier 0:** it spawns three object-595 portals (`xactportal_grey`) at (5076, 5119), (5068, 5108) and (5079, 5110)
   around the fountain. These are the re-entries. Tiers 1 and 2 get none.

So a key's tier and target are data, and the fountain check is one distance test. [UB2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/227) builds this on [MS2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/217)'s map-use hook.
## 3. Area rules (portal entry, `0x103a9780`)

- **Entries are counted** in `game+0x2628`.
- **The boss heals 20% of its maximum life** on each entry (Dclone, Lucion, and both Rathma and Mendeln). This is the
  entry code's own heal; Dclone's AI has a second, separate one (section 5).
- **Pets are removed** (`0x1037fb10` with flag 0). This covers every pet type except type 3 (`golem` in pettype.txt; the Iron Golem is type 22 and goes too), and the
  hireling (type 7) is killed. This is the "mercenary killed" rule.
- **37 states are stripped** (`0x1037f4a0` with flag 1): enchant, coldenchant, venomclaws, shout, battleorders,
  battlecommand, wolf, bear, fade, quickness, energyshield, shiverarmor, chillingarmor, bonearmor, cyclonearmor,
  bladeshield, holyshield, holysword, thunderstorm, thawing, antidote, every shrine state (128-137), monsterset and
  blood_mana. Battlecry, openwounds, freeze and cold are always stripped. These are the "pre-buffs removed".
- **Tier-0 portals are single use.** Taking an object-595 portal removes it.
- **Rathma tier 0 re-entry** comes out at the current stage's spot: (0x476b, 0x35d3) after stage 1, (0x47d7, 0x3961)
  after stage 3, and (0x4e98, 0x1419) after stage 5.
  The opening links the three portals (kept at `game+0x261c`-`0x2624`) to an `empty` marker (587) at the use spot.
  At tier 0, a portal taken from outside Harrogath into a Rathma level relinks them (`0x1038a510`) to a new marker:
  the arena portal (its level is the player's own) at the spot of stage 1, 3 or 5+ by `game+0x262a` (none in stages 2
  and 4), a portal to the next level at that level's spawn spot (`0x1038a1f0` with the destination level:
  `0x1038a000` takes D2Common's act spawn location, then `0x10389ad0` finds a free spot). The relink sets the portals'
  level too.
- On arrival in levels 136, 137, 161-163 or 185, the level's `Waypoint` objects are removed.
- **No exit block.** PD2 does not refuse save-and-exit or a death exit, and no reader of `game+0x1df4` or of the uber
  level ids does. Tiers 1-2 open no way back, and the three tier-0 portals are the only re-entry.
## 4. Tier scaling (`0x10381160`, state 241 `uberscaling`)

PD2's monster spawn hook (`0x10371c30`) runs the map stats (`0x1038af90`), then `0x10371a70`. That runs the scaling on
each monster spawning in a PD2 level (levels 0x89-0xd2 except 0xca-0xce) without state 241, with the tier from
`game+0x2629`. **The scaling only takes the 30 monsters of the uber fights** (the set at `0x105def0c`: Dclone 789, his
skeletons 886-891 and trapped souls 790-794, Rathma and Mendeln 933-936, their golems, totem and spire 937-939 and 966,
the void knights 968, 969, 1106 and 1107, Lucion 1112 with 1113-1115, 1140 and 1141). It puts its stats in a stat list
(flags 8) under state 241, attaches it, sets the new maxhp as the base stat and sets state 241, so no monster is scaled
twice. With *e* = max(entries − 1, 0), entries being the byte at `game+0x2628`:

- **Max life:** from the total maxhp, at tier 0, ×1.5 (×3 / 2, 64-bit). At tiers 1-2, ×4 for the bosses (the set at
  `0x105deec4`: Dclone 789, Rathma and Mendeln 933/934, their clones 935/936, Lucion 1112) or ×3 for the rest. Then
  + tier × trunc(that × 20 / 100), capped at 0x7fffffff. So a boss has ×4.8 at tier 1 and ×5.6 at tier 2.
- **+4 to all skills** (stat 127) per tier.
- **The bosses only:** fire, lightning and cold absorb % (stats 142/144/148) +7×tier + 2×e, magic absorb % (146) +3×tier
  + 2×e, damage resist (36) +3×e, poison length resist (110) +3×tier + e.
- Then it calls `0x1030bd80` (a D2Common thunk on the unit, not identified) and gives the list a removal callback
  (`0x10312350`).

The scripts read their numbers from the boss's monstats record: `aip1`-`aip8` per difficulty at +0x56, skills `Skill1-8`
at +0x170 with modes at +0x180. They use stats 446/447 (`mon_cooldown1/2`) as timers and phase counters. Shared by all
three: while `game+0x26fe` > 0 the boss is immune (all six resists set to 200 and curses removed, `0x10380770`) and idles.
The counter goes down only while a player is in the level. A hook at `0x102fc6c0`, on D2Game's room-release pass
(`D2Game+0x2cf30`, called when a room has gone more than 10 ticks without a player), starts that 15-tick window when the
room holds a registered boss (`game+0x2600` to `+0x2624`) from the fight-monster set at `0x105dc078`. That set holds 30
ids: Dclone, his adds and trapped souls, the Rathma group with its golems, totem and void knights, and Lucion with his
controller, spawner and adds. So a boss left alone, or pulled out of every player's range, goes immune and idle.
### Diablo Clone, "Dclone" (`0x1035b3f0`)

- It registers itself as the boss (`game+0x2600`). Each tick it counts the players in its level and keeps the count. When
  the count drops (a player leaves or dies), it heals 20% of max life, capped at max.
- **Cold-nova phases:** below 75%, 50% and 25% life (doubles 100 − (phase/2)×25), with stat 447 = 2, 4 or 6, its life is
  reset to that percentage. It then walks to the arena centre (15129, 6548), killing any monster standing on the centre
  spot (skill slot 8, MonTeleport). There it casts skill slot 5 (UberDiabSuperFire), counting stat 446 up to `aip5` (Hell:
  7, so six novas). Each cast *k* sets stat 331 (`passive_cold_mastery`) to (*k* + 1) × `aip6` (Hell: 25, so 50 up to 175).
- **Skeleton waves** at stat-447 phases 1, 3 and 5. They fire when life drops below Param4, Param5 and Param6 of skill slot
  6 (UberDiabSummon) in `skills.txt`: 85, 60 and 35, the wiki's numbers.
- **Immunity:** each tick it checks whether any of monsters 886-892 (Dclone's adds) are alive in the level, and calls the
  immunity toggle (`0x10380770`, section 5 intro). The boss is immune while any add lives, before his first phase (stat 447 = 0), and while the farthest
  player in his level is more than 0x17c away (squared subtiles); otherwise its resists are restored from `monstats`
  (its Normal columns). #470's port read this from the disassembly.
- **Trapped souls** (`0x1035bc60`, monsters 790-794) die when Dclone (`game+0x2600`) is dead or dying (mode 0 or 12,
  or life 0%). #472's port read the rest from the disassembly (Hell columns, whatever the difficulty):
  - A soul waits (idle `aidel`) while Dclone's life % is above its `aip4` + (tier − 1)×12 (souls 1-5: 100, 80, 40, 60,
    20) or while his nova count (stat 446) is not 0.
  - With its own stat 446 at 0 it casts skill 2 (UberDiabloBoulder) on its target and sets the stat to `aip5` (10);
    otherwise it counts it down and casts skill 1 (UberDiabloMeteor), skipped 1 in max(`aip6` − 5×tier + 5, 5) % of the time.
  - The meteor lands in the 50×50 square from (0x3b00, 0x197b) around the arena centre, or, for `aip8` 2 or 3 (souls 3
    and 5), at the target spread over 24 − 8×tier subtiles.
  - The delay after a cast: `aidel` + 10 at tier 0, else max(`aidel` − 4×(tier − 1), 20); the meteor's adds 0-7 − 4.
  - The same function's branch for monster 0x39a (nihlathakMap) runs mob waves (its `aip1` columns count the stages),
    then casts skill 2 (RathmaDeath) and kills itself; its branch for 0x421 in level 0xb6 is a third AI.
- **nihlathakMap** (`0x1035bc60` from `0x1035c43e`, #538). Its stage is `game+0x2628`, which the Shadow of Mendeln
  spawn sets to 1; at 0 it idles 25. With *a*, *b*, *c* the three `aip1` columns (20, 15, 10) and *i* = stage − 1:
  - Stage 1: once its target is within 14, stage 2 and cast skill 1 (NihlathakMapMobSpawn).
  - *i* < *a* + *b* + *c* + 1: a wave. Normal, champion and unique counts are `rand() %` the stage's row: `aip2`
    (*i* < *a* + 1; Normal column at most 2 gives 2, empty columns 0), `aip3` (*i* < *a* + *b* + 1; at most 1 gives 1,
    unique empty 0), else `aip4` (at most 1 gives 1); all 0 gives one normal. Each spawns 10 subtiles around it at a
    free spot (`0x10389c20`), normal (`0x1037cd00`), champion (`0x1037cbf0`) or unique with 3-6 minions
    (`0x1037caf0`). The monster is a random member of the set `0x105ddfe0` {−1, 923, 924, 926, 927} (zombie,
    charger, skeleton, archer NihlMinion), −1 meaning a random member of `0x105ddf74` {928-931} (the four mages);
    the baseline DLL holds the sets' constants at `0x10450760` / `0x10450770`. Then stage + 1, idle for `aip5`'s
    Normal column (Nightmare's past *a* + 1, Hell's past *a* + *b* + 1), and by its seed (`0x1036f320`) % 3: skill 3
    (MonCurseCast) on the target, skill 1 at its spot + 2, or nothing.
  - *i* = *a* + *b* + *c* + 1: wait 100; next think skill 2 (RathmaDeath), wait 25; then it dies quietly (`0x10356e00`).
### Rathma and Mendeln (`0x10358510`)

- They register as `game+0x2600` (Rathma, the bone clone) and `+0x2604` (Mendeln, the poison clone). Stage byte 0 -> 1 on
  the first tick.
- **Life thresholds** every 10% from 90% down to 20%, with stat 446 as the event index (read again for
  [#474](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/474)). Mendeln (rathmaPoison, not his clone) blinks to the
  stage's spot and casts slot 7 at 90, 70, 50 and 30; both poison bosses blink there and run a cast chain (slots 6, 3,
  then six of 2/5/1, then 4) at 80, 60, 40 and, from stage 5, 20. Rathma casts slot 7 at 80, 70, 50 and 30; his 90, 60
  and 40 only count. At 90, 70, 50, 30 and 15 the life is set back to that mark, so one hit never skips an event.
- **Retreat below 15%:** stage 1 -> 2 or 3 -> 4. A ghostly portal (object 585) opens at the boss, and an invisible object
  587 marks it. While the Rathma area is active, entering level 162 before stage 2 sets `game+0x2628` to 2, and entering
  163 before stage 4 sets it to 4 (section 9).
- **Death:** Rathma (`0x103767d0`) and Mendeln (`0x10376760`) each open their stage portal once, at (18387, 14667) and
  (18284, 13759).
- **Final pair:** when the first clone dies (stage 5 -> 6), `0x10376840` makes the surviving clone cast a skill through
  `0x1036d7d0`. That is PD2's general cast helper (nine callers, other AIs among them), so it is not a shared-life
  mechanic. It is RathmaDeath's buff: the helper puts the skill's auratargetstate (monfrenzy) and aurastats on the
  unit for auralencalc frames, and never runs its srvdo 169 (#474). From stage 6 the survivor's AI repeats it while it
  lacks state 103 (`monfrenzy`). When the second clone dies (6 -> 7),
  every void knight, golem and totem in the level is killed.
- **Shared life** (read again for [#475](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/475)): PD2's damage-type
  step (`0x10302ca0`, in place of 1.13c's `0x6fcfbd00`; D2Game's table of 12 types at `0x6fd22ab0`) runs after the
  resists. When a clone (935 or 936) takes one of the 9 flagged types (physical, fire, lightning, cold, magic, poison
  and the three leeches; table field 8), both boss slots are set, and the other clone is not in mode 0 or 12, the
  hit's damage of that type is halved (`0x1037c4c0` with 50 / 100: the double at `0x1044fc08` is 50.0). Unless the other
  clone has state 8, it loses that half from its life (stat 6, not below 0). So the wiki's "halved" is right: each
  clone takes half. Poison (stat 74 at -rate, `0x103055b0`) puts the same rate and length on the other clone through
  `0x10305460`, under the same slot and mode tests, without the state 8 one.
- Adds: each tick it checks whether void knights (968, 969, 1106, 1107) and the blood golem (938) are alive. That gates
  which skills are used.
### Lucion (`0x1035dca0`)

The `aip` columns are read as one int16 list *p*0-*p*23 (aip1, aip1(N), aip1(H), aip2, ...; 1.13c monstats `+0x56`),
whatever the difficulty, so each column is just one more number. The AI keeps three params: the next state, a counter,
and the state it just ran (*last*). Skills are monstats `Skill1-5`: LucionBlink, LucionNova, LucionBoneWave,
LucionPunish and MonCharge (the dash), each cast in its `SkNmode`. *aidel* is the difficulty's `aidel` minus the tier.

Each tick, before the state runs: the stage goes up by at most one (table above); the sub-step `game+0x262b` counts
down unless the state is 5; stat 446 counts down unless the state is 7 or 8. If the stage just became 3, the portal
phase runs and the next state is 4. In state 1, a player farther than √700 subtiles (or √500, 1 time in 5) makes him
blink at the target.

| State | What it does | Next |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | idle 40; stage at least 1 | 6 |
| 1 | immunity off; roll *r* < 100. *r* < *p*0: in melee range a swing (state kept); else, within 10 subtiles, 3 in 10 walk at the target and delay 15; else 9. *p*0 ≤ *r* < *p*1: 12. Else 7 if *last* ≠ 8, *r* < *p*2, stage ≥ 2 and stat 446 ≤ 0; else 4 (3 while the sub-step runs) if *last* ≠ 6, *r* < *p*3 and stage ≥ 3; else 3 (9 below stage 2 when *r* < *p*2). Idles *aidel* | as rolled |
| 2, 11 | idle *aidel* | 1 |
| 3 | attack in mode A2 | 1 |
| 4 | counter 0: the portal phase again (immune, mode 10, delay 25). Counter 1: state 146 (`invis`) with light radius −100 (`0x10380950`), `0x103a4c70`, sub-step 0, the level darkened for its players (packet 0x53, `0x1037dc70`) and sound 0xa78 (`0x1037f240`); delay *aidel* | 5, counter 6 + rand 6 |
| 5 | the frenzy, one step per tick while the counter lasts: 6 in 10 a swing (A1); else Punish at the target three times running (the sub-step 1-3), then a swing. Each swing uses up one count | 5, then 6 with the sub-step set to *p*6's low byte (Lucion: 50 ticks before the next frenzy) |
| 6 | counter 0: darkening off, sound 0x26d, idle. Counter 1: state 146 off, `0x103a4c90`, mode 11, delay 10. Then immunity off and idle | 6, 6, 1 |
| 7 | blink to the arena centre (0x6223, 0x17e1), delay 35 − 4×tier; then Nova at himself (the counter becomes 1 + rand 10000), delay 65 − 8×tier; then Nova again in mode 9 | 7, 7, 8 |
| 8 | idle; stat 446 = rand(2×(3 − tier)) − stage/2 + *p*7 (Lucion: 30) | 1 |
| 9 | Bone Wave at the target's spot | 1 |
| 10 | blink at the target, 0 or −1 subtile off on each axis | 1 |
| 12 | dash (MonCharge) to 3 subtiles past the target | 1 |
| > 12 | idle *aidel* | 1 |

| 4 | counter 0: the portal phase again (immune, mode 10, delay 25). Counter 1: state 146 (`invis`) with light radius −100 (`0x10380950`), `0x103a4c70`, sub-step 0, the level darkened for its players (packet 0x53, `0x1037dc70`) and sound 0xa78 (`0x1037f240`); delay *aidel* | 5, counter 6 + rand 6 |

records.excerpt: The install routine `0x1036ba20` writes srvdo 184 `0x103b5110`, 185 `0x103b52b0`, 186 `0x103b56d0` and srvst 76
`0x103b6aa0`. Missiles are made with flags 3 (`0x10311b20`) and sent to every client (`0x1037fe90`).

- **LucionNova (184)**, monsters only: srvmissileb when the caster's AI param 0 is 8 (the second Nova), else
  srvmissilea. A ring over D2's 64 directions (D2Game `0xfb870` / `0xfb770`) from the caster, starting at direction
  *s* & 63, where *s* = `0x10380670`(AI param 1), the cast-sequence step of `0x103805f0`. Before each missile, while
  fewer than 5 gaps were made and 8 missiles have been fired since the last gap, the next step *s* rolls *s* % 100 <
  15 (2 less per gap): then it skips 6 directions. Both Novas of state 7 share param 1, so they leave the same gaps.
- **LucionPunish (186)**: calc1 srvmissilea, with no target offset, at the skill's target + (cos *a*, sin *a*) × calc2,
  *a* = 2 × 3.2 × *i* / calc1 (the constant `0x1044fb98` is 3.2, not π). For Lucion (0x458), sub-step 2 doubles the
  count and adds 3 to the radius; sub-step 3 triples it and adds 6.
- **LucionDash (srvst 76, srvdo 185)**: the start picks a free spot at the target unit (else the skill's point), stores
  it and the distance in the unit skill, and sets flag 0x80. The do function is a leap with no attack. With 0x80 it
  sets 0x1101, collision off, path type 9 to the spot at a monster's monstats Run (1.13c `+0x34`) << 9 or a player's
  0xb00 + calc2 × 0x50, and a ring (`0x1036d250`) of calc1 srvmissilea. In flight (0x100) it lays srvmissilec at the
  caster (1.13c D2Game `0xa28f0`, flags 0x21). Within 2 subtiles of the spot it puts the collision back, ends the mode
  a frame later and makes a ring of calc2 srvmissileb.

## 7. Key drop rule (`0x103799d0`)

This runs for every monster death, after the drop chain. Each roll is `0x10375ee0(tc, mult, players)`: it takes the
odds-only TC row *tc* + difficulty and drops on `rand % (Unique × max(Set, 1)) < mult`. A Unique of 0 means no drop.
With more than one player (`game+0x90`, where values above 8 count as 1), Unique is scaled by
(127 − 2×(players − 1))/127. *mult* is 1, or 2 for monsters with stat 493 (`map_glob_skirmish_mode`).
## 8. Desecration (`0x103961b0`, roll `0x103729e0`)
- **Conditions:** the item passes a type check (`0x1030cc10`; the brick below is an amulet) and two flag checks. It must
removed (`0x1037ff80`).
- **Failure (the brick):** a new rare amulet (`amu`, item level 99) replaces the old one. `0x10375340` hands it over
rolls from `0x103649d0`:

- **`game+0x2628` in Rathma:** the tier scaling reads its low byte as the entry count, once per monster when it spawns.
  Portal entries into levels 161-163 add 1. On the normal path the group follows the retreat portal, so the stage is
  already 2 or 4 and the field keeps the entry count. Only someone entering 162 before stage 2, or 163 before stage 4,
  overwrites it with 2 or 4. That sets *e* to 1 or 3 for the monsters that spawn after, which can lower it as well as
  raise it. [UB5](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/230) checks it.

records.excerpt:
- **HD monsters and overlays: check first, inside the work item ([UR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/200)).** In HD, Hell, on a level 90+ character: summon
  a Dopplezon, visit the Countess, take a shrine, cast Battle Orders and a curse. If they are invisible, a generated
  `monsters.json` maps each PD2-only monster `Id` to the D2R model of a monster with the same `Code` (525), with a
  hand-picked list for the other 24; shared overlay rows keep D2R's `Character` folder; PD2's 33 new overlays get a
  copied D2R json as stand-in. Both get an approximated row. If nothing is invisible, [UR2](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/200) closes with no code.
- **The Ascendant is in the alpha ([UR3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/201)).** PD2's Act 4 hireling (ids 30-35, Dark and Light) and its second Rogue Scout
  set (ids 36-38) move to new hireling ids from 39, with `WType` (D2R's monstats arm item types, [#270](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/270)), the `hiredesc` strings and the `$2`
  monster's HD model. [UR3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/201) first proves ids 39+ load, hire and survive a save and load; if they don't, the Ascendant
  becomes a cut row.
- **PD2's voice and effect WAVs are converted, 27 of the 30 as FLAC (see docs/deviations.md for the other 3) ([UR8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/206))**, all in one item, after a one-file WAV-as-FLAC test under
  `data/hd/global/sfx`. The 16 drop sounds stay with the Pyre-Flies filter ([P7](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/44)).
- **Item art is scripted ([UR7](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/205)).** PD2's 219 item pictures are upscaled with [P11](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/79)'s pipeline (`.sprite` and
  `.lowend.sprite`, plus the `items.json`, `uniques.json` and `sets.json` entries); the row becomes approximated
  ("upscaled from classic art"). The shared skill icon sheet takes PD2's frames on cels 0-60, with D2R's HD frame kept
  where PD2's classic frame is D2R's ([P11](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/79)'s rule). Class icons, tree backgrounds and object graphics stay approximated.
  Missile stand-ins (P10) are final: an approximated row.
- **New core-rules rows.**
  - [UR4](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/202) reads skills `checkfunc`, `nocostinstate` and `general` in `ProjectDiablo.dll` first, then builds what play
    depends on. `checkfunc` folds into D2R's itype columns if every value matches what they allow; `general` is cut if
    only the UI reads it.
  - [UR5](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/203) finds D2R's own values for the uber and ultra code odds and `HireableBossDamagePercent` in Ghidra. A rule whose
    value equals PD2's is cut; the others are hooked. Both were cut: D2R's `MercenaryDamagePercentVSBoss` matches, and
    the code odds never act in PD2 (`docs/deviations.md`).
  - [UR6](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/204) rolls the quivers' `auto prefix` groups (321-326) with no hook: D2R loads misc, weapons and armor with one field
    list, so the merge adds the column to misc.txt and D2R's own automagic roll (`0x442d60`) reads it.
  - Folded into existing rows, with no item of their own: missile `Qty` and `SpecialSetup` and the throwing potions'
    `spelldesc` go to "Throwing potions" ([IR5](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/240)); missile `LevRange` goes to the class or map row that owns each missile.
    States `immed` is cut: PD2's loader never reads it ([#342](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/342), [states-immed](../research/skills/states-immed.md)).
- **Cut, in one docs item ([UR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/199)).** Columns that are empty in PD2 or set only on rows both games share: the skill event
  columns, `blue`, `itemspecific`, `Divide`, the S12/S13 save widths, the affix and rare price columns, itemtypes
  `Charm`, `Gem` and `CostFormula`, the qualityitems classic columns, and the empty or shared-only armor, misc,
  weapons, gems, sets, runes and uniqueitems columns. The tables `cubetype` and `treasureclass`, and `aiparms`,
  `arena`, `chartemplate`, `monname`, `uniquetitle`, `weaponclass` and `miniskillicons`. PD2's panel DC6. Belts and body
  locations close as matching.
  - `cubemain.ladder` is cut. PD2's D2Common loads it as vanilla 1.13c does (a byte at record offset 1); its values 2-4
    mark PD2's online recipe groups, and the merge leaves every recipe on, which is what single-player wants. Where
    PD2's D2Game reads it was not traced.
  - Two checks run inside [UR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/199): one D2R Ghidra lookup for the monster treasure-class drop percent (`monitempercent` is
    cut if it is 20, otherwise it gets a core-rules row), and a sane vendor price for one PD2-only armor subtype (the
    price columns are cut once it passes).
- **List fixes ([UR1](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/199)).** Gheed's event row names [MS8](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/222). The "other classes" row points at [W11](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/86)-[W35](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/125). Guild halls name the
  beta. New approximated rows: the missile stand-ins (P10), Buff HUD (buff timers, mini skill icons, the skill bar) and
  Item Roll Ranges (tooltip stat ranges).
- **Client UI.** The DPS counter is a new plugin built in `synpoox/d2r-tools` and pinned in
  `companions/manifest.json` ([UR9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/207)). The potion counter is a plugin built in `synpoox/d2r-tools` too, pinned in
  `companions/manifest.json` ([UR10](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/208), [#1464](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/pull/1464)).

Caveats: the SDK README describes SDK 0.4.0, while KB-loader reports loader 1.3.1-beta is older than the SDK, so some
service fields are missing (marked below). Local facts were observed on 93847 and not re-verified here. Only the SDK
front page was read, not its individual headers; per-header detail needs a source read before an implementation ticket
relies on it.

| Topic | Fact | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Toolchain | C++ DLL, Windows x64, CMake 3.29+, MSVC or clang-cl. Static CRT works | SDK, TPL |
| Minimum plugin | Embedded manifest resource (RCDATA id 1001 = ABI DWORD), exports `D2RLoaderGetPluginInfo`, `D2RLoaderLoadPlugin`, optional `D2RLoaderUnloadPlugin`. Without the resource the loader rejects the DLL as an "old alpha plugin" | SDK, KB-loader |
| Roles / flags | Exactly one of `Client`, `Server`, `Shared`; optional `ModScopedOnly`, `NativeHooks` (needed for inline hooks) | SDK |
| Where it loads | `<game>/mods/<mod>/d2rloader/plugins/` (mod-scoped, loaded first, replaces a same-id global copy) or `<game>/d2rloader/plugins/` (global, loads with every mod) | SDK, KB-loader |
| Which mod runs | `d2rloader.toml` `default_mod` (game-wide); a mod's own toml overrides `[d2rcore.*]` and `[d2rloader.plugins] load_order` (seen in Slot 5, #1180) | KB-loader |
| Config | One embedded default TOML (non-empty, <= 1 MiB); user config created once, never overwritten | SDK |
| Tables | The loader compiles the mod's `.txt` tables itself (no `-txt`); a shipped `.bin` becomes a "custom BIN set" that must be complete | KB-loader |
| First start | First start after install/update builds a compiler snapshot and loads only D2R's own sounds table; mod sounds resolve to -1 (silent, can crash). Needs a second start; guard via `DataTablesLoaded` | KB-loader |
| Packaging | `d2rl plugin pack` builds DLL + companion MPQ (`d2rloader/<plugin-id>/`) | SDK |
| Logs | `<game>\d2rloader\logs\d2rloader.log`; crashes in `<game>\d2rloader\crashes\`; plugin log in `mods\<Mod>\d2rloader\logs\` | KB-loader |
| Build specificity | Engine hooks use RVAs valid for one image. Template checks PE timestamp and hook entry bytes, turns parts off on mismatch. Check game major.minor, not build number | KB-loader, KB-addr, TPL |
| Debugging | Per-part off-switch file `<name>-off.txt`, status console command, guards (build, env, sound, item type ids) | TPL |
| Testing | Python harness: separate game "slots", locks, scripted launch, screenshots, keys, console lines, named checks with results JSON. Click/key/console control needs a plugin implementing the harness protocol | TEST |
| Reverse engineering | Ghidra workflow; each confirmed address recorded in `d2r.h` and the registry | KB-sys, KB-addr |

**Data** = table change only; **Limit** = hard limit or partial.

records.excerpt:
| Topic | Fact | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Local and TCP/IP games; the plugin network service is not available on Battle.net | SDK |
| Server-side rules | Spawns, drops, portals, skills run on the server side, even in single player. The client sees only what D2R syncs (units, stats, states, items) | KB-sys |
| Matching | `Shared` plugins must match host and client on id, version, ABI, scope and flags; bump version every release. Client-only plugins are not recorded | SDK, KB-sys |
| Config | Settings in `[d2rl] match` (<= 64 paths) must be equal; the embedded list is authoritative | SDK |
| Compatibility token | 64-bit token must match on both sides | SDK |
| Item changes | Only local games or the TCP/IP host change items; clients message the host (`getPeerPlayer`) | SDK |
| Messages | Private plugin messages, <= 224 bytes | SDK |
| Save history | Server and Shared plugins are recorded in the character's plugin history | SDK |
| Implication | Private TCP/IP multiplayer is workable if all gameplay hooks are `Shared` and versions match. State only the server plugin knows is invisible to clients unless it maps onto D2R's sync. Battle.net-style online play is out of scope | SDK, KB-sys |

- 30 class skills unless extended save format; 62 HD icons per class strip.
- Free slots: srvdo 172-190, cltdo 110-129, item spell 16-19, missile srvhit 61-70.
- Level ids <= 255 for portals; `Layer` < 100; 36 automap level types; portals within an act.
- 511 states assert (harmless), 1,024 wide states supported, beyond that unexplored.
- Set 6 items; runeword 7 properties; formula 255 chars.
- All RVAs are build 93847 only.
- On loader 1.3.1: panel text cannot change; item tooltip getters missing.

| manifest files | 1608 | 1613 |
| core-rules.dll | 5017fda9... | 158adeda... |

The candidate ships `core-rules`, `core-maps` and `core-ui` plus Cartographer; there is no separate core-events (the
retained map events live in core-maps). The 7z is not committed; the hashes above are from the rehearsal run, whose dll was
a build of a stale local merge commit (the load check on d2r-tools d78952d passed afterwards).

`tools/cartographer.pin` holds the oldest d2r-tools commit whose Cartographer may ship or install (d78d3bc1: knows all 25 tilesets; older builds skip 12 of them and those map items refuse to open). `tools/check_cartographer.ps1` enforces it for `install.ps1` and the `Package` step of `release.yml`. The DLL has no build stamp, so the check looks inside it for tileset names (`KurastSewer`, `Catacombs`, `Tombs`, `MazeTemple`, the last added at f4964090): they prove all 25 tilesets, not the exact commit; in the release it also checks `CARTOGRAPHER_COMMIT` descends from the pin when a `d2r-tools` checkout sits beside the toolkit. A refused DLL: `git -C <d2r-tools> pull`, `powershell tools\build.ps1 -Plugin cartographer`, then reinstall. Raise the pin when a Cartographer change is required.

## Root cause
A on the altar runs `openPanel` (`PanelManager:OpenPanel:<panel>`), which skips the controller UI switcher. D2R's switcher
(`UISwitcherPanel`, message handler `FUN_14027df80`, tab change `FUN_14027f2f0(switcher, tabIndex, dir)`) is what
sets pad focus: on a tab change it clears the old panel's focus (`FUN_140857c00`), opens the new panel by id
(`FUN_1400cd7c0`), then focuses it (`FUN_140858050(panel)` -> `FUN_1408682b0(focusManager, panel)`).
START sends `PanelManager:OpenPanel:UISwitcher` (`FUN_14011b490`); the switcher holds the tab panel ids at +0x168,
their count at +0x188 and the current index at +0x1b8. `FUN_140846170(name)` is `PanelManager::FetchPanel`; a panel's
active flag is at +0x51 (`FUN_1408682b0` asserts, an int3, on a null or inactive panel).

## Routes tried
1. **Open through the switcher** (START's message, then `FUN_14027f2f0` to the altar tab): not tried in game. Needs the
   switcher object (`FetchPanel("UISwitcher")`) and the altar tab's index in its list at +0x168, and the altar's tab id is
   assigned by the loader at route registration (not found yet). This is the next step.
2. **Focus the already open panel** (plugin, UI thread, frame callback): after `openPanel`, call
   `FetchPanel("core-maps/SacrificeAltar")` and, once +0x51 is set, `FUN_140858050(panel)`. Slot 3, level 99 Assassin,
   town, `cheat ospawn 621` altar, pad A: log `altar: pad focus set, 0 frames after the open` (no crash), but D-pad DOWN
   did nothing (a character walked in the world behind it; no confirm-button highlight), and there is no help bar.
   Via the route (START, LB to the altar tab) the same DOWN highlights the confirm button and the help bar shows.
   The focus manager takes the call, but the world open still leaves the pad in world input. Code not kept.
3. **Layout only** (`defaultWidget`, `navigation`): not a fix. The layout is the same for both opens; the route open
   focuses and the world open does not, so the difference is outside the layout.
4. `WidgetService::focusWidget`: crashes on the installed loader (given); not used.

5. **Copy what the stash world open does** (lane 1456b, 2026-11-18, slot 5). Stash path: Bank object OperateFn 32 ->
   `0x528270` -> `FUN_140480650(client, 0x10)` sends packet 0x77 -> the client opens UI 0x10 -> the BankPanel open
   handler `FUN_14023cc40`. In pad mode (`FUN_140077e10`) that handler resets the input state (`FUN_14008d540`),
   fetches the existing ControllerOverlay panel and, only if it is attached, refreshes it (`0x1f6e50(ov, int ov+0x438)`,
   `0x1f5d60(ov)`, `0x1f5a80(ov, 0x18)`, `0x1f5a80(ov, 1)`), then focuses the panel (`FUN_140858050`). Route 2 did only
   the last. `altar_panel.cpp` now does the same one frame after the altar and the inventory beside it are both active
   (panel +0x51), clearing the inventory's focus first (`0x857c00`, as the switcher does), by byte signature; each
   signature matches once in the 93847 dump. It logs the focus manager's +0x198 (`FUN_140846020()`) a few frames later
   against the altar panel.
   Result of the first version (it dispatched `OpenPanel:ControllerOverlay` and focused straight after the open): the pad
   frame and help bar showed and the D-pad drove the panel, but the first DOWN gave "Hold to Sort" (a grid focus), not the
   confirm button; LEFT then lit it. Cause guessed: the inventory opens after the focus and takes it.
   Second version (slot 3, 2026-11-18): the altar and the inventory are waited for, the inventory's focus is cleared, the
   overlay is only refreshed when attached, never opened. The focus manager's +0x198 held the altar panel three frames
   after the focus (log "same"), yet the pad frame and help bar did not show (the overlay was not up), DOWN highlighted
   nothing, and B did not close the panel. The stash's decompile (0x23cc40) does build an OpenPanel message for
   "ControllerOverlay" in pad mode, so the code now opens it when it is not up and refreshes it otherwise; that variant is

## The fix (lane 1456c, slot 4, 2026-11-18)

1. **No pad frame.** `FUN_1401f60c0` is the ControllerOverlayPanel type descriptor, not an "attached" test: the stash's loop over
   `vtable+0x58` is a type check, so the stash always refreshes the overlay it just asked for. v2 and v3 refreshed only when
   the overlay's +0x51 was set, which it was not yet. The frame is the overlay's `Background` widget, set to the two-panel frame
   by `0x1f6e50(ov, ov+0x438)`.
2. **DOWN going to the inventory.** The focus manager (`FUN_140846020()`) keeps the focused panel at +0x188, its widget at +0x190
   and the last panel at +0x198; its input handler `FUN_140866eb0` sends a D-pad direction to the +0x190 widget's
   `vtable+0x68`. With no widget there it moves to a neighbouring panel (`FUN_140868470`), which is the inventory. `0x8682b0`
   takes the panel's remembered widget (+0x160) or the first focusable one (`FUN_140857d70`). Focusing once the overlay is up
   gives the amulet slot (log `widget` non-null), and DOWN then follows the layout's `navigation.down` to `confirm`. The
   remembered widget is cleared before each focus so every open starts on the slot.
3. **B doing nothing.** D2R's panels close themselves on controller action 0x17 ("back") in their own OnMessage: BankPanel
   `FUN_14023caa0` (`*(int*)(msg[0x22]+0x10) == 0x17` -> `FUN_1400c7d30(0x18)`), UISwitcher `FUN_14027df80`. The message is
   InputMessage (field 0 hash `0x4ae067c6248b6042`) with ControllerActionBegin (field 0x11 hash `0x1e439768f7dd4594`). The SDK
   panel is a plain Panel whose OnMessage (Widget's, `FUN_140856b00`) only passes messages to its children. The SDK has no pad
   input service, so the altar panel object alone gets a copy of its vtable (17 methods) with OnMessage (slot 4) wrapped: on
   back in pad mode it closes the altar, the inventory and the overlay on the next frame. No game code is patched.

D2RLoader listed `Controller QOL Updates 1.3.1+rev.100 by PyreFly [global]` between Pyre Stash Search and Cartographer,
and `16 plugins loaded; 2 plugins failed` (the two failures are the mod's Item Durability and MassID, which failed

`Plugin safety-check patch failed at RVA 0xFABE0: game bytes did not match what the plugin expected`. It is a probe
of the loot dispatch for another plugin's (UnHoarder) hook; the next lines admit the profile
(`[QOL/ClientLoot] Native loot approach profile admitted.`) and pickup worked, so it is log noise, not a failure.

**Hook order with the harness pad.** On this core Controller QoL installs no XInput hook at all: it takes the game's
normalized input through two SDK inline hooks (game `+0x13EDD0`, `+0x13DEF0`) and reads the right stick through the
game's own axis getter. The harness pad replaces the XInput pointers the game holds (import-table swap) and answers
from its state file without calling the real export. So the order is: game, harness pad (XInput), game's input
layer, Controller QoL. The two never touch the same bytes; the export trampoline (`48 89 5C 24 08` prologue patch,
ordinal 100) is only Controller QoL's fallback on cores it does not admit. Evidence: the left stick moved the
character; START, B, LS, LT/RT, LB/RB and LB+face buttons drove Controller QoL's features (below); the right stick
moved its cyan aim cursor (held at -0.8, -0.6 it went to the lower left of the screen). `qol status` logged
`mode=native ... nativeHook=1 ... controllerEvents=2 ... faults=0`. If a later core falls back to its XInput
trampoline, the pad's state would not reach it (the pad answers before the export runs); see the risks.

  `layouts/controller/core-maps/SacrificeAltarhd.json`, and `plugin/core-events/controller_panel.{h,cpp}` with
  `FocusPanelWidgetSoon(context, threads, widgets, panelName, widgetName)`: on the UI thread, once the panel is laid
  out, it focuses a named widget through the SDK `WidgetService` (`findPanel`, `findWidget`, `focusWidget`),
  retrying for up to 300 ticks. `altar_panel.cpp` calls it after the panel opens. The helper is generic (any plugin
  panel, SDK only); the call and the layout are mod-specific.

- **Mod-specific, stays in the mod:** the controller layouts and art for the mod's grids and panels (#1440, #1441, the
  Cube, #1444's `defaultWidget`), and the stack split rule itself (core-ui, ADR 0004). d2r-tools can't hold them: its
  plugins are global and never rely on a mod shipping layouts (d2r-tools `AGENTS.md`, "Working").
- **Generic:** reading "is a pad modifier or chord held" (for #1442, and any later pad shortcut), and "focus this
  widget once this plugin panel opens" (`FocusPanelWidgetSoon`). Neither needs a hook: the first can use the game's
  controller state as Controller QoL does, or XInput; the second is SDK-only.
- **Not ours to rebuild:** aim and snap targeting, ground loot, item shortcuts, belt fill, tab paging. Controller QoL
  has them, global and maintained.

  A global pad plugin of ours would also hook the same input Controller QoL owns, and the SDK has no gamepad state
  service to share it (`input.h` is keyboard only). Revisit only if a pad feature for any mod comes up that Controller
  QoL lacks.
- **A shared library: the toolkit's `shared/plugin-common`.** That is where vendored-in helpers already live
  (pd2-resurrected links it in `plugin/CMakeLists.txt`). d2r-tools forbids code shared across its plugins, so a header
  there would not be reusable. Move `FocusPanelWidgetSoon` there as `panel_focus.{h,cpp}` once a second project needs
  it (plugin-common's own rule: "A value or helper only one project uses stays in that project until a second project
  needs the same code"); until then it stays in pd2-resurrected, in `plugin/common/` so core-ui and core-events can
  both use it.
- **Stays in the mod:** all layouts and art, and each panel's call into the helper. A mod panel gets controller
  support from the shared piece through a small adapter in the plugin that owns the panel: a controller layout (the
  data-driven focus map: `navigation` and `defaultWidget` in `layouts/controller/`) plus one
  `FocusPanelWidgetSoon` call when it opens, and B to close through the panel's own route. No API of a global plugin is
  needed.
