PD2's roll `0x10304710 (weapon, unit, x)` (disassembled):
1. Crit = the weapon mastery's crit (`0x103065d0 (unit, weapon, x, 2)`, only with a weapon) + `passive_critical_strike`

PD2's multiplier `0x103047f0 (unit, damage, x)`: on 1, physical (1.13c damage `+8`) times 200 + `item_crit_multiplier`
(256, D2Common #10910: layer 0) + its per-hand sum percent; on 2, 150 + `item_ds_multiplier` (257) + its per-hand sum.
Result flag `0x2000`; `0x1037c4c0` does `phys * mult / max(100, 1)` in doubles, saturated at `0x7fffffff`.

The per-hand sum `0x10381720 (unit, stat)` ([w35](../skills/w35-melee-splash-extras.md)) adds the stat's item-type layers that
the wielded weapon (#10061) is of, layer 0 left out: Javelin and Spear Mastery puts `item_crit_multiplier` on `spea`,
Two Hand Mastery `item_crushingblow` and `item_crushingblow_efficiency` on `2han`. 2han (PD2 row 114) counts only when
the other hand (#11139 at the other of bodylocs 4 and 5) is empty or the same item; 1han (116) only when it is not the
same item, or, for a dual-wield class (#10747), a 2han weapon beside another item.

Missiles. `0x103047f0`'s only live caller is `0x10303160`, from PD2's damage builder `0x103022b0`. The missile hit
`0x103045a0` (re-rolls on the owner at the hit, for a skill with SrcDam or Twister, Shock Wave, Tornado) and the gated
missile roll `0x103046a0` have no caller, no pointer in the image and no pointer table entry: dead code. The live
missile fill `0x102fe730` (its copy of D2Common's, in a hook table at `0x104a06f4`) rolls `0x10304710` on the owner
(the first call with no weapon) and sets missile flag 2, which 1.13c's hit doubles. So PD2's missile crit or deadly
strike is 2x, with no multiplier stats.
Sacrifice: PD2's srvdo 64 (`0x103aff30`, from the table fill `0x1036ba20`) runs 1.13c's hit through a resolved pointer
(`0x103a1b60` -> `[0x105e06b8]`) and its own self-damage block (flag `0x1000`); no PD2 strike code is on the path, so

- `WeaponDamage` (`0x44c030`): after the physical roll (stored at damage `+0x18`), the mastery crit (`0x33d4f0 (unit,
  weapon, 0, 2)`, only when its a5 is 0), `passive_critical_strike`, then `item_deadlystrike`; any success doubles
  `+0x18` and sets result `0x2000`. The block is `0x44c2b4`-`0x44c3d9`; attacker in RSI, damage in RDI, a5 in R14D.
  Its tail changes physical again (the `+0x149` element conversion, `DamageStep`), so a wrapper cannot redo the roll
  after it returns.
- `0x3ba820 (unit, weapon) -> bool`, the missile roll (callers: D2Common's missile fill `0x3bf9b0`, the server's
  `0x432f90` / `0x4333f0`): the same three rolls. The hit then doubles a missile's physical part when it carries the
  roll (`0x465420`, `0x465d60`).
to `WeaponStrike (attacker, damage, a5)` and a jump to `0x44c3d9`: PD2's roll and multiplier. The volatile
registers the block left are set again after `0x44c3d9`; R15D (0) is callee-saved.
- Hooks `0x3ba820` with PD2's roll. A missile's hit doubles (D2R's), as PD2's live code does.

`item_dmgpercent_pereth` and `item_dmgpercent_permissinghppercent` are op 4 on `equipped_eth` and `missing_hp`, which
nothing sets. PD2's stat evaluator `0x102faa90` (its copy of D2Common's) reads an op base on the owner through
`0x102fa640 (statlist, stat << 16, record)`:

- `equipped_eth`: the owner's (player or monster) worn items (`0x10382bd0`: bodyloc not 0, 11 or 12) that are ethereal
  (D2Common #10225).
- `missing_hp`: `(1 - life / maxlife) * 100` (stats 6 and 7), 0 without max life.
- `inc_splash_radius` (478): + `missing_hp` * `inc_splash_radius_permissinghp` (489), at most 40, when both are above 0.
  Only an op base reaches it, and no stat has `inc_splash_radius` as its op base, so PD2 never applies Nightmare's
  Feast's splash per missing life. Nothing to port.
- any other stat: D2Common's read (`0x103a27e0`).
PD2 also hooks an item stat-change callback (`0x102fa930`) that sets `item_dmgpercent_pereth` again on each worn item

D2R reads an op base through `0x2f9b10 (statlist, stat << 16 | layer, record)` (from `0x2f8ad0` and `0x2fa430`; the
statlist's unit at `+0xa0`). D2RCore replaces D2R's stat getters (`0x2f5020` is `jmp [0x3e2a218]`), so that read is
never called: a hook on it logged 0 calls ([#446](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/446)). D2RCore's
op 4 reads the real base stat (`cheat stat equipped_eth,2` gave Purgatory +120%). So core-rules keeps both as base
stats: `equipped_eth` (the unit's bodylocs 1-10, `0x3886d0`, holding an ethereal item, `0x3740a0`) is recounted at the
next game update after a durability callback (the item being taken off is still in its slot during it), `missing_hp`
on each life or max-life callback. The server never sends them, so a player's values are also set on its client unit.

D2R keeps each op's result in a stat list's full stats: `0x2fa430` recomputes a stat and walks the stats its record
lists as op targets (`+0x54`) only when a stat of that list changes. A new op base on the owner leaves a worn item's
op value as it was at equip time ([#320](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/320)), and PD2's own
refresh `0x102fa930` looks like a send of the item's stat to the client (a D2Game call given PlayerData `+0x9c`): PD2
evaluates ops on read (`0x102faa90`). So after each count change core-rules sets `item_dmgpercent_pereth` (or
`..._permissinghppercent`) one higher and back on the base list of each worn item that holds it;
D2R then recomputes `item_maxdamage_percent` / `item_mindamage_percent` with the new base. Seen (Slot 2): the player's
`item_maxdamage_percent` 0 -> 60 -> 120 -> 60. An op stat set on the player's own list (`cheat stat`) adds nothing to
`item_maxdamage_percent`, at any base: test these stats on an item.
PD2 replaces D2Game's add-life (1.13c `0x6fcfb570`, its calls at `0xdbb80` in the leech and `0xde23e`) with
`0x10306ca0 (unit, amount)`: life + amount up to the max, unless dead or in state 92, set through `0x102fbc50`. With
D2R's add-life is `0x451820 (unit, amount)`, called by the leech `0x450c90` (the attacker) and the hit's absorb heal in
`0x44ce80` (the victim). core-rules hooks it with PD2's test.
PD2's event 16 (`0x103469a0`), disassembled; constants from the DLL:

- Divisor: 10 on a player; on a monster, 10 for a hireling (D2Common #11104: class 271, 338, 359, 560, 561), else 8,
  except a prime evil (monstats flag `0x80`, #10278): 30 when in PD2's boss sets (`0x10371290`, filled at run time),
  else `(100 - life %) * 10 + 70` (#11027). A non-hireling monster then adds `0xaf5f0(monster_playercount) / 50`
  (D2Game's table, 0 for 1 player and +1 for each player after it, 2 less from 9). Other units: 8. Missile (event 6):
  times 2 on levels 157, 159 and 166 (PD2 levels, not in the merged data), else times 1.5.
- Blow = life / (divisor / (efficiency / 100 + effectiveness)); efficiency = `item_crushingblow_efficiency` + its
  per-hand sum; effectiveness 1, or 1 + calc4 / 100 when the unit's current skill (`0x1030dd00`) is Smite (97),
  calc4 evaluated at the unit skill's `+0x28` (hard points). The chance adds the per-hand sum of `item_crushingblow`
  (136). Less `damageresist` (36) percent (`0x1037c4c0`), nothing at 100 or more. Life set to life - blow (at
  least 0), kill flag (`damage + 4 |= 2`) at 0, overlay `0x93` (147), PD2's damage meter.
D2R's event 16 (`0x583150`) rolls and calls `0x581bd0 (game, unit, target, {damage, 4, 10, 10, missile})`, whose
entry is `jmp [0x3e2a448]`. core-rules writes `CrushingBlow` into that qword: PD2's blow for every caller (D2R's

PD2's event 15 (`0x103463f0`, thiscall: game in ECX, then attacker, target, a dummy and the node's `stat << 16 |
layer`), disassembled; constants from the Ghidra copy of the DLL (the DLL now on disk has moved them by 8 bytes):

1. Chance: the node's stat on the attacker (`item_openwounds` 135, or `map_mon_openwounds` 407, the only two with
   func 15), `rand % 100 <` it (`0x1036f320`, the attacker's seed).
2. Level part: 1.13c D2Game `0xac940 ({9, 18, 27, 36, 45}, level)` + 40, the level at least 1: `9l + 31` up to 15,
   then slopes 18, 27, 36, 45 from 16, 31, 46 and 61 (D2R's `0x584170` has the same table).
3. `deep_wounds` (501) on the attacker. On a **player** target both parts are cut: the level part to 8 / 6 / 4% by
   difficulty (game `+0x6d`; doubles `0x1044fbc0`, `fbb8`, `fba8`), `deep_wounds` to the same, halved again when the
   attacker is a Blood Golem (class 290), and the part held by the Barbarian's Deep Wounds passive list (state 225 on the
   attacker, D2Common #10871) a third of that (`0x1044fb90` = 3).
4. Damage = level part + 5 x deep. Resist: `damageresist` (36) on the target less the attacker's `passive_phys_pierce`
   (425); 100 or more ignores the pierce; a negative result counts half (to zero). A player takes `x50%` above 50 resist,
   any other unit `x(100 - r)%`. All cuts are `0x1037c4c0` (`a * x / 100` in doubles, truncated).
5. On a player in PD2's levels 157, 159, 166 inside a region (`0x1037c7b0`, `0x1037d470`): no damage. On a monster whose
   owner, or owner's owner, is a player (`0x103749f0 (unit, 1)`): a quarter.
6. Rathma's clones (classes 935, 936, with both boss slots `game +0x2600 / +0x2604` set): the damage is halved and the
   other clone, unless it has `resistall` (state 8), gets the same half as its own list.
7. The list: `0x102fc880 (target, 62, attacker)` finds the target's open wounds list from this attacker. With fewer than
   3 `openwounds_stack` (189) the old `hpregen` (74, negative) is added to the damage and set on it, and the stack goes
   up; at 3 nothing changes. Then PD2's `0x1036d7d0` request (skill 0, level 1, 125 frames, `hpregen` = -damage,
   state 62): an older list of the same skill and level only gets its timer moved, so the stat is set only on a new list.
   `openwounds_stack` is set on the result. A player attacker also adds the damage to PD2's damage meter (PlayerData
   `+0x1a8`).

The port (`OpenWounds`, `item_rules.cpp`): the crushing blow dispatch wrap also hides the func-15 nodes from D2RCore's
event copy and runs PD2's event once per hidden node after the dispatch, through D2R's `NewStateList` (its request has
the same stat and value fields; D2R's own event 15 passes `hpregen` there). A splash item event hits more units inside
the outer dispatch, where the nodes are hidden: those hits find the outer call's hidden nodes (a thread-local event) and
roll too, as in PD2. Approximated: D2R keeps one open wounds list per target (`UnitStateList`), so all attackers share
its stacks, where PD2 keys it by attacker. Not ported: the PD2-only levels, Rathma's clone split (core-maps'
`rathma_life.cpp` owns the pair) and the damage meter.

- Critical and deadly strike, Attack (srvdo 1): `item_crit_chance` 30, `item_crit_multiplier` 50,
  `item_deadlystrike` 90, `item_maxdeadlystrike` 10, `item_ds_multiplier` 25. Rolls under 30 crit at x250%;
  otherwise deadly strike, capped at 85, at x175%; a crit skips the deadly strike roll. Monster hits run through it
  with chance 0. Sacrifice (srvdo 64) builds its hit with damage flag 1, which skips WeaponDamage's roll block, so
  neither D2R nor core-rules rolls a strike on it.
- Life steal cap, `lifedrainmindam` 30 and `lifedrain_percentcap` 25: the hook runs on each of the player's steals,
  and at full life (god mode) all 50 were blocked. A steal added below 75% life was not seen.
- Crushing blow: with Goblin Toe (25%) and `item_crushingblow` 40, no blow was logged on the player's Attack hits.
  `cheat stat` adds no item event listener, and the boots' durability icon showed red, so this does not yet show
  whether D2R's event 16 runs on a player's hit. Cause ([#446](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/446)):
  D2RCore's event dispatcher (`0x5881e0` = `jmp [0x3e2a420]`) runs the item event nodes (unit `+0xe0`) through its
  own event copy and applies D2R's quarter-life blow silently. core-rules wrapped that slot (since [#385](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/385) it relays the two calls in HitEvents `0x44ce80` that raise events 5 and 6, `0x44cfc5` and `0x44cfe4`, to a wrapper around `0x44d570`, and leaves the slot to Cast Triggers), hides the crushing-blow nodes
  on events 5 and 6 and rolls the chance itself. Slot 11, Hell, The Cranium Basher (75%): rolls at chance 75, blows at
  divisor 8 less 7% resist (life 1557248 -> 1376217), life unchanged inside D2RCore's dispatch.
- Enhanced damage per ethereal item ([#446](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/446), Slot 11, Hell):
  Purgatory's tooltip read +0%, +60% with an ethereal helm worn, +0% after taking it off. Damage not measured.
- Smite's effectiveness ([#321](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/321), Slot 8, Hell, level 90 Paladin, Smite 20, zombies): each Smite blow
  logged effectiveness 1.41 (calc4 41); life 1422848 -> 1297459 at divisor 8 and resist 50, PD2's formula.
- Open wounds: a probe on `0x584170` logged nothing with `item_openwounds` 50 (stat only, no listener).
- Open wounds, ported (Slot 6, Hell, level 90 Paladin and level 95 Assassin, The Gnasher: 50%, `deep_wounds` 2):
  level part 2731 at 90 and 2956 at 95, + 10 deep, halved by a zombie's 50 resist: 1370 and 1483 /256 per frame;
  Andariel (resist 66) 1008. Stacks on one zombie (`cheat mongod 1`): 1483, 2966, 4449 at stacks 1-3, then 4449 stays
  at stack 3 on later procs; a proc 7.6 s after the last starts at stack 1 again (125 frames). Splash hits roll it too.
- Spawn commands: `cheat uniques` rows past the "Expansion" separator row are one lower than the merged table's
  (Fleshripper 304, The Gladiator's Bane 250); Attack is the bottom-left icon of the left skill picker.

Ghidra 12.2 headless, read-only, with throwaway scripts kept outside the repo: an immediate search for the PD2 stat
ids in `ProjectDiablo.dll` (`curse_slots` 190, `max_curses` 368, `curse_effectiveness` 504), decompiles and
disassembly of the hits, PD2's patch table for the 1.13c call sites it redirects, and the D2R 93847 dump for the
functions core-rules hooks. Ids below are PD2's; core-rules uses the merged ids (374, 421, 557,
`merge/ids-itemstatcost.tsv`).

PD2 replaces 1.13c D2Game's state list creator (seven call sites, `+0x3acf9` ... `+0x9a22d` in its patch table, the
necromancer curse function among them) with `0x1036d7d0`. It takes the same request D2R's `NewStateList` takes
(caster, target, skill, level, frames, stat, value, state, callback).
[#265](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/265). In `0x1036d7d0`, state 196 skips the curse gate (stat 109 and curse resistance). After the slot walk

D2R's `NewStateList` (`0x433d20`) starts with `jmp [rip+x]`: D2RCore hooks it, so core-rules cannot. The curse srvdo
(slot 30, `0x55c840`, every player curse, Dark Pact included) hands D2R's necromancer curse function `0x55a7e0`
(`SkillNec.cpp`, `(target, &CurseParams)`) to its area walk, once per target; `0x5598f0` and `0x568ad0` call it too.
Its entry is D2R's own. core-rules hooks it (`item_rules.cpp`):

- before: PD2's slot walk on the target's first chain of stat lists (unit `+0x88`, chain `+0x90`, flags `+0x1c`, next
  `+0x68`). `NewStateList` removes the first curse-flagged list it finds, so every curse list that must stay loses its
  curse flag while `0x55a7e0` runs: all of them while a slot is free, all but the oldest when full, all but this state's
  own when the target has it;
- after: the flags come back; a new list gets `curse_slots`; each stat `0x55a7e0` set is set again, resisted. The
  value comes from D2R's own per-stat helper `0x55bfb0` (a fifth of a resist cut on an immune monster), so the order is
  PD2's: the immunity cut, then resistance. aurastat1 is resisted only on a new list, as PD2 does it before the
  refresh check.

PD2's gate ([#264](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/264)), before the slot walk: a curse whose aurastat1 resists to 0 (the cap above) is cancelled;
stat 109 cuts the frames to `frames * (100 - r) / 100`, r at most 75 on a player, and 0 frames cancel it. D2R's
NewStateList, for a curse state, refuses at stat 109 >= 100, otherwise takes `frames * r / 100` off uncapped
(`0x433f32`), then refuses a unit with attract (state 57, `0x433fc8`). Its entry is D2RCore's, so core-rules runs
`0x55a7e0` with the target's stat 109 cleared on its base layer (`SetUnitStat` to `base - r`) and the PD2 frames in
CurseParams, and with the attract bit off (the state bits at stat owner `+0xaf0` that `0x2f6220` reads; `SetUnitState` writes a second array, so it does not do); both come back after the call, the bit only while the
attract list is still there.

Ghidra 12.2 headless, read-only: PD2's cube walk (`0x366f40`), found from op 30's research
([pd2-map-system-dll.md](../../pd2/map-system-dll.md), section 3), and its callees; the `HOTKEY_ItemQuantity` string's one
code use. On the D2R 93847 dump: the cubemain output parser (`0x3e5e60`, from the string `usetype`), the executor
(`0x5269c0`) and the `uniques` cheat (table entry at `0x238b600`, handler `0x411340`).
**The cube walk (`0x366f40`, player, cube owner).** It collects the candidate rows (`0x365fe0`), then tries each in
order with the input matcher (`0x364e30`). On the first match: op 30 stops (nothing made), op 31 calls the reroll
(`0x3669b0`), any other op runs the row (`0x3653d0`). After a row has run, the row's `ladder` byte (record +1) decides

- `2` (a corruption roll row): if `0x364960` holds (the cube has no Worldstone Shard, `wss` or `cwss`, still carrying
  stat 360), the walk resets the player's +0x25fc frame stamp and runs again: the outcome row fires in the same press.
- `3` (a "destroyed" outcome): each item in the cube that fails `0x10309c60(item, 0x68)`, carried the `0x1030cc40`
  flag before the row and has neither stat 360 nor that flag now gets `0x1030cca0`. Which flag that is was not traced
  (op 31 reads it as a choice between two item-make modes); [P9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/56)'s merged rows already mark these items.
- Outcome rows (`ladder` 1 and 3) are only candidates while `0x364960` holds.
`maxstack` is deleted, except arrows and bolts (`aqv`, `cqv`). `0x365b50` limits presses to one per 10 frames.
**Op 31, the reroll (`0x3669b0`, `CubeFunctions.cpp`).** For each item in the cube:
- a unique (quality 7) or set (5) item: a new item of the same row is made (`0x103841d0` / `0x103840c0`, the row and
item level from the old item, a new `rand()` seed, mode 4 or 2 by the `0x1030cc40` flag). The new item takes the old one's base code (it
**`HOTKEY_ItemQuantity`.** Its one code use is the key's handler at `0x102bc140`: in game, it switches D2Client UI
state 6 on or off (through the resolved D2Client functions at `0x105e32a4` and `0x105e32b4`); otherwise it prints the

- The cubemain output parser (`0x3e5e60`) knows `qty`, `pre`, `suf`, `nor`, `hiq`, `mag`, `set`, `rar`, `uni`, `crf`,
  `tmp`, `eth`, `sock`, `mod`, `uns`, `rem`, `reg` (flag 0x40, keeps quality), `exc`, `eli`, `rep`, `rch`, `lvl`.
  `reg` is the remake (below).
- The `uniques` cheat (`0x411340`) makes an item through `0x43cd50(game, &params, 0)`: a 0xb8-byte block with the
  player (+0), the game (+0x10), the item level (+0x18), the item id (+0x20), the room (+0x30), the quality (+0x40, 7)
  and the unique row (+0x50, zero-based), two seeds (+0x58, +0x5c). It drops the item on the ground.
- The `uniques` cheat path is not the cube's: in the executor (`0x5269c0`, at `0x52748e`) a `usetype` output with
  `reg` (flag 0x40) takes the input's quality (`0x36cf60`), unique or set row plus 1 (`0x36ce70`, into +0x50) and item
  level (`0x36ccf0`). The unique (`0x443910`) and expansion set (`0x58c2f0`) makers honour that 1-based row when the
  base code matches. The unique maker skips rows already made this game (bits at game +0x3638); PD2's op 31 maker
  (`0x103841d0`) clears that bit for the remake and restores it after (`0x1037ff00` / `0x1037ff30`, game +0x1b24).

Confirmed in the 1.13c `D2Game.dll` on disk: `+0x13033` is `4d dec ebp`, in the branch after `+0x12fd8` (an item whose
durability would reach 0, `dec ebp; jle +0x12fd8` at `+0x12f6f`). It reads stat 70 (`+0x13021`), and when it is above 1
(`cmp ebp,1; jle +0x130b4`) the `dec ebp` is followed by `SetStat(70, ebp)` (`+0x13038`) and
`SetStat(72, GetMaxDurability)` (`+0x13065`-`+0x13073`). At quantity 1 the `jle` goes to `+0x130b4`, which zeroes both
stats and removes the item. So the NOP keeps the stack and refills durability; a stack of 1 is still used up.

# Spike: PD2 Split Throw in a free srvdofunc slot
Throwaway. Answers "Spike a PD2 skill function in a free srvdofunc slot"; kept on tag `archive/research/split-throw`; folded here as a note.

- `plugin/`: the toolkit plugin template, plus `SrvDoSplitThrow` in srvdofunc slot 189 (PD2's own number for Split Throw).
  It's installed into `SrvDoTable` (RVA `0x238ea00`) with `PatchWriteU64`, using 8 zero bytes as the expected value.
- `mod/`: a modkit mod. Its patch turns vanilla Double Throw (id 140) into a stand-in. The patch sets srvdofunc 189, PD2's calc1 `par1+(min(lvl/5,par2))` (Param1=3, Param2=4), srvmissilea `throwaxe`, and cltdofunc 0.
- `pd2-spike.log`: the plugin log from the test run on build 93847.

- The slot installs cleanly: `skills 2/2 installed: srvdofunc 172 missile fan; srvdofunc 189 split throw (spike)`.
- Casting at level 10 runs the function server side. It logs `5 of 5 missiles (row 35), spread 30`, which is PD2's count (3 + min(10/5, 4) = 5).
- The missiles are not drawn on the client, even with `ClientSend=1` on throwaxe. The function and table side work, but what a player sees needs a client do function. PD2 pairs 189 with cltdofunc 118, and D2R's cltdofunc table is at RVA `0x235f7d0` (130 slots, 110-129 free, dispatcher `0x216d20`). The template has no example for this table yet.

| Progressive Affixes | yes, no shared hook | rare affix minimum, rare jewels always 4 | the 4/5/6 split above the minimum is a guess until IR8 reads PD2's roll |
| Mass Identify | yes, no shared hook | shift-click identify with a Tome of Identify | not the Almanac (it only takes `ibk`) |
| Vendor Stock Refresh | yes, no shared hook | nothing | not needed: D2R already has the gamble refresh button |

- **The gamble refresh button is D2R's own.** D2R's vendor panel has `button_refresh` (`PANEL\Vendors\Gambling_Refresh_Button`,
  `VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll`) in `global/ui/layouts/controller/vendorpanellayouthd.json`, and Vendor Stock Refresh
  says "Gambling keeps its original refresh behavior". So it is not a deviation, and the "cut" row added in #191 should go.
- **PD2's ethereal bonus is 25%, not D2R's 50%.** No plugin covers it, and core-rules has no row for it (below).
- **PD2's weapons lose durability at half the rate** (wiki). Item Durability's resistance applies to every normal item,
  armor included, so it can only approximate this. It needs a row.

records.excerpt: **`0x43acb0` is a hard clash.** Before it hooks a site, Cast Triggers checks that the site's entry bytes are vanilla.
`ProjectDiablo.dll` `0x2fb710` (`D2COMMON_10890_ITEMMODS_ApplyEthereal_INTERCEPT`) replaces 1.13c's ApplyEthereal. It
- Add core-rules and unported rows: "Ethereal bonus 25% (PD2's ApplyEthereal `0x2fb710`)", IR8; "Weapons lose durability

**Hook:** D2R 93847 `0x546cc0` (A5Q3AnyaGiftExecute, the deferred event queued by the a5q3 handler `0x54d610`). The detour runs the original, then if `game+0x104 == 2` it finds the player (FindUnit; closure `+8` guid, `+0x10` game) and calls QuestCreateItem 3 times with a `t1m` code, item level 99, quality 2, drop flag 1. Each map is picked uniformly from the items rows whose type (items record `+0x12e`, int16 itemtypes row) is the `t1m` itemtypes row; both come from the loaded tables, never a fixed list. Quest 0x25 bit 10 (set before the event is queued) makes it fire once per character per difficulty.

### The "death" and the loot (`0x1037a330` -> `0x10375fe0`) — new here
PD2's dead-mode wrapper `0x1037a330` runs its steps in order: `0x10375f70` (context), `0x10375fe0`, `0x103760a0`,
`0x10376380`, the class switch `0x10378d80` (no `0x39a` case), then `0x10379170`-`0x10379920`; only the last two
(`0x10379950`, `0x103799d0`) skip a unit with flag `0x20000`. `0x10375fe0` runs **before** that check, so the quiet

```
0x375ff8: 0x1036ebc0(game, unit, "rtmv", 7, 0x83, 0, 0, 0, 3)   ; one rtmv, quality request 7, item level 131
0x376022: count = rand() % 5 + 0x14                             ; 20-24
0x376032: tc = 0x1037f430(0x3b7)                                ; txt row 951 = ShadowOfMendeln, plus the compiled base
0x376055: 0x103164f0(7, frame + 1, 0x10372780, count, tc)       ; a unit timer one frame later
```
- `0x10372780(game, unit, _, left, tc)`: rolls the TC through 1.13c's TC drop `0x1030f120(game, unit, unit, tc, 0,
0x1037fa90(), 0, items[6], &dropped, 3)`, so at most 3 items per roll, at the monster's level (`0x103a1b00`, as

- Main: `KillQuietly` sets `UnitNoDrop`; no death listener or think code drops anything for port class 939. **No loot
  at all.**
- PR #1132 (a1f111d3) is data only: it gives `nihlathakMap` the TC `Mendeln Soul Drop` (picks −2: `ShadowOfMendeln`
  once, plus `Mendeln Soul Roll`, `rtmv` 1 in 9). It does not touch `nihlathak_ai.cpp`, so `KillQuietly`'s no-drop flag
  still blocks the TC: nothing drops. Even if the kill kept loot, the result would be one 6-pick roll (about 6 items)
  instead of 20-24, and `rtmv` 1 in 9 instead of always.

1. **Loot missing** (the main gap): `rtmv` always + 20-24 items from `ShadowOfMendeln`, 3 per roll, at the monster's
   level.
2. PR #1132's `nihlathakMap` TC: not PD2's and dead under the quiet kill. Revert that one monstats change (keep the
   row's TC empty as PD2's) and drop the `Mendeln Soul Drop` / `Mendeln Soul Roll` TCs, or keep them only if the owner
   wants `rtmv` at 1 in 9 instead of PD2's 1 in 1 (then a deviations row).
3. Wave champions and uniques spawn as normal monsters (known shortcut, deviation row "nihlathakMap's AI"): needs D2R's
   champion/unique maker, not in the toolkit's addresses. Late waves are weaker than PD2's.
4. Wave spot search: PD2 `0x10389c20` (size 2, mask 0x101, reach 4, no shift); `FindEventSpot` (`map_events.h`) is that
   search and now exists, so `SpawnWaveMonster` can use it.
5. Unit `+0xd0 = 11` mark on spawn: not identified, no known reader. Leave.

- **Treasure Fallen.** `0x10378d10` (class `0x3b1`, from the death switch): with the monster's AI control
  (`unitdata+0x28`) arg `+0x14` = *n* below 9, it calls `0x103843d0` `9 − n` times, each a 1.13c monster TC drop
  (`0x1030f2b0`) skipped for a no-treasure unit. With the stock death drop that is up to 10 rolls of `Treasure Fallen
  H` (3 picks each). Port: one. *n* is decoded in section 5: PD2's own Fallen think drops the TC once per 10% of life
  lost and counts it in *n*.
- **Invaders.** Not built (MS10). PD2 spawns `InvaderPortal` up to 3 times; the rest is `AiThink4.cpp`, never read.
  Until then the event rolls silently (no spawn, no notify). Either leave it out of the roll (`event_roll.h` draw 10 ->
  0) with a deviations row, or build MS10.
- **Horazon's 10% roll** (`0x10381510`, open in map-system "Not settled"): seed & 7 picks one of 8 cases; each looks up
  an item code (`0x1037c880`, `0x1037c020`, `0x1037ff30`, not decoded) and drops it once with `0x1036ebc0` at quality
  request 7, item level 131. Decode those three to know the 8 items, then add it to `horazon.cpp`.
- **Dark Wanderer:** merge PR #1131 (shards).
- Deviations row "Map events on Cartographer's native maps" lists only Wanderer, Mendeln, Treasure Fallen and Gheed;
  `map_events.cpp` runs all events but the invaders. Text fix.

1. `plugin/core-events/nihlathak_ai.cpp`, constants (comment: PD2 `0x10375fe0`, docs/research/map-events-audit.md §2):
   `MendelnTc = "ShadowOfMendeln"`, `SoulCode = D2RL::Items::MakeItemCode("rtmv")`, `SoulItemLevel = 131`,
   `LootMin = 20`, `LootSpread = 5`, `LootPerRoll = 3`, `MaxRolls = 40`, `StatLevel = 12`;
   `static_assert(LootMin + LootSpread - 1 == 24)`.
2. New `DropMendelnLoot(Game* game, Unit* unit) noexcept -> int32_t`:
   - `DropUniqueAt(game, unit, SoulCode, -1, SoulItemLevel, 2)` (`uber_drops.h`; quality 2 normal, as #1131 does for
     `wss`).
   - TC lookup as `lucion_chests.cpp:52-63` (`DataTablesOf`, `TcIndexByName`, `TcRecord`); warn and stop if missing.
   - `ilvl = UnitStat(unit, StatLevel, 0)` as `horazon.cpp:60`.
   - `target = LootMin + RandomBelow(UnitSeed(unit), LootSpread)`; loop up to `MaxRolls` while `dropped < target`:
     `Unit* items[6] = {}; int32_t n = 0; TcDrop(game, unit, killer, tc, 0, ilvl, 0, items, &n, LootPerRoll);
     dropped += n;` (signature as `lucion_chests.cpp:66-68`). `killer`: PD2 passes the monster itself; pass `unit`,
     and if the engine refuses a non-player killer (no items), fall back to `NearestPlayer(game, unit, LevelOf(unit))`
     and note it in a deviations row.
   - `plog::Info("nihlathakMap: rtmv and %d of %d items from %s at ilvl %d", dropped, target, MendelnTc, ilvl)`; add a
     drops counter to `NihlathakAiCounts` (and its status line in `dclone_ai.cpp:436-446`; widen the array to 5).
3. Call it in the `i > last + 1` branch right before `KillQuietly(game, unit)` (`nihlathak_ai.cpp:113-117`). Keep
   `KillQuietly`: PD2 also kills with no treasure; the loot is the death step's, not the TC's.

4. Optional, same PR: `SpawnWaveMonster` uses `FindEventSpot(room, xy, 2, 0x101, 4, false)` (`map_events.h`) in place
   of `FindFreeSpot`, and the deviations row "nihlathakMap's AI" drops the spot-search clause.
5. Data: coordinate with PR #1132 — remove its `nihlathakMap` TC change and the two `Mendeln Soul *` TCs (PD2's row has
   no TC), unless the owner wants `rtmv` at 1 in 9 (then skip the `DropUniqueAt` and keep the data).
6. Docs: deviations rows "Shadow of Mendeln's loot: one frame" (approximated) and, if used, the killer fallback;
   changelog fragment `#### Maps` / `- The Shadow of Mendeln drops its loot again when it fades.`
7. Game check (Hell, level 99, `core-events event mendeln` then a map; or wait the ~80 s fight): log lines
   `nihlathakMap: after the nova, it dies` then `rtmv and N of T items` with 20 <= T <= 24 and N >= T; a Splinter and a

PD2 swaps the `Fallen` think. `0x10361150` (called from `0x10344580` at start-up) writes PD2 functions into 1.13c's AI
table (`DAT_105ddeb0`, 0x10 bytes a row, the think at +8): `+0x68` is row 6, `Fallen`, set to `0x1035a3c0`. That think
runs for every `Fallen`-row monster:

```
0x35a3c0: if no monster data, or monstats +0x84 (word) != 1, or no AI control (monster data +0x28):
              1.13c's Fallen think (D2Game +0x83130, PD2 thunk 0x10318910); return
          pct = D2Common #11027(unit)             ; life * 100 / max life (stats 6 and 7), read in D2Common +0x32330
          n   = control +0x14                     ; 1.13c's first AI param
          if n < 10.0 - ceil(pct / 10.0):         ; the 10.0 is 0x1044fbc8
              control +0x14 = n + 1
              0x103843d0({0, unit, 0}, game)      ; one TC drop, the same call the death step makes
          then its own movement (below)
```

- **The gate.** Monstats `+0x84` is `aip8` in Hell in 1.13c's record (aip1-8 as words, three difficulties each, from
  `+0x56`; the offset is inferred from that layout, not read from a table loader). Only `treasurefallenMap` (945) sets
  `aip8(H)` to 1 in PD2's monstats; every other `Fallen` monster keeps the stock think.
- **So *n* counts the drops it already made while hit.** Every think tick (`aidel` 12/8/5 frames) it may drop one TC
  roll: one for each 10% of life lost, at most one per tick. At 95% life ceil(9.5) = 10, threshold 0, nothing; at 85%
  one drop owed; at 5% nine. A burst that takes several tenths in one tick catches up one drop per later tick.
- **The death step** `0x10378d10` (class `0x3b1` in the death switch `0x10378d80`) drops the rest: `9 − n` more calls
  of `0x103843d0`. With the monster's own death drop that is **always 10 rolls** of its TC (`Treasure Fallen H`, 3
  picks each in Hell): up to 9 while it is hit, the rest on death, plus the stock one. A one-shot kill gives all 9 on
  death.
- `0x103843d0(drop, game)`: skipped for a no-treasure unit (flag `0x20000` at unit `+0xc4`), a class with no monstats
  record (`0x1037c1d0`) or a unit with no room (D2Common #10331, the path's room); else 1.13c's monster TC drop
  (D2Game `+0x75680`, thunk `0x1030f2b0`; D2R's `MonsterTcDrop` `0x447b80`) with the record `{0, monster, killer 0}`:
  no killer, so no player's magic find.
- **Its movement** (the rest of `0x35a3c0`, not asked for, noted because the port runs D2R's stock Fallen think): it
  tracks its own position in control `+0x18`/`+0x1c`; standing still 3+ ticks with the target closer than 10 it walks
  to a spot 2-4 cells past its own position away from the target (`0x103a1880`), so it **runs from the player** rather
  than fighting like a fallen. Not decoded further.

Issue #1153, branch from main. Files: a new `plugin/core-events/treasure_fallen.cpp` + `.h`, registered next to the
others in `core_events.cpp`'s start-up (as `horazon.cpp` and `key_drops.cpp` are), and `plugin/CMakeLists.txt`.

1. **Signature.** Add D2R's Fallen think to the toolkit (d2rAI-toolkit `shared/plugin-common/src/rvas_93847/ai.h`
   `AiFallen = 0x5ae650`, `sig/shared.inc` and `sig/cache_6ab3782c.inc` rows, `knowledge/d2r-93847-addresses.md`):
   monai row 6's think, read from the AI table (`0x2396ea0 + 6 * 0x20`). Unique pattern (20 bytes would do):
   `4c 89 44 24 18 55 56 41 55 41 56 48 81 ec 88 00 00 00 48 8b e9 49 8b f0 48 8b ca 4c 8b f2 e8 ?? ?? ?? ??`.
   D2R's think already uses the first AI param (`control +0x44`) as a "fled" flag, so **do not keep *n* there**.
2. **State.** `struct Drops { uint16_t game; uint32_t unit; int32_t n; }` in a fixed array of 16 (at most 3 fallen a
   map); find-or-add by game id and unit id, clear the slot on death.
3. **Think** (`RegisterAiThink(context, 6, d2r::sig::AiFallen.address, 962, &Think)`; 962 is the port's
   `treasurefallenMap`, `map_events.cpp:77`): `pct = life * 100 / UnitMaxLife` (as `dclone_ai.cpp:131`); if
   `n < 10 - (pct + 9) / 10` (integer ceil), `++n` and one `MonsterTcDrop(game, unit, 0, &drop)` with
   `drop = {nullptr, unit, killer}` as `uber_deaths.cpp:39-44`. Killer: the tick's target (`tick + AiTickTarget`) when
   it is a player, else `NearestPlayer(game, unit, LevelOf(unit))`; no player, no drop (PD2 passes none; D2R's drop
   reads the killer for the quality roll, so a null one is not safe). Skip a unit with `UnitNoDrop`. Then always
   `VanillaAiThink(6)(game, unit, tick)` (keep D2R's Fallen movement; the flee is a deviation). Log
   `treasure fallen: hit drop %d of 9 at %d%% life`.
4. **Death** (`registerMonsterDeathListener`, as `horazon.cpp:77-160`): class 962 → `9 - n` calls of the same drop, the
   killer from the event as `uber_deaths.cpp:27-37`; log `treasure fallen: death drops %d (n %d)`. The stock death
   drop stays.
5. **Docs:** deviations row "Treasure Fallen: D2R's Fallen think" (it fights instead of fleeing; drops need a player
   as killer); changelog `#### Maps` / `- Treasure Fallen drops its loot as it is hit and on death, ten times in all.`
6. **Game check** (Hell, level 99): force event 15 on a map, hit a fallen (no god one-shot: `cheat god` kills in one
   hit, so first check the one-shot case: `core-events kill 962` -> `death drops 9 (n 0)`), then without god let it
   be hit down: `hit drop k of 9` lines and `death drops 9-k`.

- **champion `0x1037cbf0(game, room, x, y)`**: 1.13c `SpawnMonster` (D2Game `+0xeef10`, thunk `0x10313070`); then
  AI control `+8 |= 1`, `+0xc` = its own id, `+0x10` = 1, `+0x28` = game; monster flags `|= 1, 4, 8` (other, champion,
  unique, as 1.13c's own champions); one champion mod `0x103a2280` = D2Game `+0x23ae0` (a weighted pick of the
  monumod rows with `cpick`: 16 champion, 36 ghostly, 37 fanatic, 38 possessed, 39 berserk, weight 1 each in PD2) added
  by `0x103a22a0` = `+0x22920`; `0x103a22c0` = `+0x248a0(…, 3, 6)` (applies the mods, minion range 3-6); and
  `0x103a2260` = `+0x47880`, the champion pack: `rand() % 3 + 1` more of the class, each a champion with mod 16.
- **unique `0x1037caf0(game, room, x, y)`**: the same spawn and AI control; flags `|= 1, 8`; unique mods
  `0x10313100` = D2Game `+0x23ca0(game, unit, 0)` (0: no roll to champion; difficulty-scaled count of `upick` mods,
  at most 9); `+0x248a0(…, 3, 6)`: mods applied and 3-6 minions.

The thunk targets come from PD2's version tables, column 0 (1.13c): `0x104a9a14` -> `0x23ae0`, `0x104a8dcc` ->
`0x22920`, `0x104aaf5c` -> `0x248a0`, `0x104aa7e4` -> `0x47880`, `0x104a8854` -> `0x23ca0`, `0x1049be78` -> `0xeef10`.

D2R 93847, read-only RE, then implemented in `plugin/core-rules/item_rules.cpp` (`MapStackEqual`).

**Hook:** D2Common `Items.cpp` `ItemsStackEqual(Unit* target, Unit* other)` at `0x375960` (1.13c #11102), returns 1 when two items may merge. Entry
`48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 74 24 10 55 57 41 56 48 8B EC 48 83 EC 20` (21 bytes, matches once; the first 16 bytes match twice).
The native check compares class, unique/set row, items.txt stackable, ethereal, quality (only 1-3 pass) and stats 21-24, 159, 160, 194. It ignores every other stat, so
`cartographer_map_level` (564) and `map_force_event` (553, layer 1) were ignored.

**Callers (one hook covers all):** D2Game `0x4f2a80` (drop item onto item, then `0x4c1940` moves stat 70), inventory scans `0x386840` / `0x386e00` (ground pickup auto-stack, vendor buy,
the vendor UI), place-at-cell `0x38d0d0`, the client cursor `0x2c81d0`. Not used by the cube (`cube_stacks.cpp` counts itself) or the stash save.

**Split and cube leftovers:** the split is Ctrl+left click with the stack held. The source keeps its stats; `splitStack` copies none. The new piece gets its own Area Level (564) when it is made, and core-ui sets only the forced event (553) on it (see #1499 below). Cube leftovers are remade by `createItem`
in `cube_stacks.cpp`: for a `cmap` source its forced event (stat 553) is passed to `createItem` as property 383 `map-force-event-l` (param = layer, value as it was); Area Level (564) is not passed, since cartographer's hook adds property 374 onto the map's base level (174 instead of 87), and createItem gives a normal map its own level. A `SetUnitStat` on the made unit (through `editNativeItem`) reached neither the client tooltip nor the save (Slot3, #1400). `UnitStatEntries` entries are 16 bytes under D2RCore (`int32 layer, stat, value`, then a dword of unknown use; `D2RCore+0x832940` copies with `movups` and `add r8,0x10`; a dump of a map's stat 564 read `00000000 00000234 00000057`; the stat compare checks layer, stat and value one by one), the `pd2::mapstack::Entry` of `plugin/common/map_stack.h` read with `pd2::mapstack::Collect`, as the split does; a map with any other non-70 stat is refused as a partial take (the log names the stat).

Cause: the native check also compares item data +0x34 (the unique/set/superior row). D2Game's create path writes -1 there for a fresh normal item before the quality roll;
the save decoder writes it only for quality 1/3/5/7, so a map loaded from a save holds 0 (or whatever the allocation left). The field is not saved for normal items.
So a map dropped this session onto a stack loaded from a save was refused by the native call (server caller image +0x4f2b3a, client guess +0x2c8391 said merge), and our
stat compare never ran. Seen in slot 2: `item data +0x34 a 0 b -1` (loaded target, fresh cursor) and `a -1 b 0` (the reverse).

Fix: `MapStackEqual` sets +0x34 to -1 on both items when both are normal-quality maps, before calling the native check. Game check after the fix (slot 2): a fresh map dropped onto a loaded map made a 2-stack; after a save and reload, the loaded 2-stack held on the cursor and dropped onto a fresh map made a 3-stack. Both directions log `merge (equal -1)` from both callers.
The log is one summary line (no stat entry dump): the first verdict per (item, item, caller) in a 32-entry ring, and at most one line a second overall.

Cause: after `splitStack`, core-ui wrote the source's stats onto the new piece with `SetUnitStat`. The piece already had its own Area Level from creation: it read 87 before the write
and 174 after (`UnitStatEntries`, server unit), while the client's copy and the save kept 87. So the client's cursor guess (+0x2c8391) said merge and the server's
check (+0x4f2b3a) refused it (`stat differs 564`: a 87, b 174), in both directions. A save and reload wrote and read 87, so it stacked again in the next game.

D2R's `itemstatcost` has no `Divide` column, so core-maps carries PD2's values as `Routes` in
`plugin/core-maps/map_stats.cpp`, in the port's stat ids (`merge/ids-itemstatcost.tsv`). The port's ids keep vanilla's
0-358, so the targets are PD2's `Divide` values, except `map_mon_splash`: PD2 359 `item_splashonhit` is port 412. The
table was checked against PD2's `itemstatcost.txt` and the id list with a scratch script (no entry missing, extra or
different). A stat that is not in the table goes to monsters as itself, which is PD2's default `Divide` 1024.
## PD2's list builder (`0x1038aa00`)

- It makes a stat list (flags 8) with state 198 (port 244, `map`) unless the unit has one, attaches it and sets the
  state. The port uses flags 0, as D2R's own permanent lists do (`0x49bef0`, `0x48e600`).
- The list stat setter (D2Common #10188 -> #10261) sets and does not add, so two map stats with one target (for example
  `map_mon_att` and `map_mon_tohit`, both to-hit %) keep the later one, in stat order. D2R's `0x2f7c00` sets as well.
- A value of 0 is stored as 1. The stat keeps its layer.
- `item_maxhp_percent` on a monster multiplies its `maxhp` directly: `maxhp + maxhp / 100 * v` (unsigned, capped at
  0x7fffffff), and the list gets stat 432 (port 485) = 1 as a mark. Current life is not raised.
- Phys-as-extra (PD2 432-436, port 485-489): `(int)(v / 100.0f * damage)` of the monster's `mindamage` and
  `maxdamage`, as lightning 50/51, cold 54/55, fire 48/49, poison 57/58 and magic 52/53. The min goes through the 0 -> 1
  rule, the max does not. Cold length 56 and poison length 59 take the stat's layer, or 25 and 125 when it is 0.
- PvP arena stats and Horazon's resist rewrite (an area entry, [MS9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/223)) are not part of [MS3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/218). The area slots' extra monster
  stats (slots 4, 12, 14) are [MS4](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/219).

- **Opening:** `RouteMapStats` runs after the red portal opens (`map_open.cpp`). It reads the item's magic list
  (`0x2f5b80(item, 0, 0x40)`; entries `{layer, stat, value, extra}` at +0x30, count at +0x38) and keeps the monster
  and player lists in D2R's per-game counters (`0x5d88b0` on game `+0x1aac8`), so a new game starts without them.
- **Monsters:** `0x494a60` (spawn params, monster) is D2R's per-class setup of a new monster. Its only caller is the
  spawn core `0x493cc0` (`D2Game\src\Monster\MonsterSpawn.cpp`), which every spawner reaches (`0x492cf0` and the
  others), after the unit's stats and its alignment (`0x48e600`, from monstats `Align` at record `+0x87`) are set. A
  hostile monster in a map area (port levels 138-201) gets the list. PD2 gives a monster with an `Align` an empty list
  under the state; the port gives it none.
- **Players:** PD2 checks on a level change (`0x1038b000`, its hook of 1.13c D2Game `0x1cae0`). The port checks every
  frame in the player's life regen event `0x42e600` (`D2Game\src\Player\PlrModes.cpp`, unit event 3, which adds itself
  again for the next frame): in a map area the player gets the list unless it has one, elsewhere it loses it (state
  cleared, list detached and freed).

- Opening logged each stat and its route. First map: magic and gold find 22 and experience 22 to players, density and
  rarity elsewhere ([MS4](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/219)), `lifedrainmindam` 7, `item_maxhp_percent` 17, `item_openwounds` 8, `damagepercent` 14 and
  `map_mon_dropweapons` 4 to monsters.
- Entering Ruins of Viz-Jun (level 144): "player list on"; the first monster's maxhp went 10002 -> 11702 (+17%).
- Back through the portal to Harrogath: "player list off".
- Second map (new process): the player's totals in the map were exactly the map's values (magic find 80, gold find 80,
  experience 7, block -13, life regen -37); a monster's were poison mastery 7, armor % 63, `map_mon_droparmor` 3.
  24 monsters got the list.
- A new game, then `cheat goto 144` without a map: no list on the player or the monsters.

The 2000-2999 rows of [MS3](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/218)'s `Routes` table ([ms3-map-stats.md](ms3-map-stats.md)) are area slots (`Divide - 2000`), in
the port's stat ids. A scratch script checked all 28 against PD2's `itemstatcost.txt`. On opening, `RouteMapStats`
keeps each slot's first value in the per-game counters (`AreaSlot(game, slot)`); PD2's getter `0x1038a9e0` also returns
the first entry.

`0x1038a9e0` has five callers: `0x102fc400` (area level), three in the drop hook `0x10372180` (ethereal, corrupted,
sockets) and `0x1038bfc0` (extra boss). The region rewrite `0x1038b4d0` reads the slots itself. Nothing reads slots 7-9
and 15 (the boss drop stats), and slot 10 is only matched in `0x1038aa00` for Horazon's entry ([MS9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/223)). So leaving those
unported keeps parity.

- `*(game+0x1d0)` is an array of region pointers by level id (`0x508740` reads it). `0x5098b0` builds every region once
  per game (`0x508750`), from the levels row: groups chosen by `0x509940`, each group's component picks by `0x4195e0`.
- The layout is 1.13c's: `+0x10` group count, `+0x11` rarity sum, `+0x12` spawn count, `+0x14` groups of 0x34 bytes
  (`{monstats id u16, rarity u8, picks u8, ..., components at +0x10}`), `+0x2b8` `MonDen` (u32), `+0x2bc`/`+0x2bd`
  `MonUMin`/`MonUMax` (u8). From `+0x2e8` on are D2R's terror zone fields.
- `0x50acf0` spawns a room's packs: it caps `MonDen` at 10000 and spawns when `rand % 100000 <= MonDen`. The pack
  picker `0x419e80` weights the groups by their `+2` byte against the `+0x11` sum.
- D2R never reads the region's monster level (`+0x2dc`, `+0x2e0`), which PD2 rewrites for the area level. Monster, unique
  and item code all get it from `0x508f80(game, level)` (levels `MonLvl`/`MonLvlEx` through `0x32c700`, plus the terror
  zone bump `0x35b340`).
`ApplyArea` (`plugin/core-maps/map_stats.cpp`) rewrites the opened map's region the way `0x1038b4d0` does:

| Slot | Effect |
|---|---|
| 0 density | `MonDen` x (1 + v/100) |
| 1 area level | a hook on `0x508f80` adds v in map areas (138-201) |
| 2 rarity | boss pack min and max x (1 + v/100), truncated to a byte |
| 3 add monster | group `{id, rarity 1, picks 1}`, count and rarity sum + 1, 13 groups at most; an id that is not a monstats row is skipped |
| 4 fortify | density and pack counts x v/100; the monster list gets +100 `item_maxhp_percent`, +40 `damagepercent`, +40 to 329-332, +20 `passive_mag_mastery` (357) and `map_glob_skirmish_mode` (546) = v |
| 12 drop bonus | the monster list gets `map_glob_dropbonus` (399) = v |
| 14 treacherous/phasing | the monster list gets +100 `item_maxhp_percent` and `treacherous` (402) = v |
| 1 area level | a hook on `0x508f80` adds v in map areas (138-201) |

**The added group, read again.** The affix values are PD2 `hcIdx` ids (PD2's `monstats.txt` has an `Expansion` row,
so row and id part after 469): Ghastly adds `wraithMapMod` (port 1128), Rampant `baalminion3MapMod` (port 1186), both

  `ApplyArea` rewrote.

records.excerpt: The port hooks `0x43cd50(game, drop, 0)`, which makes the item from the request, and acts only when it returns to the
TC drop (`0x44486b`), so vendors, gambling, the cube and gold pass through.

**Sockets** (`0x103816c0`): not item types 38 `tpot`, 48 `thro` or 56 `misl` (`0x10364cb0` reads the item's own type);
1-2 sockets, 2-4 when the items row is `2handed` (1.13c `+0x11c`, D2R `+0x12b`).

**Corruption** (`0x103649d0`, second argument 0): nothing for an item that has `corrupted`. It walks cubemain: enabled
rows of op 16 or 18 on `corruptor` with a value, whose second input is the Worldstone Shard (or none) and whose first
matches the item by PD2's own test `0x103647d0` (class, type, quality, socketed, ethereal; no tier or runeword flags).
The group's "destroyed (rare)" row is the roll row: rare `usetype` output (`0xff`; `0xfe` is `useitem`, read from PD2's
`cubemain.bin`) and no third mod. It sets the roll to `value + rand() % (1000 - value)`, and the first row after it whose
value beats the roll puts its mods on the item through 1.13c `#10914` (mod type 7), D2R's `0x3d3420`. So a drop is never
destroyed. D2R's record is packed: inputs at `+0x14`, 10 bytes each; output A at `+0x5e`, quality `+0x64`, type
`+0x67`, mods from `+0x77` (`0x529d50`, `0x5269c0`; the field table `0x3e3ff0` gives offsets 0xe lower).

## [MS4e](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/494): the unique map drop (`0x10381510`)

**The roll.** `0x103799d0`, PD2's odds-only TC rolls on a monster's death, calls `0x10381510(game, unit)` when the unit's
level passes the map-area test `0x1037c510` and `0x10375ee0` hits TC 1020 `Unique Map Monsters` (Unique 4218, Set 10:
1 in 42180), or TC 1021 `Unique Map MapBoss` (Unique 2250) when one of the death record's `+0x20`, `+0x28`, `+0x30` or
`+0x38` is set. `0x103760a0` fills those from four monster id sets, the same ids as four of slot 5's sets:
`0x105deb54` (= `0x105de938`), `0x105dea4c` (= `0x105de7d4`), `0x105debcc` (= `0x105de9c8`) and `0x105debdc`
(= `0x105de9d8`). The mult (`+0x50`) is 2 when the monster has `map_glob_skirmish_mode` (PD2 493) and is no map boss
(`+0x48`, which also counts `0x105debb4` and `0x105dea84`, slot 5's other two sets), else 1.

**The drop.** `0x10381510` takes `0x1036f320(unit) & 7` (the unit's seed), then for each value: the map's base code from
its level (`0x1037c880`, PD2 level in `ecx`), `0x1037ff30(game, unique, 0)` (clears the unique's bit in the game's
dropped-uniques mask at `+0x1b24`, so it can drop again), and `0x1036ebc0(code, 7, 0x83, 0, 0, 1, 3)`: quality unique,
item level 131, by the unit. The eight (PD2 unique id, the port's runtime `uniqueitems` row):
Horazon's handler `0x10377ca0` also calls it, after the portal opens, when CRT `rand() % 10 < 1`.

**The port.** `RollUniqueMap` (removed with the unique-map roll, which was cut) rolled the TC by name on every map-area death (levels
138-201), with key drops' skirmish mult (1 for the TC 1021 bosses); `DropUniqueMap` draws one of the eight by the
monster's seed and drops it through `DropUniqueAt` (`uber_drops.cpp`, D2R's monster drop with the unique row forced, at
item level 131). Horazon's portal calls `DropUniqueMap` on a 1 in 10 of the monster's seed. D2R's unique roll `0x443910`
tests a forced row against the game's dropped-uniques mask too (`game+0x3638`, one bit per row, set on a drop): a second
Ureh City in one game came out normal. So `DropUniqueMap` clears the row's bit first, as `0x1037ff30` does.

**Game check** (Slot9, Hell, the level 95 Sorceress; a scratch build that forced the first 12 rolls and Horazon's 10%
to hit, not committed): in a Sewers map a kill logged `unique maps: monster 0 in level 142 rolls TC "Unique Map
Monsters" 1 in 42180 x1`, then `unique drop: t54 unique row 489 ... quality 7`. Before the mask fix a second Ureh City
came out quality 2; after it a second Warlord of Blood in one game came out quality 7. In a fortified map the roll
read `x2`. `cheat mspawn summonerMap` killed in the Sewers map logged `horazon: ... red portal to level 170`, then
`horazon: 10% unique map roll hit` and a unique drop.

- **Fortify** (magic map + `fort`, slot 4 = 50): density +30% then x0.5, 2062 -> 1340; packs 40-60 -> 20-30. Monster
  maxhp 8846 -> 17691; monster list totals `25=40 329=40 331=40 330=40 332=40 357=20 546=50`.
- **Treacherous** (magic map + `ivep`, slot 14 = 4): monster maxhp 10995 -> 21989; totals `402=4`.
- **Area level** (magic map + Worldstone Shard: cubemain row 216 came up on the 31st corruption, `+1 to Area Level`,
  slot 1 = 1): `area level +1`, and the level's monsters spawned at monster level 88, not 87.
- **Extra boss**: seen in a Sewers map (slot 5 section above).
- After Save and Exit, a new game opened a second map (`red portal to level 142, 2 opened`). An earlier run's refusal
  ("already open in this game") did not come back.
- Stat 489 (+13% physical as magic) reads 0 in the totals line by design: like PD2's `0x1038aa00`, `Apply` turns the
  phys-as-extra stats 485-489 into the element's min and max damage (489: stats 52 and 53) and never sets 489 itself.

The skirmish mult (slot 4, x2 rolls) stays 1 for the map bosses and their minions, as PD2's `+0x48` does, for the
key rolls as well as the unique map roll ([#529](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/529)): every TC roll in
`0x103799d0` takes `+0x50`.

- **Map items:** 48 `misc` rows with `pSpell` 12. 41 are tiered maps (T1 10, T2 10, T3 9, dungeons 3 plus the disabled `t41`, uniques 8),
  2 PvP arenas, 5 uber-boss keys (`ubtm`, `dcma`, `rtma`, `luca`, `uba`). The item code does
  not give the tier; the item type does (`t1m`..`t5m`, with `t?me` "exc" twins).
- **Map stats and rolls:** all data. Maps roll Normal/Magic/Rare from 118 magic prefixes and 124 magic suffixes (itype `t1m`-`t4m`),
  plus 18 rare prefixes and 10 rare suffixes that list `map`. Each affix sets one to three of 105 `map_*` stats (`map_mon_*` on monsters,
  `map_play_*` on players, `map_glob_*` on the area). Unique maps (T5) are 8 `uniqueitems` rows with nine fixed-range mods each.
- **Map recipes:** all data except op 30. 189 enabled `cubemain` rows take or make a map or a map ingredient: orb recipes per tier, 3-to-1 upgrades, corruption
  outcomes by `corruptor` band (op 16), heroic, fortify, ears, Catalyst Shard, Horadrim Scarab, uber-key difficulty. The 26 op-30
  rows are all blockers placed just before a real row.
- **Map areas:** 74 `levels` rows (ids 137-210) are PD2-only; 66 of them are map, event or uber areas (the rest are 3 PvP
  arenas and 5 guild halls). The area level a tier opens is `MonLvl3Ex`: T1 87, T2 88, T3 89, dungeons 92. No table links a map item to its area.
- **Map events and invaders:** the monsters, treasure classes and strings are data; the event roll, spawning, timers, Horazon's
  portal, Gheed's shop and the invader brain (`AiThink4.cpp`) are DLL code.
- **In the DLL:** using a map (gate checks, the item-to-area table, opening the area), copying the map's stats onto the area, its
  monsters and players, all `map_glob_*` effects (density, area level, rarity, extra monster groups, extra boss, drop bonuses,
  fortify), the event system, cube op 30, map stacking, the Maps stash tab and `.kills` counters.
- **Hook points core-rules already has:** six map-plan rows (map items, op 16/18, op 30, events and invaders, life regen cap,
  stackable items) and four rows whose map part is deferred (Find Item boss list, Desecrate list, death novas, Teleport 3 levels).

records.excerpt:
Data rows on `docs/unported.md` that the map system will reopen: map items never drop (treasure classes and `spawnable`, `merge/item-tables.txt`
no-drop lines 19-32), automap and monpreset (map presets), level types, new PD2-only areas.

- **74 PD2-only levels**, ids 137 to 210 in PD2's `levels.txt` (every row whose name D2R's `levels.txt` lacks). All are
  preset levels (`DrlgType` 2), built from **144 distinct DS1 files** (145 preset slots; `lvlprest` File1-6 are
  random alternatives) of 162.6 MB, all at new paths in `pd2maps.mpq` (`expansion/map` 138, `guild/pd2` 5,
  `act1/tristram` 1).
- Every tile they load exists: **205 vanilla DT1** that D2R ships, **180 PD2-only DT1** in `pd2assets.mpq`, and 3 DT1
  that PD2 ships over vanilla paths (`act4/fort/foregate.dt1`, `expansion/town/waypt.dt1`, `act1/barracks/warp.dt1`).
  No referenced DT1 is missing.
- **D2R has no HD art per DT1.** HD terrain is drawn from one HD preset per DS1 (`data/hd/env/preset/<ds1 path>.json`
  with its own `terrain_lod0.model` and `terrain.physics`, 2,100 of them), plus per-DT1 blend masks in
  `data/hd/env/tilemasks/*.json` (263 of D2R's 266 DT1). **None of the 144 PD2 DS1 has an HD preset**, and none of the
  180 PD2-only DT1 has a tile mask. All 205 vanilla DT1 they load do have one.
- **Import:** each level can be imported as its DS1 for layout, collision and classic graphics. No DS1 needs a rebuild
  for that: every DS1 is version 18 and every DT1 it loads exists. Importing them still takes table and engine work,
  not art: level ids shift (D2R uses 137 for Colossal Summit), 14 new level types sit past D2R's automap limit of 36,
  56 levels name `monpreset` rows D2R lacks, and 40 levels hold negative object ids, which no D2R DS1 uses. For HD,
  **all 74 must get a new HD preset** (built from scratch or stood in), since no PD2 DS1 has the same tile layers as a
  D2R DS1 whose preset could be reused.
- **HD stand-ins:** 29 levels use vanilla tiles only (counting the 3 overrides as vanilla), so their stand-in can draw
  on D2R's own biome and tile masks. 45 levels use PD2-only tiles: **180 DT1 files in 27 tile sets need an HD
  stand-in** (sets: levels that share PD2-only DT1 files are joined into one set).

- PD2 tables: `levels.txt`, `lvlprest.txt`, `lvltypes.txt`, `monpreset.txt`, `objects.txt` from the local extract of
  `pd2data.mpq` (`tools/pd2_extract.py`, git-ignored `pd2-data/`). DS1 and DT1 from the live `pd2maps.mpq` and
  `pd2assets.mpq` in `C:\Games\PD2\ProjectD2`, read in memory with `tools/mpq.py` (nothing extracted to disk).
- D2R: file list and file contents of the installed game's CASC storage, read with the toolkit's `modkit/casc.py`
  (175,823 names); tables from `d2rAI-toolkit/d2r-data/93847`.
- A level's tiles are its `lvltypes` row's `File 1-32`, filtered by the OR of its presets' `Dt1Mask` (bit n = File
  n+1). These are the DT1 the game loads for the level, so they are counted here; the tile list inside each DS1 was
  not used.
- DS1 parsing (version 18): header, tile layers (wall and orientation layers, floors, shadow, tag), then the object
  list (type, id, x, y, flags). Type 1 ids index `monpreset` rows of the DS1's act, type 2 ids index `objpreset` rows.
- "Same tile layers" compares a SHA-1 of the tile layer block plus the size against all 2,277 D2R DS1. No PD2 DS1
  matched, neither the whole file nor the layers alone.
- The tile-set count joins levels that share any PD2-only DT1 (union-find over levels).
- Rules on tiles and level types: `d2rAI-toolkit/knowledge/engine-limits.md` (level types fixed at 36 for the automap;
  classic tiles load in HD too), `tables.md` (`Layer` < 100, portal ids <= 255), `debugging.md`.

records.excerpt:
- **Data and DLL.** About half of each fight is data that PD2's tables already hold: monsters, skills, missiles, levels, items,
  cube recipes and chest treasure classes. The other half is code in `ProjectDiablo.dll`: the portal that opens at the Blood
  Fountain, the scripted phases, the tier scaling, the guaranteed drops, the key drop odds and the whole of Desecration. None of
  that code is reverse-engineered yet.
- **One shape for all three.** You cube three ingredients into an entry item: Vision of Terror (`dcma`), Voidstone (`rtma`) or
  Shadow of Hatred (`luca`). You cube the entry item alone to cycle its tier 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 (stat 185 `uber_difficulty`), then
  use it at the Blood Fountain in Harrogath. That opens the fight's PD2-only area. Tier 0 gives three single-use portals; tiers 1
  and 2 allow no re-entry.
- **Their ingredients depend on other features.**
  - Dclone needs the map system (Pure Demonic Essence drops from map bosses) and Uber Tristram (Black Soulstone).
  - Rathma needs map events (Splinter of the Void comes from the Shadow of Mendeln event) and Uber Tristram (the Hellfire Torch).
  - Lucion needs PD2's corrupted zones (Talisman of Transgression), which the owner cut for D2R's Terror Zones. So the
    Talisman's source must be moved, a decision for the owner.
- **Desecration** is a second corruption on an amulet, made in Lucion's reward room, the Temple of the Triune. One attempt is
  allowed per kill. The success chance is 50% at tier 0 and 60% at tiers 1 and 2. On success it adds one mod from an
  eight-mod, high-rarity pool. On failure the amulet becomes a rare that keeps two random corruption mods (the bricked outcome).
  Desecration is in no cube recipe. It is DLL code with its own UI panel (`desecratepanel`) and stats 206 `desecrated` and 207
  `desecrator`, which mirror Corruption's 360/361. It is new work.
- **Existing rows** already cover the boss skill functions: unported rows UberDiabSummon/UberDiabRun, RathmaSummon, Lucion kit,
  death novas, Rathma bone spear and uber immolation arrow, and the matching core-rules rows. The entry items are already blocked
  from dropping (`merge/item-tables.txt`). The rest is new: the opening, the areas, the phase scripts, the tiers, the guaranteed
  drops and Desecration (section 7).

- **PD2 data:** `pd2-data/` from `tools/pd2_extract.py` (the baseline in `pd2-baseline.json`). I read it with throwaway scripts
  kept outside the repo, using `cubemain`, `misc`, `monstats`, `skills`, `levels`, `treasureclassex`, `uniqueitems`,
  `itemstatcost`, `properties`, `states` and `objects`, plus `patchstring.tbl` through `tools/pd2_strings.py`'s `read_tbl`.
  "Row N" means the Nth data row, counted from 0 after the header. Monster HP is the Hell base, before PD2's player and tier
  scaling.
- **ProjectDiablo.dll:** printable strings only (ASCII and UTF-16), no disassembly.
- **PD2 wiki:** [Lucion](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Lucion) (it holds the shared pinnacle page: tiers, Dclone,
  Rathma, Lucion), [Rathma](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Rathma) (a stub marked possibly outdated),
  [Desecration](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Desecration),
  [Vision of Terror](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Vision_of_Terror),
  [Voidstone](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Voidstone),
  [Shadow of Hatred](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Shadow_of_Hatred) and
  [Annihilus](https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Annihilus). The wiki is a secondary source. Where its numbers and the data
  disagree, the data wins and the disagreement is noted. Phase scripts and DLL-only odds come from the wiki alone, because the
  data has no trace of them.
### Diablo Clone (`uberdiablonew`, Hell level 110, HP 10530 base, resists 30/30/30/30)
### Lucion (`Lucion`, Hell level 110, HP 24000, resists 30/30/30/30)

- Reimagined has two endgame area systems. The **Forsaken Labyrinth** (released) is pure data: 28 fixed levels and a
  reusable cube token. **Maps** (`feature/maps`, unreleased) are 30 map items (10 themes x 6 tiers) opened in the
  cube, 120 generated levels, and a closed-source D2RLoader plugin `d2rl-maps.dll` for rolled modifiers, events,
  treasure monsters and level fixes.
- Opening an area needs no plugin: a cube recipe with output `"Red Portal,lvl=<level id>"` opens a red portal to any
  level. This corrects our capability matrix, which says the cube portal output opens only the Cow Level (that is
  true of the plain `Cow Portal` output only).
- Licence: the mod repo is **GPL-3.0** (`LICENSE.txt`, the GNU GPL v3 text; GitHub detects `gpl-3.0`). The map
  plugin source is **not public**. The LAN repack ships plugin DLLs with no source and no licence.
- Copyable as is: the Python generator and its validators (`scripts/maps/`), the custom-arena builder, and the
  engine knowledge in their notes. Their table rows and maps are their own design, not PD2's, so they are templates
  for PD2 parity rather than parity data. Copying any GPL-3.0 file binds our release to GPL-3.0 (see Licence).

The D2R side of the uber key opening. PD2's side is [pd2-uber-bosses-dll.md](../../pd2/uber-bosses-dll.md), sections 2
and 3. D2R addresses are RVAs in the 93847 dump (`ImageStamp 0x6ab3782c`), read in Ghidra (`D2R.gpr`); PD2's are VAs
in `ProjectDiablo.dll` (`PD2.gpr`).

- **Check:** the map gates, in PD2's order, then the Blood Fountain. PD2's `0x1037d840` returns the squared distance,
  so the user must stand with `dx² + dy² <= 0x95` from (5074, 5114): about 12 subtiles. A refusal keeps the key.
- **Use:** PD2's `0x1038a680`. The user, then every other player in Harrogath who is level 80 or more with a squared
  distance under 0x96, is handled in turn: pets removed, 37 states stripped, warped in. The others are picked before
  anyone moves. If the user does not arrive, nobody else goes and the opening fails, as in PD2. The tier (the key's
  stat 370) and the number who arrived go into the game's counters (keys `UBRT` and `UBRE`, PD2's game `+0x2629` and
  `+0x2628`), and the opening counts on `MAPS`, the one-per-game gate the maps use.

- **Warp:** `0x488180` (game, player, level, 0). In the same act it finds the level's arrival spot through
  `0x2ef8b0` (the level's warp search in `D2Common\src\Drlg\DrlgWarp.cpp`) and teleports there with `0x491ca0`; else
  it changes act. D2R's debug "Warping to level..." handler `0x402820` calls it the same way. PD2 instead places an
  invisible portal object (587) and runs each player through its portal-entry code.
- **Players:** the game's clients are a list at game `+0x138`, each client's next at `+0x628` (`0x484d90` walks it to
  find a client by id). `0x484c90` (client, 0) is the client's player.
- **Pets:** PD2's `0x1037fb10` (flag 0) walks every pet type but 3, `golem`, and kills the hireling (type 7). core-maps
  walks D2R's pet table (`PetEntry`, `FirstPet`) the same way and removes each pet with `RemovePet`, which kills it.
  PD2 removes the summons without a death. The merged pettype.txt has 31 rows.
- **States:** PD2's `0x1037f4a0` with flag 1. Each state that has a stat list is turned off, and the list is detached
  and freed, as D2R's `RemoveSkillState` does per state.

- **Operate table** `0x23a51c0`: 75 slots of `int fn(args*)`, args = {game, object, player, seed, class id}, indexed
  by objects.txt `OperateFn` (record `+0x15e`). The dispatcher `0x592c40` skips a null slot, so with core-maps off a
  grey portal does nothing. D2R's portal operate 15 (`0x58f680`) moves the player next to the linked partner portal,
  and fails without one: PD2's grey portals have no partner, so the slot-60 function warps with `0x488180`.
- **Making a portal:** D2R's portal maker `0x432ce0` spawns the object with `0x490410` (2, row, x, y, game, room, 1, 1,
  0, 0) in the room `0x38dfb0` finds for the spot, sets mode 1 and adds event 1 (the opening) after the row's
  `+0x9c >> 8` frames. Then `0x435dd0` makes a linked return portal in the target level. core-maps does the first part
  only and sets the destination with `0x34e9d0`.
- **Removing an object:** as operate 15 removes a used town portal: `0x2ef4d0` (room, 2, unit id) tells the room's
  clients, `0x48faa0` (game, unit) frees the unit, `0x2f0530` (room) marks the room changed.
- **Rooms and units:** `0x2efde0` gives a room and its neighbours, a room's units start at `+0xa8` and go on at unit
  `+0x160` (as `0x593630` walks them). The game's monsters are 128 lists at game `+0x2630`, by unit id & 0x7f, the next
  at `+0x158` (`0x48fe80`, `0x4925b0`).
- A key used up when nobody arrives: PD2 keeps it (`0x10383060` returns 0); the port's check refuses every case it can

Request: research-uber-arenas. Read-only research, 2026-11-15. Sources: pd2-resurrected `origin/cartographer-migration`,
d2r-tools `origin/main` (d78952d), d2rAI-toolkit (with its D2R 93847 data cache `d2r-data/93847/`), GitHub issues #958,
#960, #961, #962, #1027 and PR #1030. Claims marked **[suspicion]** were not checked in game or in code.

- **D2R ships this exact pattern.** Level 136 (Uber Tristram, "Act 5 - Pandemonium Finale") is an Act V row with
  `LevelType 11`, `Layer 25`, `DrlgType 2`, the same as Tristram (38). Its own `lvlprest` row 1090 points at Tristram's
  `Act1/Tristram/Tri_Town4.ds1`, an Act I DS1 (`d2r-data/93847/data/global/excel/levels.txt`, `lvlprest.txt` row 1090
  vs row 300). The toolkit lists it as the clone pattern ("Stock DS1s already have HD presets, so a clone needs no new
  art", `d2rAI-toolkit/knowledge/new-game-systems.md:138-142`).
- **HD is per DS1, not per tile.** D2R draws a level from one preset per DS1 path,
  `data/hd/env/preset/<ds1 path>.json`, holding a sculpted `terrain.model` and placed models
  (`knowledge/hd-graphics.md:169-173`; `research/pd2-only-levels` doc lines 15-18). A stock DS1 brings its own
  Blizzard-made preset. A DS1 Blizzard did not make has none, and that gap is what the converter tried to fill.
- **That gap is where parity failed.** #1030 froze the converted arenas. Dclone's HD and legacy matched, but Lucion's
  lava rim did not: "solid lava where legacy draws thin cracks ... thin cracks need new HD art" (PR #1030 game-check
  comment). The owner closed it: "frozen arenas did not reach legacy/HD parity". Any approach that makes a new HD scene
  for a non-Blizzard tile layout ends up in the same place.
- **The fights need little geometry.** All they read from `placements.h` is a centre, a square of free floor (Dclone
  souls 50x50 subtiles = 10x10 tiles, Lucion adds 44x44 = about 9x9 tiles), boss spots, a marker and 1-3 portal spots
  (`plugin/placements/dclone.cpp`, `rathma.cpp`, `lucion.cpp`; `bitterdepths.cpp` has only a binding). Every
  candidate room below has more than that. Rathma bosses already "take the nearest free spot"
  (`docs/deviations.md:111`).

records.excerpt:
1. **Reserve 7 `lvlprest` ids** in `merge/ids-lvlprest.tsv` (shared, serial; the next free id is after 1156,
   `TombEventMap 1153`...`Descent Map 1156`).
2. **`tools/static_levels.py` plus one data file** (for example `merge/static-levels.tsv`: level, stock DS1, objects to
   strip, objects to add with tile x/y). At merge it:
   - reads the stock DS1 from modkit's cache (as `pd2_coverage.py` already does) and writes a copy under a new path
     (for example `data/global/tiles/pd2r/static/<name>.ds1`). Only the object block is rewritten; the header and
     tile layers stay byte-identical (`object_list` gives the offset);
   - copies the stock preset JSON byte-for-byte to `data/hd/env/preset/pd2r/static/<name>.json`. Its `terrain.model`
     and `terrain.physics` paths stay absolute paths to the stock files, so no mesh is copied
     (`wstone01.json` terrain filename `data/hd/env/preset/expansion/baallair/wstone01/terrain.model`);
   - emits the `levels` `set` ops and the new `lvlprest` row;
   - prints each named DS1 tile's world subtile coordinates (origin `OffsetX*5`, 5 subtiles per tile **[suspicion:
     check one against an existing Place]**), so `Place`s are copied, not guessed.
   - When no object needs changing, `File1` names the stock DS1 itself and nothing is written (the 136 way).
   - Generated, not committed (ADR 0002). Blizzard files stay out of git.
3. **Test** (`tools/tests/test_static_levels.py`): for every row, the copy's tile block hash equals the stock DS1's, the
   preset bytes equal the stock preset, the size and `LevelType` match the source level, and every `Place` of the
   bound encounter lies on a walkable tile of the DS1 (collision bit `0x20000`, `knowledge/hd-graphics.md:189`). This is
   the parity gate in CI: parity holds by construction, and the test proves the construction.
