- **Dclone: a Mesa fixed plan.** An interior of 2x2 grid cells (16x16 tiles) holding one 16x16 Mesa 3 ("Chaos", City
  of the Damned) fill, inside a ring of the 8x8 border pieces (W 800, N 801, E 802, S 799, corners 803-806,
  `d2r-tools docs/cartographer/tilesets/a4-mesa.md`). That makes a 32x32-tile square level, fully closed by cliffs,
  with 16x16 open floor. Two gaps: Cartographer's Mesa has no game check yet, and its smallest interior is 6 cells
  (`kMinCells`, `plugins/cartographer/src/outdoor/mesa_plan.h`). A fixed 2x2 mode needs to be built.
- **Lucion: the Lava/Chaos route.** Chaos Sanctuary is LevelType 28 (level 108 in `levels.txt`), the same as
  Cartographer's Lava tileset (`maze_tilesets.h:53`). Its lava filler ring (closed cell 836) is proven in game
  (#372). So a fixed plan with one Chaos piece in the middle (Heart 862, 24x24, the pentagram; or Entry 857), ringed
  by closed lava cells, gives a 72x72 level: the piece enclosed by lava, the same lava art in both views. Two risks:
  the Heart's four sides open to wings that will not be there, so the piece meets lava filler on a seam Blizzard
  never paired; and its clear square reads only about 9x9 between the pentagram blocks. **[suspicion; check in
  game]**
- **Rathma's boss stages and Bitter Depths** fail the rule in their C picks too (largest open squares of 8). If the
  rule covers them, they take the same Mesa or Lava plan, and the clear-the-area stages get smaller.
- **The Temple** has no boss. It can stay C (Act III Temple), unless the owner wants it square too.

Research for running pd2-resurrected leagues on our own hosted servers, the way Reimagined runs its ladder. It builds on
[multiplayer-options.md](multiplayer-options.md) (read that first: TCP/IP, the EULA, Reimagined's three launch modes).
Sources read 2026-11-18. Web pages are cited by URL, repo files by path and line. Reimagined's repos were read at their
default branches that day (`reimagined-launcher` at `7fb009b`). Nothing here was run in a game or on a server.
**Unconfirmed** marks what no primary source states; **estimate** marks our own arithmetic. Not legal advice.

- A hosted league is five things: a **headless game server** (D2R plus a D2RLoader plugin), a **lobby** that puts
  games on those servers, **server-owned characters**, **one account** across launcher and website, and a **signed
  release** the server can require. Reimagined appears to have built all five in about two weeks (our inference from
  the Ladder wiki page's creation date, 2026-11-04, `wiki-content/Ladder.md` line 8; build dates are not public) on top
  of a website and API that existed before.
- **Nothing headless is available to us.** D2RLoader's docs and changelog never mention a dedicated mode
  (https://d2rloader.net/docs.html, https://d2rloader.net/changelog.html). Reimagined's `d2rl-d2rds.dll` lives in a
  private repo (`d2rl-plugins` returns 404), and none of its repos carries a license (GitHub API `license: null` for
  `reimagined-launcher`, `d2r-reimagined-website`, `wiki-content`), so we may read but not copy them. We build our
  own, or ask.
- **It is feasible:** D2R.exe already contains the game server (single player runs a local server; the server-side
  game table has 1024 game handles, `Pyre-Flies/D2R-Mods` `docs/reverse-engineering/README.md` line 94), and
  Reimagined proves a plugin can run it with no player session.
- **Biggest risk is Blizzard's EULA, not cost.** Section 1.C.viii forbids hosting "matchmaking services for the Game(s)"
  and 1.B.ii limits use to "personal and non-commercial entertainment"
  (https://www.blizzard.com/en-us/legal/fba4d00f-c7e4-4883-b8b9-1b4500a402ea/blizzard-end-user-license-agreement,
  revised 2024-03-21). No Blizzard action against a hosted D2R mod server was found (section 3.4).
- **Cost headline (estimates, 2026-11-18 prices, Windows boxes on OVH Game servers):** small test league (~50
  concurrent) about **$120-150/month**; mid (~500) about **$700-850/month**; large (~2,000+, three regions) about
  **$2,700-3,200/month**. The same large league on AWS on-demand Windows is about **$12,000/month**. Capacity per box
  is unmeasured; beta run 1 must measure it (section 4.3).

| Work item | Detail | Breaks if skipped |
|---|---|---|
| Keep every gameplay hook in a `Shared` plugin | Already so: `core-rules` and `core-events` are Shared (`plugin/core-rules/plugin.cpp` line 54, `plugin/core-events/plugin.cpp` line 50), `core-ui` is Client (`plugin/core-ui/plugin.cpp` line 57) | A Server-only rule runs on the host alone and clients desync, or a Client rule changes gameplay unchecked |
| Bump each Shared plugin's version every release | The loader matches Shared plugins by id, version, ABI, scope and flags (toolkit `third_party/PluginSDK/README.md` lines 193-196) | Two builds with the same version but different code join each other |
| `[d2rl] match` list in each Shared plugin | Today no plugin config in `plugin/` declares one (grep for `[d2rl]` finds none). List every gameplay setting, up to 64 paths (SDK README lines 99-121) | A host with a changed drop or event setting plays different rules than its clients, silently |
| Client-to-host plugin messages | Client-side item or game-thread work goes to the host by `NetworkService` message, <= 224 bytes (SDK README lines 1125-1150; `knowledge/d2rloader-capabilities.md` lines 117-118) | Features that work in single player do nothing on a TCP/IP client (a client has no game thread) |
| Two-player game checks | W37's shared shrines first (`origin/research/w37-server-rules`, `docs/research/w37-server-rules.md`) | Multiplayer-only rules ship untested: a single-player check never proves sync (`knowledge/d2rloader-capabilities.md` line 113) |
| Measure the host | CPU, memory and network of the host's D2R process per player and per game, and the player cap per game | Section 4's sizing stays a guess |
| Player guide "Play with friends" | Offline character, Multiplayer screen, port TCP 4000, Public/Unlisted/LAN, what must match, save backups (https://d2rloader.net/tcp-ip.html) | Support load: "cannot join" and port questions |

| Work item | Detail | Breaks if skipped |
|---|---|---|
| Pin and check the loader version | `release.toml` already pins D2RLoader `1.3.1-beta` and game build `93847`; the launcher shows "missing or the wrong version" (launcher README *System requirements*) | Clients older than the host's loader cannot join (1.2.1-beta changelog, https://d2rloader.net/changelog.html) |
| Turn on the TCP/IP button | Write `show_tcpip_button = true` in `d2rloader/config/d2rloader.toml`, as Reimagined's launcher does (`ReimaginedLauncher/Utilities/D2RLoaderLaunchSettings.cs`, `UpdateDefaultMod`) | Players cannot find Multiplayer |
| File hashes per release | Already produced: `release-manifest.json` schema 3 for the launcher (toolkit `release/README.md` line 12; `release.toml` `[catalog]`) | Repair cannot restore a clean mod, and "same version, different files" joins fail |
| Signed release metadata | Deferred in the launcher today (`docs/specs/launcher-v1.md` line 12: "signed game-release metadata ... remain deferred") | Needed in step 3: the server must refuse unsigned or altered packages |

- **Reimagined:** a ladder has `startDateUtc`, `endDateUtc`, `archivedAtUtc`, and can be hidden; admins may preview a
  scheduled ladder and "Nothing played in a preview is saved"; hidden tester ladders take uploaded saves
  (`src/lib/ladder-schedule.ts` lines 22-29, 56-63; `src/lib/tester-saves.ts`). Ladder-only rules are data in the
  package (rarer high runes, locked settings, `wiki-content/Ladder.md` lines 13-43). What happens to characters at a
  ladder's end: **unconfirmed** (no public page).
- **PD2:** at season end ladder characters move to non-ladder, shared-stash items do not; an open beta on the main
  realm tests the reset for 2-3 days, then downtime; beta downtime is about 5-10 days; Season 13 ran 182 days from
  2026-04-24 and Season 14 started 2026-10-23 (https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/Seasons). The PD2 FAQ says the
  ladder resets every four months (https://wiki.projectdiablo2.com/wiki/FAQ), which the season table contradicts.
- **Ladder-only items in our data:** `runes.txt` already has `disallowCraftingInLadder`, `disallowCraftingInNonLadder`,
  `firstLadderSeason`, `lastLadderSeason` (`files/data/global/excel/runes.txt`, header columns 4-7). Whether a TCP/IP
  or `d2rds` game counts as ladder for the engine: **unconfirmed**. PD2's online recipe groups in `cubemain` were cut
  for single player (`docs/deviations.md` line 32) and come back with leagues.
- **For us:** migration to a non-league realm is a save-API job (move the files to the standard realm's manifest),
  not game code.

**Blizzard's game has none.** Blizzard dropped TCP/IP before launch: its beta FAQ said TCP/IP "will not be available in
the upcoming Beta or the final game" (August 2021, reported by
https://www.gameinformer.com/2021/08/11/diablo-2-resurrected-open-beta-details-revealed-quietly-removes-peer-to-peer-multiplayer),
and a community-team post in September 2021 gave the reason as security
(https://www.diablofans.com/news/49602-diablo-ii-resurrected-console-lobbies-tcp-ip, quoting the Blizzard forum post,
whose own URL no longer loads). No later patch put it back (unconfirmed beyond the toolkit's own review,
`d2rAI-toolkit/docs/distribution.md`, *Play modes and policy*).

- Every plugin sets one role: `Client` (UI, input), `Server` (gameplay rules and saves) or `Shared` (both). "The host
  performs both roles."
- `Shared` plugins must match host and client by id, version, plugin ABI, scope and compatibility flags. Client-only
  plugins are not checked and not recorded in the save.
- A Shared plugin can list up to 64 config paths under `[d2rl] match`; those values must be equal on both sides.
- Only the local game or the TCP/IP host may change items; a client sends a plugin message (<= 224 bytes) to the host.
  A TCP/IP client has no game thread (`d2rAI-toolkit/knowledge/d2rloader-capabilities.md`, *Multiplayer implications*).
- The plugin network service does not exist on Battle.net (same file).

**Battle.net: not possible.** Blizzard's EULA forbids connections to "any unauthorized server that emulates" its
platform (section 1.C.ix, https://www.blizzard.com/en-us/legal/fba4d00f-c7e4-4883-b8b9-1b4500a402ea/blizzard-end-user-license-agreement).
No Blizzard source gives mod authors realms, private ladders or modded Battle.net play
(`d2rAI-toolkit/docs/distribution.md`). Mods are offline only on Blizzard's side.

**Server emulators for D2R: none found.** No public D2R Battle.net emulator turned up. In 2021 Blizzard sent
cease-and-desist letters to D2R modders over tools for the technical alpha, "citing security concerns"
(https://www.wowhead.com/tbc/es/news/blizzard-issues-cease-and-desist-letters-to-modders-citing-security-concerns-322566;
whether one was a server emulator: secondary sources only, **unconfirmed**). The classic bnetd case went Blizzard's way
in 2004 (https://gamedeveloper.com/game-platforms/blizzard-wins-latest-round-of-bnetd-court-battle; a news report,
not the ruling). Not legal advice.

1. **D2RLoader TCP/IP, player-hosted (beta run 1).** Works today. Needs from us: keep every gameplay hook in the
   `Shared` plugins and bump their version every release (already the rule); list gameplay config in each Shared
   plugin's `[d2rl] match`; send client-side item work to the host by plugin message; a two-player game check for
   rules with a multiplayer side (W37's shared shrines first). Docs: a player page "play with friends" (offline
   character, Multiplayer screen, port 4000, what must match, back up saves). No launcher needed if the release 7z
   pins one loader version and every companion.
2. **Same, plus a small launcher or install check.** Reimagined's experience shows the real pain is version drift. A
   launcher (or `install.ps1` step) that fetches our release, checks the loader version and turns on the TCP/IP
   button removes most "cannot join" reports. Needs: a release manifest with hashes; no server. The owner's
   `resurrected-launcher` already exists and its accepted contracts fix the account and hosted-join shape
   ([hosted-leagues.md](hosted-leagues.md) section 1.2).
3. **Hosted league (beta run 2).** Needs, as Reimagined built it: a headless-server plugin on D2RLoader, a lobby
   plugin and listing service, a server-saves plugin and web API owning characters, signed release packages with a
   plugin allowlist, hosting boxes, accounts, and moderation. That is a separate project of its own; the EULA clause
   on unauthorized servers is a risk the owner must weigh first. Before building, ask whether D2RLoader's authors will
   offer a dedicated mode or the `d2rds` approach as a shared component. Reimagined's repos carry no license, so
   their code is reference only; the EULA's matchmaking clause (1.C.viii) applies too.
4. **Battle.net.** Not an option.

- **Most table rows can close without code.** Their columns and tables can be cut outright or close once one small
  check passes. They are either empty in PD2, set only on rows both games share (vanilla 1.13c leftovers
  that D2R handles its own way), or tied to a cut feature (PvP, ladder, the classic editors). Belts and body locations
  match D2R apart from the classic pixel boxes of one belt, so that row closes.
- **Five data columns need a core-rules row** (engine code): skills `checkfunc`, `nocostinstate` and `general`; missiles
  `Qty` and `SpecialSetup` on PD2's new missiles; difficultylevels `HireableBossDamagePercent` and the uber/ultra code
  odds; and the hireling `WType` columns, which go with the next item.
- **A whole hireling is missing.** PD2's Act 4 hireling, the Ascendant (hireling ids 30-35, two kinds: `ascd`/`ascl`),
  and PD2's second Rogue Scout set (ids 36-38) are not in the merge, because D2R uses ids 30-38 for its own new Desert
  Mercenary and Barbarian rows. The unported row calls this "level brackets left out", but it is the whole Act 4
  hireling. Bringing it back needs new hireling ids past D2R's 38 (untested) and engine code for its weapon types.
- **Art: two gaps with no unported row, which may be visible in HD today.** (1) None of the 549 PD2-only monster rows
  in the merge has an entry in D2R's `data/hd/character/monsters.json`. That includes three superuniques in ported areas
  (The Countess, Bloodwitch the Wild, the Wisp Boss) and summons of ported classes (Dopplezon, Lesser Hydra, the
  Necromancer's Summon Resist archer, the Lightning Sentry's chain sentry). (2) The merged `overlay.txt` takes PD2's
  `Character` values (`all`, `Bar`, `Assasin`, `?`). D2R uses that column as the HD overlay folder name, so 144 vanilla
  overlays (shrines, shouts, curses, the barbarian and assassin overlays) and all 33 PD2-only ones point at folders
  that don't exist. Both findings come from the tables and the toolkit's HD notes. Neither was checked in game; that
  check comes first.
- **Item art and the shared skill icon sheet are scripted art work, no layout decision.** PD2's class-less skills use
  icon cels 0-60, which fits D2R's 62-icon strip, so nothing has to compete for a slot. Where D2R and PD2 put different
  skills on one cel, the D2R skill is a monster skill or shares the picture (Attack, Town Portal), so PD2's frames can
  simply win. Item pictures follow the same upscale-and-sprite pattern as P11.
- **Audio: the cut holds.** Of PD2's 46 WAV, the 16 drop sounds serve the loot filter, and the Pyre-Flies filter ships
  its own 16 (P7; not compared one by one). The other 30 are boss and NPC voice lines and a few effects for areas and
  bosses not ported yet (counts from [asset-inventory.md](../../pd2/asset-inventory.md)). They can be cut with the sounds
  row, or converted later, one FLAC per file (open question from #5).
- **Rows to fix on the list itself:** the Gheed event row belongs to MS8. The "other classes" row is stale, since the
  pre-alpha now builds those classes as W11-W35. The level-pipeline rows wait only for #151's work items. The missile
  stand-in models (P10) have no row. Nor do PD2's client UI overlays: the Buff HUD companion covers buff timers, mini
  skill icons and the skill bar, Item Roll Ranges the tooltip stat ranges, and a D2R Reimagined plugin can cover the
  potion counter, so each needs only a row naming its plugin. Only the DPS counter needs a plugin built; it is in the alpha (owner).

Every "not yet" row on [unported-rows.md](../../pd2/unported-rows.md) (at `4c8f3e3`) that names no open work item, plus the
approximated art and hireling rows the ticket names. Rows whose P item is closed (P3, P4, P11) are in scope: the
closed item no longer owns them, as #148 found for P3. Left out:

goes to vanilla's srvdo 113 (`0x1031b200` stub). In the port, 582/583 keep srvdo 113 and run D2R's own srvdo 113.

`PerfectShrine` is a string key in `patchstring.tbl`: "Perfect Gem Shrine activated". Shrine table `0xfa5f8 + 0xd8`
(shrine code 18, Gem Upgrade): vanilla `0x6fc8b430`, PD2 `0x103a0fc0`. Three changes:

1. **Stacked gems.** The upgrade goes through `0x10371200`: when the gem's quantity (stat 70) is over 1, it takes one
   off the stack and creates one upgraded gem; otherwise vanilla's upgrade (`0x6fc8b070`), which replaces the whole
   item with one new gem. The port's gems stack to 50 (`files/.../misc.txt`), and D2R's gem shrine is vanilla's, so a
   stack of 50 chipped gems would most likely become one flawed gem (not run).
2. **No gem.** One random chipped gem, as vanilla (PD2 rolls with `rand`, vanilla with the object's seed).
3. **Perfect Gem Shrine.** On the chipped-gem path only, `rand() % 5000 < 2` (1 in 2500) sends a game chat line
   (packet 0x26, the player's name and "Perfect Gem Shrine activated") to every client in the game. No item or stat
   change was found with it: it is an announcement.

4. **Shrines are shared.** Codes 6 (armor), 8-11 (resists), 12 (skill), 13 (mana recharge), 15 (experience)
   (`0x103a0de0`), 7 (combat, `0x103a0e80`) and 14 (stamina, `0x103a0f20`) run vanilla's effect on the user, then on
   every other player in the game whose position is within a squared distance of 450 (`0x1037d840`, about 21
   subtiles) of the user.
5. **Resist shrines raise the cap.** After codes 8-11 (`0x103a0d60`), the shrine state's stat list gets +10 of the
   matching max resist: fire (state 131) `maxfireresist`, cold (132) `maxcoldresist`, lightning (130)
   `maxlightresist`, poison (133) `maxpoisonresist`. shrines.txt does not hold it (its Arg0 is the +75%).

(`min(ln12/2, 32)`, Arctic Blast 24), calc3 missiles (`min(2 + lvl/4, 5)`, Arctic Blast 2), srvmissilea / cltmissilea

1. A monster: vanilla srvdo 19 (`[0x105e25d0] + 0x4c`), D2R's Inferno (`0x554460`).

## cltdo 111 (`0x103abce0`)

Same target, range and count, from cltmissilea. One seed roll first: when count > 1 and roll % 100 < 40 the line is
pushed count subtiles further. The rolls are the seed's new low dword taken as signed (`IDIV`, signed multiply by
the reciprocal), so a negative roll always passes both tests; the port keeps that. Per point a roll r: the flame is
drawn when r % count < 2, with range calc1 + r % 2 - 1.
PD2 also writes a velocity (missiles.txt Vel at 1.13c +0x9a, - 6 + r % 8, halved on the first point when over 2) but
its flags (0x8020) leave out 4; D2R's client create (`0x1b7760`) reads params velocity only with flag 4, so the flame
keeps Vel (D2R +0xc0), as in PD2. After each flame PD2 calls `0x103a45c0` (a D2Common pointer) with calc1 and the
missile; D2R's Inferno client (cltdo 24, `0x2203f0`) calls `0x34da60 (missile, MsAnimSpeed << 8 / calc1)` at the same
place, and the port does that. The ending matches cltdo 24 under state 12 (inferno): rewind the frame by 2, or set
+0x4c / +0x64; D2R does it only for other players, PD2 for every caster; the port keeps D2R's check.

[plrmodes.md](../../pd2/plrmodes.md) put PD2's gate A on D2R's `0x429d10`. That function is an entry of D2R's mode table
(`0x141d18fb8`, stride 0x18) that requests neutral with no skill. D2R's gate is `0x42bfb0 (game, unit, requested
mode, the request's unit skill or null, flag)`: 0 allow, 1 refuse, 4 buffer (D2R's queued input). It switches on the
current mode (+0xc) like PD2's, and hands a busy player (modes 7, 8, 10-16, 18) to `0x42d840` with the same arguments,
which holds D2R's frame windows, `seqinput`, Concentration and bear rolls. `0x42de40` (the queued-command mode entry)
calls `0x42d840` with the queued skill, `0x42ced0` with none.

PD2's gate A (`0x10373290`), after its uninterruptable (state 54), dead and "flag 0 allows" steps, reads the current
skill's srvdofunc: 182 allows any request whose skill has a record; 48 refuses a request whose skill's srvdofunc is 48
too and allows any other. core-rules hooks `0x42d840` (entry `48 89 5c 24 08 48 89 6c 24 10 48 89 74 24 18`) and
applies those two rules (except that a request for the held skill itself goes to D2R's gate, see below)
when the request carries a skill, the requested mode is not death or dead and the player is
not uninterruptable; everything else goes to D2R's code. The skill id comes from `0x33e080`, srvdofunc from skills
+0x4e. Not covered: D2R's `flag` is not PD2's (it lets a neutral or walk request through `0x42bfb0` only), so PD2's
"flag 0 allows" step has no place here, and the client's own input handling is left as D2R has it.

  before its action frame (a hook on D2R's client do `0x216d20` saw Firestorm's calls, none for Arctic Blast). PD2 gets
  by with its event re-timing (`0x1037a7c0`); without it the rows keep D2R's seqinput 10 (`merge/standins.tsv`).
- D2R re-sends a held skill every frame: with "182 allows any skill" applied to it, the channel restarted ~30 times a

The window: D2R's frame counter is `Game+0x170` (`rva::GameFrame`), the game is `Unit+0xd8`. D2R has no playerdata field to spare and a unit stat is not allowed, so `pd2::parry::AvoidWindow` (`parry_roll.h`) keeps a 16-slot table of (player id, until frame) beside the hook, server thread only. An entry is live only while `0 < until - frame <= 4`, so a new game (frame counter restarted) or a passed window frees its slot at no cost, and a full table overwrites round-robin (`next_ % 16`), which cannot happen with 8 players. ## srvdo 164 (`0x103b25c0`): router 190

1. Sets the skill flag and takes the target from the caster's path; no target returns 0.
2. Rolls to-hit (the skill's ToHit), fills the damage and applies the melee hit (D2Game `0xded30`).
3. Fills a second block with the skill's damage and takes its poison as `poison * rolledLength / ELen` (D2Common
   #10510 is ELen with synergies).
4. `0x1036d250`: a ring of srvmissilea at the target's position, MissileParams flags 3 (placed at x/y, target an
   offset), one missile at every `64 / Param3`-th of D2's 64 directions (Param3 0 or over 64: 64), so Param3 10 makes 11
   missiles. Each gets the poison added to poisonmindam (57) and poisonmaxdam (58); stats 21, 22, 59 and 326 get 0.
5. Returns 1, whether or not the hit landed.

The srvdo table ends at 190 (core-rules-inventory Q1), so 164 joins the router (skill ids 73 and 550, Spider Boss).
core-rules runs D2R's own Poison Dagger do function (srvdo 32, `0x55cc50`: skill flag, target, apply the queued hit)
for steps 1-2, then step 4. The poison is `0x437d00` on a zeroed block: `+0x38` = min + rand(max - min), `+0x3c` = ELen.
Since the fill's length is ELen, PD2's rescale is a factor of 1 (approximated on the deviation list). D2R's direction
offsets are the int32 tables at `0x1d1b650` (x) and `0x1d1b750` (y), radius 30, the ones Nova's srvhit 5 aims at.

out of range is skipped). Returns 1 with no game, missile, row or valid state, 0 with no hit unit or owner, else
`2 + (row +0x186 != 0)` (1.13c's CollideKill; D2R's is `+0x1ae`, field table `0x3c4233`).
The result matters: D2R's missile collision (`0x4639a0`) calls the hit function through its table and builds and applies

## Golem start (PD2 srvst 74, `0x103b69d0`)

`(game, unit, skill, level)`: refuse unless the unit has a skill record with `+0x44` set; then `0x103746c0(game, unit, 1)`;
on 0 it sends the "can't" message (`0x1036d1b0(unit, 0x13, 0)`) and refuses the start.
`0x103746c0` (the golem count rule), on PD2's pet types (golem 28, irongolem 3):
1. limit = max of petmax(Clay Golem 75), petmax(Blood Golem 85), petmax(Fire Golem 94) (`0x103806d0(unit, skill)`);
3. While the player has golems (type 28) and their count >= limit, kill the oldest (`0x103a4660(unit, 28)`,
`0x10319ac0(game, unit, pet, 1)`).

Merged ids: pet type golem = **3** (D2R's own row, takes PD2's values), irongolem = **22** (appended). D2R's srvstfunc
table has 91 slots, 74 is empty. The golem rows' srvstfunc is a stand-in (blank) until this lands.
D2R: summon is `0x4350e0` (enforces petmax per pet type); golem do (srvdo 56) is `0x55c080`.
## Revive aura event (PD2 event 32, `0x10347370`)
the unit as an event (`0x103b2340`, the item-event cast). Revive's row has `auraevent1 domeleedamage`, so a revived
D2R: the aura event function table is `0x238e5c0`, 41 slots (dispatcher `0x43823a`, bound `cmp eax, 0x28`; lookup
`0x438f70`, `cmp ecx, 0x29`). Every slot 1-40 is filled. Slot 32 is `0x42eea0`, a skill damage event that is **not**
SkillNec code (`0x55b2d0`, `0x55b0c0`, `0x55b6a0`), Chilling Armor's 3 is `0x552a50`.

Merged id of `proc_SplashDamage`: **430** (PD2 358). Skills record: auraevent1-4 u16 `+0xa4..+0xaa`, auraeventfunc1-4
u16 `+0xac..+0xb2` (field table `0x302380`). The aura path copies both into the state list (`0x55c840`,
`0x55a7e0` -> `0x438370`).

Game check: D2R's Revive do (srvdo 58, `0x55e7e0`) never registers Revive's aura events on the revived monster; with
slot 32 filled, six revives fighting fallen never reached it. Golems get theirs elsewhere. The skill-event register
is srvst 66, `0x42fa90 (game, unit, skill, level)`: it reads auraevent1-4 / auraeventfunc1-4 of the skill and calls
`0x588670` then `0x438230 (game, unit, event, skill, level, ..., func, ...)` per event (the `0x438370` path does the
same for aura states). core-rules wraps srvdo 58 and calls it on the target after D2R's Revive: the corpse is revived
in place (same unit, return 1, mode neutral; the owner fields at `+0xe8` stay 0/0 for a pet). Then a revive's melee
hit fires event 5 (domeleedamage) into slot 32.

The event's cast (`0x5896e0` -> `0x589930`) of proc_SplashDamage returns 0: the skill has no do function yet ([W33](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/119)).
`0x589930` refuses a skill whose `ItemEffect` (`+0x20a`) is 0; proc_SplashDamage's is 1, so the refusal is later.
## Gate B (PD2 `0x1037bb20`)

- Current mode get-hit (4) or block (9): allow when `game frame + 2 >= end`, end = the unit's earliest type-1 timer
  (`0x103a4290(unit, 1)`, the mode-end event); else refuse.
- Current mode neutral (1) or run (3), requested cast (10) or sequence (18): refuse while
  `[PlayerData + 0x16c] + 5 > game frame`.

The stamp: 1.13c PlayerData ends at `+0x168` (`dwGameFrame`, written by the walk/run message handler at D2Game
`0xcc00d`; D2MOO's layout agrees), so `+0x16c` is past the vanilla struct. No store to `+0x16c` on a player data pointer
was found in `ProjectDiablo.dll`, `PD2_EXT.dll` or `D2Game.dll` (byte scan for every `+0x16c` operand; the only stores
are a client-side tick stamp at `0x1029260a`, a data-table field at `0x1036c21f` and a list head in D2Game). PD2's patch
table is not stored as plain `{dll, offset, ...}` records, so a byte patch into D2Game could not be ruled out.
D2R's mode change `0x429d10` is a rewrite (see [plrmodes](../../pd2/plrmodes.md)). Current mode 4, 9 or 19 goes through a
jump table at `0x42a2ca` (index bytes `0x42a5c8`, targets `0x42a5b8`): requested 9 and 19 keep the refusal; 1 checks
the unit first (`0x42a2e8`); the rest fall to `0x42a309`. Which of these allow needs a game check.

The install routine `0x1036bb1c` writes srvdo 157 = `0x103b1aa0` (D2Game do table, `+0x274`) and srvst 66 =

D2R fills all three slots (srvdo 157, srvst 66 `0x42fa90`, cltst 56 `0x2b67e0`), so the merge moves them: srvdo 157 to

`cost = max((double)(uint32)calc1 / 100.0 * life, calc2)`, truncated with `cvttsd2si`; life is stat 6 (hitpoints,
in 1/256). PD2's row: calc1 `12 - stat('blood_warp_life_reduction'.accr)` (percent of current life), calc2
`min(ln34 * 256, 15360)` with Param3 2, Param4 2 (2 life at level 1, 2 more per level, at most 60). calc1 is converted
as unsigned, so a reduction over 12 makes the product overflow to `INT32_MIN` and calc2 is the cost.

- srvst 66 and cltst 56: return 1 when `cost < life`, else 0 (the cast is refused). Same body on both sides.
- srvdo 157:
  1. PD2's teleport core `0x1036cd20(game, unit, 1)`, shared with Teleport's srvdo 155; return 0 if it fails.
  2. The cost again, at the new point; return 0 if `cost >= life`.
  3. Life = life - cost (`0x10307eb0`, stat 6).
  4. A timed state through PD2's helper `0x1036d7d0` with {owner, unit, skill, level, frames = auralencalc (125),
     stat = aurastat1 (hpregen), value = cost / frames + 1, state = aurastate (bloodwarp)}. The helper's
     curse-length branches (stats 109 / 504, states 58, 60, 89, 196) don't apply to bloodwarp. For a non-curse
     state it looks up the unit's list of that state (`0x1030c320`):
     - none, or another state or skill: build a new list (an old one is removed first, `0x1030c530`);
     - same skill, higher level: replace it;
     - same skill, lower level: return 0 and keep the old list (the life is already paid, no regen is added);
     - same skill and level (the usual recast): only move the old list's expiry to now + frames (`0x1030c4a0`,
       timer `0x103734a0`) and, for a player, send packet `0x83` with the new timer. The old regen value keeps
       running.
PD2's regen hook reads the bloodwarp list's value too ([plrmodes](../../pd2/plrmodes.md), life regen).

D2R's `NewStateList` (`0x433d20`) has vanilla's version of the same rule: it finds the unit's list of the state

match moves the expiry (`0x2f7ab0`, timer `0x48b720`) and returns the old list; a lower level returns null; anything

core-rules (`plugin/core-rules/skill_functions.cpp`): srvst 80 / cltst 63 are the cost check; the router's Blood Warp

The install routine `0x1036ba20` writes srvdo 180 = `0x103b4870` (do table `+0x2d0`), srvst 72 = `0x103b67e0` (start
table `+0x120`) and cltdo 112 = `0x103abfb0` (client do table `+0x1c0`); the client start routine `0x103ad290` writes
cltst 57 = `0x103ace50` (`+0xe4`). PD2's Charge row is the only one using these four numbers. Vanilla's are srvst 31,
srvdo 67, cltst 25, cltdo 37; D2R keeps them (`0x564dc0`, `0x5622c0`, `0x22e1a0`, `0x22d420`).
D2R leaves srvdo 180 and srvst 72 empty, so core-rules installs there. cltst 57 is D2R's (`0x2b68c0`); cltdo 112 is

1. **Start speed.** Both starts set the path speed to `base * (max(velocitypercent, 50) + Param1) / 100`, base the
   class's charstats byte (1.13c `+0x41`) `<< 8`. PD2 reads it for monsters too (indexed by the monster's id). D2R's
   client start (cltst 25) does the same with Param1 at skill `+0x1b8`; D2R's server start (srvst 31) adds **calc2**
   (`+0x194`) instead, which PD2's row leaves empty, so on merged data D2R's server charged at a third of PD2's speed
   while its client drew PD2's.
2. **Distance and splash.** The server start stores the distance from the caster to the path's first point in the
   skill's param (`0x103091d0`, D2R's unit skill `+0x24`): D2Common ordinal 10080 (`0x6fdcf5e0`), `max(dx, dy) +
   min(dx, dy) / 2`. On the hit (flag 1 clear, target in reach), before the damage is applied, if the caster has no
   `temp_skill_buff` (224, merged 270) list it gets one ending 3 frames later with `inc_splash_radius` (478, merged
   531) = `param / 4 * 20`, and the param goes back to 0.

The hit itself is vanilla's: damage% calc1 (1.13c `+0x138`, D2R `+0x190`), calc4 when the elemental byte is set, then
the damage apply and the target's 0x93 flag; D2R's srvdo 67 does the same calls (`0x44b600`, `0x44b2b0`, `0x349020`).

The client halves change nothing: cltdo 112 counts the param up to 2 like D2R's cltdo 37 (`+0x24`), and cltst 57 sets
the same speed as D2R's cltst 25.

- srvst 72 calls D2R's srvst 31, then, when it set off a charge (skill flags `0x1001`), sets PD2's speed (players from
  charstats `+0x3d`, monsters from monstats Run, as D2R's client does) and stores the distance to the skill's
  target point in `+0x24`. Any other start clears `+0x24`, so a charge cut short leaves no distance behind.
- srvdo 180, on the hit frame, asks what D2R's srvdo 67 asks before it strikes: its target (the skill's, `0x48fe80`,
  else the nearest, `0x4331d0`), in reach (`0x348650` with `0x34aa90`'s reach) and the caster alive (`0x34c2c0`). When
  the hit goes off it builds the splash list (unless the caster already has a `temp_skill_buff` list) and spends the
  distance, then calls D2R's srvdo 67.
- The merge points the client columns at D2R's 25 and 37 (`tools/pd2_port.py` FUNCS).

Deviation (approximated, on the deviation list): the distance is measured to the skill's target point, not the path's first point; a monster's speed is its monstats Run (D2R's Charge reads `+0x6a`, Run).

PD2's gate A ([plrmodes](../../pd2/plrmodes.md)) keys on `srvdofunc`: Charge (67 and 180) and Whirlwind (76) allow the same skill
again, and PD2 also lets requests with no skill through to gate B (frame check for the sequence mode). D2R's mode
change (`0x429d10`) keys on skills.txt flags instead (skill `+0x24` & 0x10, `+0x27` & 0x80, `+0x36`), and the merged
Charge and Whirlwind rows have the same flags, so Charge stays in Whirlwind's group with srvdo 180. A skill-less request
during either one reads as queued until the last 2 frames of the sequence in the decompile; PD2's frame-check window
is not compared. Not checked in game: the plugin does not log mode changes. Approximated row on the deviation list.

records.excerpt: The install routine `0x1036ba20` writes srvdo 176 = `0x103b3cc0` (D2Game do table `+0x2c0`). D2R's 176 is empty.

1. The skill record (null: 0). The caster's path target, after `0xe07a0` refreshes it; none: return 1.
2. Heal min/max = cltcalc2 / cltcalc3 `<< 8` (1.13c skill `+0x118`, `+0x11c`; D2R `+0x170`, `+0x174`). Damage
   min/max = the skill's elemental min/max with synergies.
3. When the target is hostile to the caster the heal is halved, otherwise the damage.
4. D2Game's area search around the target with radius aurarangecalc (`+0x64`, D2R `+0x84`), unit mask aurafilter
   (`+0x50`, D2R `+0x70`; 0 is the search's default `0x583`) and callback `0x103043b0`.
5. srvoverlay (`+0x4e`, D2R `+0x6e`) on the target. Returns 1.

Callback `0x103043b0`, per unit: the caster is skipped. An ally heals min + rand(max - min) on the caster's seed and
gets overlay 26. Anything else takes a 0x70-byte damage block: result flags 1, or 9 (knockback) for an undead monster
that is not the target; magic (`+0x20`, D2R `+0x30`) = min + rand(max - min); PD2's apply `0x10305760`.
`0x10305760` is 1.13c's area apply: avoid roll, the same result-flag edits, state 0x36, damage step, events (area 1),
deal. D2R's area apply `0x436e90` does the same steps, so core-rules calls it.

Hostile (`0xe0a60`): pets and missiles are swapped for their owners; the same unit is not hostile; two players ask the
PvP state; otherwise D2Common #10666, which reads #10830's alignment (0 hostile, 1 neutral, 2 ally, other types 2) and
calls two units allied when both are 0 or both 2. D2R keeps #10830 as `0x2f4190`; pets carry alignment 2.

Holy Light's row: cltcalc2 `ln12 + Prayer blvl * par6`, cltcalc3 `ln34 + Prayer blvl * par7`, aurarangecalc 6,
EType mag, srvoverlay valkyriestart, cltdofunc 36 (D2R's own, the same as Fist of the Heavens'), cltmissilea
holylightdelay. srvmissilea holylight is not read by srvdo 176.

PD2's missile install `0x103a6c50` writes clthit 66 = `0x103a69c0` (D2Client table `[0x105e1364]`); D2R's 66 is
empty. On a hit: with the missile's owner and its CltHitSubMissile1 (1.13c `+0x2c`, D2R `+0x4e`) a valid row, the
client area search around the missile with radius cHitPar1 and callback `0x103a6bd0` puts that missile on each unit
(flags 0x22, the unit as origin and target, the row's Skill and the missile's level), skipping the unit hit. Returns 1.
PD2 leaves clthit 26 vanilla: 1.13c D2Client `0xbad40`, read from the install's table at `0xdda10`. D2R's 26 is
`0x1adcb0`. Both: the missile's HitSubMissile1 must be set; owner, skill and level from the missile; zero when the

- **The limit.** Both compute cHitPar2, else calc4. 1.13c overwrites the result before storing it, so its callback
  (`0x6fb663c0`) compares the unit count against an unset stack slot and creates no bolt once that slot is not above
  the count.
  D2R stores it (at least 1) and creates at most that many. Fist of the Heavens' calc4 is ln12 = 50.
- **The struck unit.** D2R's callback (`0x1bc380`) aims the bolt for the missile's target unit at the caster; 1.13c
  aims it at the unit.
- D2R also sets the unit as the missile's target and passes UnitStateKey of the delay missile (`+0x68`); core-rules
  keeps D2R's key (1.13c's parameter block has no such field) and leaves the target unset, as 1.13c does.

3. A second block, result flags 1, for the burst:
   - per element E (fire 48/49, cold 54/55, lightning 50/51): min/max = the caster's stat total less the same stat on
     its lists of states holyfire 35 and enchant 16 (fire), holywind 43 and coldenchant 188 (cold; merged 223), holyshock 46
     (lightning); pct = calc1/calc2/calc3 + passive_fire/cold/ltng_mastery (329/331/330);

(`plugin/core-rules/skill_functions.cpp`), which calls a PD2 do function by skill id. It is ours, not D2RLoader's.
The prg functions can't share it with srvdo 170. The release dispatcher calls them with the charge-up skill's
own id, which the router already maps to the 170 port. So they need real slots. D2R's free 172-190 are all used or
planned. 181 (TorajanBossNest) and 184-186 (the Lucion kit) are after-the-cut monster do functions, each with its own
skill id, so they are still built (after the cut), as router cases instead of in their own slots, and their slots
go to the four prg functions. Until then their stand-ins (`merge/standins.tsv`) keep those monsters' srvdofunc off
181 and 184-186. 188 is avoided: item casts need it empty (`ItemEffect`).

6. Returns 1. D2R's collision (`0x4639a0`) deals the missile's own damage only on bit 2, so the struck unit takes
   only the splash.

Callback `0x10304a90`: copies the block (one roll for every unit), and with a missile owner (type 3) and a player
victim sets the victim's player data `+0x194` to the missile's skill for the apply; then PD2's area apply
`0x10305760`, which [w17-holy-light](w17-holy-light.md) found equal to D2R's AreaApply `0x436e90`. A missile owner is
never a missile, so that branch is not taken.

D2R missile record: HitFlags `+0xd0` (u32), ResultFlags `+0xd4` (u16), 1.13c + 0x28, read from the missiles field
table built by `0x3c2c70`.

Deviation (approximated, on the deviation list): no physical damage (none of the four skills has MinDam/MaxDam) and no
missile in the block. PD2's deal step reads block `+0x5c` for a missile kill; D2R's block has no field found for it.
PD2 `0x10346020 (game, event, unit, attacker, ?, skill, level)` and D2R `0x552a50` do the same:

| apply | PD2's event pass (area 1) `0x10305990`, deal `0x103025b0` | HitEvents `0x44ce80` (area 1), DealDamage `0x44a9b0` |
| overlay | the skill's srvoverlay on the attacker | the same |
| damage | the skill's elemental damage at max(level, 1) from the unit | the same (`0x437d00`) |

Answers work item [W29](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/104) ([#104](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/104)), on the slots [w25-assassin-finishers](w25-assassin-finishers.md) chose. PD2 side read
from `ProjectDiablo.dll` (VAs `0x10...`) and PD2's 1.13c `D2Game.dll` (RVAs named "D2Game") in the PD2 Ghidra
project, D2R side from the 93847 dump (`ImageStamp 0x6ab3782c`); other addresses are D2R RVAs. Read statically.

- **Shared charges (`0x1036ee80`)**: confirmed. For each progressive state (data tables `+0x16c`, count `+0x170`) the
  unit has a list of, it reads the list's skill (stat 350), that skill's `aurastat1`, and the list's value of it. It
  returns the highest, clamped to 0-3.
- **Release dispatcher**: PD2 does not hook it. Its version table holds 1.13c's release (D2Game `0x91b70`) once
  (`0x104a90f4`), read by an address accessor (`0x1031b5b0`) whose one user is a call wrapper (`0x103a1b20`) that two
  PD2 do functions (`0x103af640`, `0x103b4180`) call. So the finishers release through D2R's own `SrvPrgDispatch`
  (`0x56c3e0`), which does what 1.13c's does ([W25](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/100)). Both its prg calls pass the level in R9, so a prg function gets
  `(game, unit, skill, level)` whether the release or srvdo 170 calls it.
- **The 139 missile helper**: `[0x105e08b0]` is resolved from version table entry `0x104a91a4` to D2Game `0x91340`,
  vanilla's charge missile: a skill with charges gets srvmissilea/b/c for 1/2/3+ charges, any other skill
  srvmissilea. D2R has the same function (`PickSkillMissile`, `0x571700`, used by D2R's srvdo 37). D2R's own 139
  (`0x585440`) takes srvmissilea (`+0x68`), so the four monster rows on 139 get the same missile from both: the
  core-rules `verify` row is data.
- **The Cobra Strike branch of 171/172** (skill 265 only, not RakanothStrike): it fills a hit's damage block for the
  skill and adds its poison, scaled by its rolled length over ELen (D2Common #10510, version entry `0x104a8b1c`), to
  each missile's poisonmindam and poisonmaxdam (`0x1036e500`). As in Poison Dagger ([W11](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/86)), the port takes the
  skill's rolled poison from D2R's fill, whose length is ELen, so the scale is 1.
## srvdo 170 (`0x103b2c60`): router 190

1. Shared charges (above). At 3 every progressive list is freed and the count is 0.
2. The target is the path's target unit (not the caster); `0x103049e0(unit, target, 5)` must pass. For a player
   target, `0x1037c820` sets a flag that lets results with `0x8390` count as hits.
3. Roll: to-hit = the skill's ToHit (`0x1030b960`) + the unit's progressive_tohit (stat 325).
4. On a hit (bit 0, and the player flag or none of `0x8390`): charges are added (PD2's AddCharge copy `0x1036efe0`)
   while this skill's count is at most the shared one, so it ends at the shared count + 1. Cobra Strike and
   RakanothStrike (`aurastat1` 319, `progressive_steal`), at the 2nd charge: a stat list (flags 4, until frame + 3, no
   state or event) with lifedrainmindam and manadrainmindam = calc1 and damagepercent = calc2.
5. Vanilla `0x922a0(unit, block)` (progressive states whose record byte `+0x44` is 1), the damage fill
   (`0x1031b4a0`), then vanilla `0x91e30(unit)` (types 2-4) when the count is 1 and the skill isn't Cobra Strike, and
   the queue (`0x103a1630`). Vanilla runs those two only in its release; their per-type bodies (D2Game `0x91f10`,
   `0x91400`, `0x91a30`, `0x918d0`) are not read.
6. Hit after the fill: srvprgfunc[min(charges, 3)] through the do table (bound 191) as (game, unit, skill, level),
   then the charge packet (`0x103a1c40`: target, unit, skill, level, the unit's next random number with the seed
   left as it was, 0, n), which is the release packet. Miss: the charges added in step 4 are taken back and an empty
   list is removed. Then the hit is applied (D2Game `0x10310eb0`).
**Port.** D2R's srvdo 34 (`0x570a70`) is the same hit with one charge: target, to-hit (`0x339040`), roll
(`0x44b720`), queue (`0x44b600`), `AddCharge` (`0x56dae0`, D2R's copy of step 4's adder: list with stats 350/351,
timer, +1 up to 3, aurastat2) when the queued hit has bit 0, apply (`0x44b2b0`). core-rules' `SrvDoChargeUp` does
sends `SendChargePacket` (`0x5396d0`). Building the hit in core-rules would mean rebuilding srvdo 34's damage block

- **171 -> 184** (`0x103b30a0`): prgcalc[charge] (1.13c `+0x38`, D2R `SkPrgCalc1` `+0x58`) missiles of the charge
  missile, flags `0x10820` (D2R's CreateMissile reads `0x10000` as 1.13c's does: it goes with params `+0x64` to the
  missile's setup `0x3bf9b0`), 1.13c params `+0x44` = 1, from the caster to points along PD2's spread (`0x1037d780`):
  Multiple Shot's line through the target, stepping the other way, with PD2's own slip for a target within 2 subtiles
  (`ChargeSpread`).
- **172 -> 185** (`0x103b3360`): PD2's ring (`0x1036d250`, the one Poison Dagger uses) of prgcalc[charge] (64 for
  every user) of the charge missile at the target's position, or the caster's with no target, flags 3.
- **39 -> 186** (`0x103aee00`): vanilla srvdo 38, then 39 (D2R's 38 `0x56ef30`, 39 `0x571860`).
- **139 -> 181** (`0x103b0cf0`): D2R's 139 with the charge missile (Blades of Ice's charge 2: srvmissileb,
  boiwavemaker).
All four read the charge with PD2's `0x1037ddf0` rule (the list's aurastat1 value, run only at 1-3).

`tools/pd2_port.py` FUNCS: srvdofunc 170 -> 190; srvprgfunc1-3 171 -> 184, 172 -> 185, 39 -> 186, 139 -> 181 (only
the finishers use those values there). The stand-ins (`merge/standins.tsv`) keep only the client columns
(cltprgfunc1-3) for [W30](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/105).

Answers work item [W30](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/105) ([#105](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/105)), on the slots [w25-assassin-finishers](w25-assassin-finishers.md) chose. PD2 side read
from `ProjectDiablo.dll` (VAs `0x10...`) and PD2's 1.13c `D2Client.dll` / `D2Common.dll` (RVAs named "D2Client",
"D2Common") in the PD2 Ghidra project, D2R side from the 93847 dump (`ImageStamp 0x6ab3782c`); other addresses are D2R
RVAs. PD2 reaches vanilla code through version-table thunks (module index, offset in column 0 for 1.13c), resolved
here by reading the table entries. Read statically.
D2R's handler for the charge/release packet (`0x216380`, which the server's `SendChargePacket` feeds on each

- **cltprg 106 (`0x103ab920`) -> cltdo 127**: the client half of srvprg 171. The charge (PD2's `0x1037ddf0`, run only
  at 1-3), the client missile (1.13c D2Client `0x40550` through `[0x105e0a08]`: cltmissilea/b/c for 1/2/3 charges,
  cltmissilea for a skill without), and cltcalc[charge] (1.13c `+0x114`, D2R `+0x16c`) missiles. The aim is the
  path's target unit (D2Common #10392), else the path's target point. Params as the server's: flags `0x10820`,
  owner and origin the caster, start at the caster, 1.13c `+0x44` = 1, aim points along PD2's spread (`0x1037d780`,
  core-rules' `ChargeSpread`). A do-while: at least one missile.
- **cltprg 107 (`0x103aba80`) -> cltdo 128**: the client half of srvprg 172. The same charge, missile and count, then
  PD2's client ring (`0x1036d370`, the server ring's twin: flags 3, the count 0 or over 64 makes 64, one missile at
  every 64/count-th of the 64 directions) at the target unit's position, else the caster's.
- **cdo 69 (`0x103a60d0`) -> cdo 79** (fistsoffireexplode, bladesoficecubes): first the missile's step (1.13c
  D2Client `0xb17c0`, the body almost every vanilla client do function calls; D2R's cltdo 1), then, when the
  missile's frame counter (D2Common #10737, data `+0x10`, counting down) equals its range (#10534, `+0xe`) - 1, its
  `CltSubMissile1` (fistsoffirefirewall, bladesoficeexplode) placed at its position (flags 3, no aim), with the
  missile's skill (`+0xa`) and level (`+0xc`). That is the missile's **first** frame, not its last as [W25](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/100) read it.
  D2R's `0x3bb0f0` returns the range minus the frames left, and D2R's own cltdo 1 tests it for 1 the same way.
- **chit 67 (`0x103a6aa0`)** (clawsofthunderbolt): on a hit unit, `CltHitSubMissile1` (cotthunderstorm) placed at the
  unit hit (D2Client `0x1630` / `0x1660` on it; flags 1), with the row's `Skill` and the missile's level. On the new
  missile it sets the graphic's height to `CHitCalc1` (280, "z height offset") through 1.13c D2Client `0xc7e30`
  (`[0x105e0608]`; gfx `+0x30` `+0xc`, << 11), and writes `cHitPar1-3` (0, 0, -81920, "movement offset * 256") raw to
  the graphic's motion (`+0x10..0x18`): the storm bolt falls from above onto the unit. Returns 1.

D2R's Meteor client do (cltdo 9, `0x1b6480`) is 1.13c's (`0xb8f00`) and makes the same two writes on its falling
meteor: `0x193a80(missile, x, y, z)` stores the offset << 11, and `0x193ad0(missile, x, y, z, shift)` the motion,
shifted with `shift` set, raw without. So chit 67 is built exactly: `SetMissileOffset(bolt, 0, 0, calc)` and
`SetMissileMotion(bolt, cHitPar1, cHitPar2, cHitPar3, 0)`. `CHitCalc1` is at D2R `+0xb0` (1.13c `+0x8c` + 0x24, as
the cHitPar and DmgCalc fields move), `CltSubMissile1` at `+0x40` (D2R's cltdo 9 reads it there).

Answers work item [W31](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/106) ([#106](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/106)). PD2 side read from `ProjectDiablo.dll` (VAs `0x10...`) and PD2's 1.13c `D2Game.dll`
(RVAs named "D2Game") in the PD2 Ghidra project, D2R side from the 93847 dump (`ImageStamp 0x6ab3782c`); other
addresses are D2R RVAs. Read statically.

The install routine `0x1036ba20` writes srvdo 178 = `0x103b4180` (D2Game do table `+0x2c8`). D2R's 178 is empty. Only
Dragon Flight uses it. `(game, unit, skill, level)`:

1. The skill record (null: 0). The target is the unit's path target (`0x103096b0(unit + 0x2c)`); none: 0.
2. The teleport core `0x1036cd20(game, unit, 0)` (Teleport's, [sorceress-w26](sorceress-w26.md); the 0 skips the Hell
   level set, which is never filled); a refusal returns 0, with no kick.
3. A zeroed 0x70-byte damage block. To-hit = the skill's (`0x1030b960`) + the unit's progressive_tohit (stat 325).
4. The melee roll (`0x103048a0(target, unit, game, to-hit, 0)`: no always-hit). On a hit: damage% (block `+0x0c`) =
   **calc2** (`+0x13c`), then the melee fill (`0x103a1bc0`).
5. The queue (`0x103a1630`, flag `0x80`), the release (`0x103a1b20`, 1.13c's `0x91b70`: srvprgfunc for the charges,
   [w29-assassin-finishers](w29-assassin-finishers.md)), the hit (`0x10310eb0`).
6. PD2's aurastate helper `0x1036cb90(game, unit, unit, skill, level, 1, 0)`: a stat list of aurastat1-6 with
   aurastatcalc1-6 for auralencalc frames. It returns before anything when aurastat1 is empty, as on PD2's Dragon
   Flight row. Returns 1.

PD2's row: calc2 `ln12` (Param1 100, Param2 25: 100 + 25 per level after the first), anim `KK` (one do frame),
srvstfunc 12, no aurastate or aurastat.

**D2R's own (srvdo 52, `0x56fc80`)** splits the cast over two do frames, on a counter in the unit's data (`+0x24`):
the even call clears the unit's skill flag and teleports (`SkillTargetXY`, the level's `Teleport` column, collision
`0x804` when 2, `0x491ca0`); the odd call kicks: to-hit `0x339040(unit, skill, level)` + stat 325, roll
`0x44b720(game, unit, target, to-hit, always, 0)` with always-hit from Param8 (`0x574070`), damage% (block `+0x1c`) =
**calc1**, fill `0x573af0(game, &block, unit, target, skill, level)`, queue `0x44b600(..., skill +0x24d or 0x80)`,
release (`SrvPrgDispatch` on `QueuedHit`), hit `0x44b2b0(game, unit, target, 0, 1)`, then the skill flag back on
while the caster lives, and the block's cleanup. The block has `d2r::LeapKnockback`'s layout (list `+0x40`, tagged
pointer `+0x158`).

PD2's server missile install `0x103a7220` writes srvdmg 15-19 (D2Game table `[0x105e1648]`, `+0x3c`): 15 =
`0x103a6c90`. Only psychichammer uses it in PD2. D2R's 15 is Holy Bolt's (holybolt, fistoftheheavensbolt), so ours
takes 22 (20 and 21 are [W6](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/53)'s and [W9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/55)'s; 18 and 19 stay for PD2's own).
`0x103a6c90(game, missile, target, damage)`: with the missile's row and skill valid and its owner (`0x103749f0`):
Lightning's chain, 1.13c D2Game `0x3d020`, D2R `0x45d5e0`) throws the next hammer with one bounce less, so the k-th
**Is it reached?** Only D2R's srvhit 1 (`0x45bc40`) references the dmg table in Ghidra's xrefs, but D2R's collision
(`0x4639a0`) also calls `[0x2391270 + n*8]` (a computed call the xrefs list misses): after the row's srvhit, when its
result has bit 2, it builds the damage (`0x465420`), calls the row's dmg function and deals it (`0x462e40`). 1.13c does
the same in `0x3ede0`. srvhit 12 returns 3 on a hit in both, so dmg 22 runs on every hammer hit.

Answers work item [W32](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/107) ([#107](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/107)). PD2 side read from `ProjectDiablo.dll` (VAs `0x10...`) and the 1.13c `D2Game.dll`,
`D2Client.dll` and `D2Common.dll` in the Ghidra project `PD2.gpr`, D2R side from the 93847 dump (`ImageStamp
0x6ab3782c`). Addresses are D2R RVAs unless they start with `0x10`; 1.13c addresses are offsets in their DLL.

PD2's missile installs write srvhit 34 = `0x103a7c70` (`0x103a9170`, table `+0x88`), clthit 6 = `0x103a6530`
(`0x103a6c50`, `+0x18`) and srvdmg 19 = `0x103a7130` (`0x103a7220`, `+0x4c`). D2R fills srvhit 34 (echoingstrike);
clthit 6 is below D2R's free range (66 on), so the merge moves them to 69 and 68 (`tools/pd2_port.py` FUNCS). dmg 19
is free.

Constants: `0x1044fa48` 1.0, `0x1044fbd0` 64 / 2π, `0x1044fc9c` 64.0. Create flags `0x22`: from the origin unit (the
fragment), aimed at an offset (D2R's create reads them the same way).

- **A wall** (no unit): only when frames left <= the activate frame, >= 2 and < the range, the fragment's own subtile
  collides (mask `0x806`, its size + 1) and it has a path. n = owner -> fragment, normalised. For each of n fragments,
  offsets -((n - 1) / 2) * step, step apart: n reflected off normal (1, 0) first (x negated, a
  vertical wall), else off (0, 1) (y negated) (atan2 in D2's 64 directions, + the
  offset); the first mirror whose point `size` subtiles ahead is free gives a HitSubMissile1 fragment aimed at that
  direction's table offset, with generation + 1 and frames max(left - drop, 0), at least cHitPar1 on generation 0,
  0 under cHitPar2. Then the parent's frames are set to 0. Returns 0.
- **A unit**: one `rand()`. When its `% 100` is under min(Param1, 100), n - 1 fragments at directions (`rand & 63`) +
  offsets from -((n - 2) / 2) * step, the value growing by 0x11 per fragment; each with generation + 1, frames
  max(left - drop, 0) (0 under cHitPar2), and sent to every client.

`(game, missile, target, damage)`, for a missile: life, mana and stamina leech (1.13c `+0x38-0x40`, D2R `+0x120-0x128`)
times dParam2 / 100 (unsigned). Then a `rand() % 100` over dParam1 sets result flag 0x20 (`+0x04`) and, on a fragment
whose generation is not 0, zeroes the leech.

Both halves take a direction as a signed `% 64` (`and 0x8000003f` with the sign fix): a negative index reads before
the tables. 1.13c keeps the y table right before the x table, so x reads y's tail (-2 to -14) and y reads the bytes
before it (0, -1, 1, 1, -1): the fragment leaves roughly west where directions 59-63 point east. With PD2's row a wall
bounce's first fragment and a split's are offset -5; it happens whenever the mirrored direction is under 5. core-rules
wraps the index (docs/pd2/origin-bugs.md).
entry, D2Game `0x9dcd0`, never sends a missile, so the send must be explicit). They hit; another client draws them

records.excerpt: ## The cast stamp at PlayerData + 0x16c

Every `+0x160`-`+0x174` operand in `ProjectDiablo.dll` that is not on the stack was listed (FindDispRange). The only
store to a player data `+0x16c` is `0x102925a0`, and it is client code:

- it reads the client's own player (`[[0x105d6c78]]`, a unit of type 0) and its player data (`+0x14`);
- it stores `GetTickCount() + 250` (milliseconds, not game frames) at `+0x16c`, counts calls in `+0x174`, and sends a
  `0x5b` message (`0x103a1cd0` -> `[0x105e083c]`) with 2 on the first call and 0 when a 250 ms window passes 200
  calls; then it calls the hooked function (`0x10325280`). It has no static caller: PD2 installs it as a hook.

The server's player data is a different block from the client's (1.13c's single player keeps separate server and
client units), and no store to it was found in `ProjectDiablo.dll`, `PD2_EXT.dll` or `D2Game.dll`
([necromancer-w14](necromancer-w14.md)). So on the server gate B compares the game frame with a field nothing
writes: a zeroed block reads 0, and `0 + 5 > frame` only holds in a game's first 5 frames. By this reading
PD2's single-player server never delays a cast from neutral or run; no runtime read of PD2 confirms it. Its online servers run their own build, which this install does not
ship, so a writer there can't be ruled out. 1.13c's own player data ends at `+0x168`; the server allocation size in
`D2Game.dll` was not found, so whether `+0x16c` lies inside the block is not settled. A read past the block would
give the neighbouring heap bytes, and a large value there would refuse every cast, which players would have noticed.
D2R allows every request from neutral (`0x42bfb0`, case 1 and 5), so it already does what PD2's single-player server
## D2R's get-hit/block gate (`0x42d700`)
`0x42bfb0 (game, unit, mode, unit skill, flag)` hands current modes 4, 9 and 19 (knockback) to `0x42d700 (game, unit,
requested mode, flag byte)`. A flag that is not 0 only reaches it for a neutral request (`0x42bfb0` refuses the rest
- requested 4: refused (except one knockback case, `0x343240` on the unit's `0x34ae80` returning 0), 9 and 19 refused;
- requested 2, 3 or 6 (walk, run, town walk): buffered (4) while `end - frame > 1` (`cmp eax,1` at `0x42d7d0`);
- anything else: refused while `end - frame > 1` (`cmp eax,1` at `0x42d806`);
- refused outright when the unit is in knockback (`0x34ab60` is 19).
end is `0x48b230 (game, unit, 1, 0)`, the earliest type-1 timer, 0 when there is none. So D2R opens the window one
`0x429d10`, the path the issue named, is the mode-table entry for a neutral request, not the gate
([druid-w21](druid-w21.md)); its jump table at `0x42a2ca` was not read again here.
The install writes 2 over both immediates (`0x42d7d2`, `0x42d808`) and hooks `0x42d700` only to log the result per

- a get-hit, block or knockback request in get-hit/block is refused; PD2 allows it in the window;
- a walk or run request outside the window is buffered (D2R's queue) where PD2 refuses it;
- a neutral (1) or town-neutral (5) request with flag 0 is refused outside the window; PD2 always allows it;
- D2R's client holds a request made in get-hit and sends it when its own window opens: every request the server
  saw came at 1 frame left (below). So in single player the 2-frame window is not reached. PD2's own client most
  likely does the same (below), so this is listed but not counted as a deviation.
  The client side was not found. What is ruled out:
  - the server does not hold the request: temporary logs on `0x42d020` (StartMode, entry `4c 8b dc 4d 89 43 18 53
    55 56 57 41 54 41 55`) saw every request made in get-hit come from the skill message handler (`0x4f8de0`, return
    `0x4f8f66`) with 1 frame left, so the message itself arrives then. `0x4fdca0`, which `0x42d020` calls first, is
    skill validation (its `0x4249f0` test is not a mode test), not a queue;
  - the client's held command (`D2Client\src\Unit\UnitMode.cpp`; stored in the client player data `+0x1c8`-`+0x1d4`
    by `0xf9680`, `0xfbef0` and the click handlers such as `0x1017b0`, released by `0xf9bc0` every client frame
    from `0x8b3c0` and `0x94b40`) is the "move, then act" follow-up and has no frame test;
  - the sender `0xfabe0` skips only for a skill flag (`0xffac0`), not for get-hit.
  So the hold comes from the client's own player mode: the local get-hit animation ending, one frame before the
  server's mode end.

PD2's client most likely holds the same way. 1.13c's `D2Client.dll` has the same `..\Source\D2Client\UNIT\UnitMode.cpp`:
  `0x2a7c0` is D2R's `0xf9bc0`/`0xfabe0` pair, with the held command at player data `+0x150`-`+0x15c` (D2R
  `+0x1c8`-`+0x1d4`), and `0x29f30` lets a skill through only from neutral or town neutral. A scan for code
  comparing one value with both 4 and 9 within six instructions finds no get-hit/block test in 1.13c's client
  (`0x69660` walks a skill list) or in `ProjectDiablo.dll` (only gate B and `0x102fcb40`, an item count fill).
  So PD2 did not patch its client here, and its 2-frame server window is most likely not reached from a player's
  input there either: the client hold is not a deviation. Not confirmed in a running PD2, and `PD2_EXT.dll` is not
  in the Ghidra project, so it was not scanned.

`hit-window` (tag core-rules-w34). Run on Slot8 (2026-11-04, Hell, level 95 Assassin, god mode, Blood Moor, six Venom
Lords (`megademon3`) and eight zombies, attacking and casting while they hit): all three checks passed (again on Slot6 after [W19](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/94) landed: level 90 Paladin, 60/60 parts installed); the window
lines read `1 frames left: 0` (attack, skill 4 and sequence requests). A temporary log on `0x42bfb0` saw five
requests while the player was in get-hit, every one at 1 frame left, none earlier: the client holds them.
A request at 1 frame left is allowed with or without the patch, so the check shows the hook and the window's results,
not the 2-frame patch itself, which the install checks by its bytes. The cast delay has no game check: nothing is
ported for it.

records.excerpt:
`calc3 + 0x10381720(unit, 478) / 20`, minus 1 when the weapon (`0x103309b0`, D2Game) has a record (`0x103072e0`)
whose `+0x80` (code) equals `+0x84` (normcode), that is, a normal-tier base.

`0x10381720` reads every layer of stat 478 (`inc_splash_radius`) from the unit's full stat list (D2Common #10702). It
skips layer 0. It adds a layer's value when the wielded weapon (#10061) is of the item type the layer names (#10744).
The masteries put their passive stats on their passiveitype's layer: One Hand Mastery on 1han, Two Hand Mastery on
2han. The 1han and 2han layers also check the other hand (#10417 body location, #11139 item at a body location,
#10747 can dual wield, that is, a Barbarian or an Assassin):
### Room check (`0x1037c820`)

It refuses when the unit's level (`path->room->roomEx->level->+0x1d0`) is 157, 159 or 166: Pvp Map, Pvp Map 2 and BR
Arena (`0x1037c7b0`).
### Callback (`0x10303190`), per unit

1. Result flags = 1 (no to-hit roll) | the skill's; damage% and hit class from the block; hit flags = the skill's.
2. Smite (97) by a player: `0x103060c0`, the shield's damage (record `+0xfe`/`+0xff` × 256, plus state 101's stats)
   through D2Game `0x103a4480`, hit flags |= 2, hit class 0x65. The kicks (255, 270, 275): the first queued combat
   entry's damage (`[unit+0xac]+0x14`, 0x70 bytes) replaces the block. Every other skill clears hit flag 2.
3. Concentrate (144) with an EType: conversion type = EType (`+0x1dc`), percent = calc4 (`+0x144`).
4. D2Game `+0x9f210`: the skill's elemental damage. D2Game `+0x9f1a0`: its physical damage. Then D2Game `+0xddde0`:
   weapon damage at SrcDam.
5. Life leech / 2 (at least 1). A player victim's data `+0x194` = the skill id. Apply: `0x10305880`, with flag 0.

The 1.13c physical fill `0x9f1a0` adds `min + rand(max - min)` (D2Common #10567 / #10297 with `(unit, skill, level,
0)`, the unit's seed at `+0x20`) to the damage's `+0x08`.
### Handlers skipped (`0x10305c30` -> walker `0x10347510`)
The apply passes flag 0, so the walker gets the handler set `0x105dc628` (built by `0x10111890`). It holds item event
358, set `0x105dc5c8`). Those would be a splash inside a splash, which core-rules already refuses.

- Current skill: `CurrentSkill` (0x34ba40), `UnitSkillId`, `UnitSkillLevel` (0x33d1e0, bonus 0 = hard points; the
  srvdo dispatcher 0x43acb0 calls it with 1).
- Elemental fill: `ElementalDamage` (0x437d00), as D2R's melee start (srvst 32, 0x567070) uses it.
- Physical fill: no D2R function adds it alone. core-rules adds `SkillPhysMin` (0x3385b0) + a roll below
  `SkillPhysMax` (0x338160) - min, on `UnitSeed`, to `DmgPhys`. Those are the min/max pair D2R's kick fill (0x573af0)
  reads.
- Concentrate: D2R's melee start sets the same conversion for a skill with an EType: type at +0x149 and calc4 at
  +0x14c (1.13c's +0x65 / +0x68).
- Kicks: `QueuedHit(attacker, struck)`; core-rules copies the block's plain fields (+0x00-0x40, +0x118-0x158), not its
  list.
- Radius: `UnitWeapon`, `ItemIsType` for each itemtypes row (count at DataTables +0x1350, ItemIsType's bound) and
  `UnitStat(unit, inc_splash_radius, type)`. Normal base: `ItemRecord` (0x314110) code +0x80 vs normcode +0x84 (items
  field table in 0x315fd0).
- Skipped handlers: nothing to port. Item event functions 14 (0x583580) and 20 (0x583b30) are reached only through
  `AuraEventTable` slots 14 and 20 (Ghidra's other reference to 0x583b30 is `.pdata`). The splash itself runs inside
  slot 20 (item_splashonhit), and its hits' event 5 never reaches slot 14 or 20: a test build wrapped both slots,
  and over Frenzy and attack splashes with Bladebone (40% Teeth on striking) the wrappers never ran during a splash.
  The walker (`0x5881e0`) jumps outside the dump, so whether it also drops other domeleedamage handlers on splashed
  units (crushing blow, open wounds, which PD2 fires) is not known.

- Smite's splash takes Smite's own skill damage. PD2 deals its shield damage and adds a state 224 list with
  inc_splash_radius = skill `+0x158`.
- The radius counts the layers of the weapon's own item types. PD2's off-hand rules for 1han and 2han are left out:
  D2R's item-at-body-location (0x3885e0) treats weapons in slots 5 and 6 specially and is not decoded.
- A player victim's last-hit skill (1.13c's `+0x194`) is not written.
- The room check is left out: it refuses only the PvP maps, which are cut, as for [W9](https://github.com/synpoox/pd2-resurrected/issues/55)'s bounce.

PD2's table fill `0x1036ba20` writes srvdo 173 = `0x103b3520`, srvdo 181 = `0x103b4cf0` (D2Game do table `[0x105de8fc]`),
cltdo 109 = `0x103abba0` (`[0x105de71c]`) and srvst 67 = `0x103b6520` (start table `[0x105de8ec]`). Its server missile

`0x103b3520(game, unit, skill, level)` calls the do table's slot 22 with the same arguments, then slot 84 with skill

1. The skill record (`0x1037c110`) and the unit's current skill (`0x1030dd00`); none: 0.
2. `0x1037b990(game, unit, 1)`, D2R's `RemoveUnitEvent` (`0x48b890`) as D2R's Nest calls it.
3. A monster with 1.13c AI data (`unit+0x14 -> +0x28`) only. Its counter (`+0x1c` there) below Param1 (`+0x148`),
   else 0.
4. `0x103104e0(unit, 0)` (D2R `0x48e820`), then the current skill's spawn (D2Common getters `0x10309230` monster,
   `0x10309260` x, `0x10309290` y, `0x103092c0` mode, which srvst 49, Nest's start, set from the monstats spawn
   columns), the room at x/y (`0x103a16c0`), the spot cleared (`0x1030bed0(room, x, y, 1, 0x100)`), and **one**
   spawn (`0x103130a0`, 1.13c's spawn monster, with 1, 0).
5. On a spawn: counter + 1, unit flags (1.13c `+0xc4`) `|= 0x4020000`, and the skill's `+0xe6` overlay when not
   negative. Returns 1.

D2R's Nest (srvdo 91, `0x57c590`) does steps 2 and 4 with the same calls (`0x48e820`, `RoomAtXY`, `0x3636d0`,
`SpawnMonster` `0x492cf0`), but spawns the start's count (`+0x34`), has no cap, sets the same two flags through
`0x34e8d0` (`+0x124 |= 0x4000000`) and `0x34f010` (`|= 0x20000`), puts the skill's `+0x13c` overlay on, and links the
spawn to the nest's minion list and callback. D2R's unit flags at `+0x124` are 1.13c's `+0xc4` bit for bit: 0x20000 no
treasure class, 0x4000000 no experience.

1.13c's srvst 67 is empty: PD2 wrote it. Vanilla's CorpseCycler and VineCycler used srvst 63 (1.13c `0xd170`, D2R
`0x587b50`): with a monster caster and a target corpse not in state 118, it sets 118 on the corpse, refreshes it
(Ordinal 10158, D2R `0x38ebf0`), creates srvmissilea (`recycler delay`) whose hit heals, and sends packet 0xa3 (D2R
`0x5396d0`, `SendChargePacket`).
PD2's `0x103b6520(game, unit, skill, level)`:

1. A monster, skill id in range and not 0.
2. The target (`0x1036d440`: the refreshed path target, not the caster), not in state 118, and not owned by a player
   (1.13c owner type `+0x94` / id `+0x98`: the `OwnedByPlayer` test).
3. State 118 on, the refresh, then aurarangecalc (`+0x64`), calc1-3.
4. calc3 must be 6 (life) or 8 (mana), else 0 (the corpse stays taken). heal = calc1 + rand(calc2 - calc1).
5. The area search `0x103a1450` at the caster, radius aurarangecalc, mask aurafilter (`+0x50`), callback `0x1036d5a0`:
   stat = min(stat + heal * 256, max) with max 7 (maxhp) or 9 (maxmana). No alignment test beyond the mask.
6. Packet 0xa3 (`0x103a1c40(corpse, unit, skill, 1, 0, 0, 0)`), as vanilla's 63. Returns 1.

PD2's rows: aurarangecalc 40, aurafilter 73731, calc3 6 (CorpseCycler, Cycle of Life's vine) and 8 (VineCycler,
Vines'). D2R's 67 is Frenzy's start, so ours takes 83 (71-90 free; PD2 uses 72-79).
**Port.** srvst 83 does PD2's steps with D2R's calls (UnitHasState, SetUnitState, `0x38ebf0`, AreaUnits, UnitStat,
SetUnitStat, the caster's seed, SendChargePacket). The corpse is D2R's skill target (`0x48fe20`, what D2R's 63 reads),

PD2's `0x103a7750(game, missile)`: with the missile's skill in range and its row: monstats `sHitPar1` (`+0x4c`), unless
-1, spawned at the missile's x/y in its room (`0x103a1420`) in mode `sHitPar2` (`+0x50`, 1 when 16 or more), then
`sHitPar3` (`+0x54`, unless negative) or-ed into its unit flags. Returns 1.
D2R's srvhit 6 (`0x45ce90`) spawns the same (`0x50a050(game, room, monster, x, y, mode, 0)`, which returns the monster),
but never reads `sHitPar3`. PD2's five rows set 0x4020000 (no treasure class, no experience; sharptooth's adds 0x1e), so
1.13c's clthit 11 is empty, and so is D2R's; D2R's dispatcher (`0x1b8e60`) skips an empty slot. Data.

1.13c's cdo 12 (D2Client `0xb2d00`): with CltParam1 and CltParam2 at least 1, and unless D2Common #10985 says no, a
screen shake of strength CltParam1 with (CltParam2 / 3) * 1000 twice; then the default missile do (cdo 1). D2R's 12
(`0x1b6b30`) is the same with a three-part shake, (CltParam2 / 3) * 1000, (CltParam2 - 2 * (CltParam2 / 3)) * 1000,
(CltParam2 / 3) * 1000, then cdo 1 (`0x1b5380`). PD2's row has CltParam2 1, so 1.13c passes 0, 0 and D2R a middle part
of 1000: the shake's length may differ (approximated row; the siege beast is a map monster, not seen in game).
